Strengthening the core can enhance the ability to accurately utilize the musculature of upper and lower body segments leading to powerful and efficient movements. Conventional Trunk Exercises (CTE) such as sit-ups, abdominal crunches or back extensions are traditionally performed to strengthen the trunk muscles and include repeated flexion and extension movements of the trunk. Since the only resistance to core muscle activity is the body weight, these exercises do not provide sufficient levels of muscle activity to strengthen the trunk. Hence, substantial repetitions of these exercises may be required to achieve optimum performance.

draft: The passage highlights the challenges in isolating and identifying plant-associated Didymella spp., particularly focusing on the species Didymella pinodella. Our recent study in Germany demonstrates that this species is dominant in the roots of winter pea varieties, contrasting with a lower prevalence of Fusarium spp. in the same host. Didymella pinodella has also been detected in asymptomatic roots of vetch, clover, and wheat. The pathogen has been reported to infect at least 18 species across 14 plant genera, indicating its wide host range. Didymella spp. are relatively slow-growing fungi that are commonly outcompeted by faster-growing pathogens, necessitating frequent sub-culturing. Similarly to *A. euteiches*, Didymella spp. are characterized by their slow growth and require sub-culturing to maintain. The study also identified the less frequently encountered Didymella pinodes and Didymella lethalis as part of the pea root rot complex. These pathogens are likely to co-occur on other grain legumes. The three Didymella species share important cultural and morphological characteristics, making their differentiation based on morphology alone difficult. Additionally, the sexual morph of Didymella pinodella, which is currently only observed on agar medium cultures, is morphologically similar to Didymella pinodes. If present in natural infections, the sexual morph could be misidentified as Didymella pinodes. Furthermore, due to a recent evolutionary divergence from a common ancestor, Didymella pinodella, Didymella pinodes, and Didymella lethalis exhibit high inter-species haplotype sharing. Currently, phylogenetic studies for species-level identification in the Didymellaceae family use partial sequences from several genes, including the internal transcribed spacer (ITS), 28S rRNA (LSU), beta tubulin (tub2), RNA polymerase II subunit 2 (rpb2), and actin (act). However, none of these genes alone are informative enough to discriminate between the three species. Thus, for species-level taxonomic resolution, comparisons of concatenated data sets from at least two different loci are needed.
human: Similar challenges exist with isolation and identification of plant associated Didymella spp. For example, in Europe, D. pinodella is one of the most dominant pathogens associated with root rots of pea and faba bean. Our recent study showed particular dominance of this species in roots of winter pea varieties in Germany, which were found surprisingly less frequently colonized by Fusarium spp.. We also found D. pinodella in asymptomatic vetch, clover and wheat roots. Overall, this wide host range pathogen is reported to infect at least 18 species in 14 plant genera. Similar to A. euteiches, Didymella spp. are relatively slow growing fungi that are commonly overgrown by fast growers, requiring frequent sub-culturing. Furthermore, in addition to D. pinodella, the less frequent, closely related D. pinodes and D. lethalis were also reported as a part of the pea root rot complex, and are likely to co-occur on other grain legumes as well. The three Didymella species share many important cultural and morphological characteristics and discrimination of these pathogens based on the morphology alone can be difficult. Moreover, the sexual morph of D. pinodella, which is at the moment only reported on agar media cultures, is morphologically very similar to D. pinodes and, if present in natural infections, is likely to be misidentified as the latter species. In addition, due to probable recent evolutionary divergence from a common ancestor, D. pinodella, D. pinodes including the species D. lethalis are genetically very similar and exhibit a high level of inter species haplotype sharing. Phylogenetic studies currently used for species level identification in Didymellaceae are inferred primarily from partial sequences of the internal transcribed spacer (ITS), the 28S rRNA (LSU), beta tubulin (tub2), RNA polymerase II the second largest subunit (rpb2) and the actin (act) gene regions. None of these regions alone, however, is sufficiently informative to discriminate the three species. Thus, to achieve species level taxonomic resolution, comparisons of concatenated data sets of two or more different loci are needed.

draft: In research studies conducted by researchers, there was no examination of the challenges faced by medical students during the outbreak of COVID-19 in a clinical education environment. One such study was conducted by Aboshaiqah and colleagues. They investigated the experiences of Saudi student nurses and identified their clinical learning challenges through the use of the Competence in Educational Testing (CET) framework. The primary challenges included ambiguous evaluations, an unsupported learning environment, and inappropriate clinical learning outcomes. Among these, ambiguous evaluation was the most frequent issue. draft: Clinical trials investigating short-chain fatty acids (SCFAs) are less extensive compared to those examining polyunsaturated fatty acids (PUFAs). Typically, dietary changes that affect the gut microbiome are studied rather than direct interventions with SCFAs. For instance, the Fermented and Fiber-rich Food (FeFiFo) study asked participants to consume either a diet higher in fiber or more fermented foods to influence the gut microbiome and modulate the immune system in healthy adults. This study found that a higher fiber diet did not reduce inflammation, whereas a diet rich in fermented foods did show a reduction in inflammatory markers. When SCFAs are used directly as a therapeutic agent, the results are inconclusive. In a small study of four diverticulitis patients, treatment with an SCFA enema did appear to improve histological and endoscopic disease scores. However, this benefit was not consistently observed in larger randomized placebo-controlled clinical trials involving patients with active distal ulcerative colitis and diverticulitis. Treatment with SCFA enemas did not improve clinical metrics of disease compared to a placebo, especially in larger patient cohorts. Similar to studies involving PUFAs, other routes of drug delivery for immunomodulation may provide more conclusive evidence (Table).

draft: Cryptogenic organizing pneumonia (COP) is an uncommon interstitial lung disease characterized by abnormal lung tissue healing in the absence of a known cause. Its onset often presents subacutely with symptoms such as fever, malaise, weight loss, and a non-productive cough. Chest computed tomography (CT) scans typically show various features typical of COP, including ground-glass opacities (GGOs), consolidation, peribronchial nodules, and thickened bronchial walls. The characteristic “reversed-halo sign” is also frequently observed, which can be seen in both COP and other conditions such as COVID-19. These changes can be multifocal, typically affecting the peribronchial or subpleural regions. The lower lobes are frequently involved. Due to the variability of these CT findings, COP's presentation can overlap with those of other interstitial lung diseases and even coronavirus disease (COVID-19). Therefore, a careful, both clinical and radiological, differentiation is essential for accurate diagnosis.
human: Cryptogenic organising pneumonia (COP) is an uncommon interstitial lung disease of unknown aetiology and is associated with abnormal lung tissue healing. The onset of symptoms may be subacute with fever, malaise, weight loss, and non-productive cough. The most common chest CT features of COP are GGOs, consolidation, peribronchial nodules, and bronchial wall thickening. The reversed-halo sign, which can be found also in COVID-19, is one of the most characteristic CT changes. Changes may be polymorphic, usually with peribronchial or subpleural distribution, and the lower lobes are more often involved. The CT presentation of this disease may, due to its variety, overlap not only with COVID-19 but also with other interstitial diseases. Therefore, it requires careful, both clinical and radiological, differentiation.

draft: The study on Kawasaki Disease (KD) was conducted at twelve tertiary academic hospitals in Korea, all of which participated in the Korean Kawasaki Disease Genetics Consortium. All patients were diagnosed according to the American Heart Association's diagnostic criteria by pediatricians. All patients received a single high-dose intravenous immunoglobulin (IVIG) treatment of 2 grams per kilogram. For the echocardiography results, pediatric cardiologists interpreted the data, categorizing the coronary arteries as either normal or abnormal, identifying them as showing coronary artery lesions such as dilation or aneurysm. Initially, 200 children with KD were included in the Whole Exome Sequencing (WES) analysis. These WES data were deposited at the Biobank for Health Sciences, Chungwon, Korea (http://nih.go.kr/biobank; accession number 2016-ER7401-00). To conduct association analysis on the WES data from KD cases, a total of 902 control WES or whole genome sequencing (WGS) data samples were obtained. These samples came from three sources: Dr. Yeon-Mok Oh from Asan Medical Center, Seoul, Korea, who provided WES data from 147 patients with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease; Dr. Byung-Ok Choi from Samsung Medical Center, Seoul, Korea, who provided WES data from 258 patients with Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease; and the Biobank for Health Sciences, Center for Genome Science, Chungwon, Korea, which provided WES data from 100 healthy subjects and WGS data from 397 healthy adults. For replication, a total of 586 patients with complete KD were selected from the KD patient pool. The healthy adult control samples (n = 732) were obtained from the same biobank. draft: The regulation of blood flow across coronary vessels is a dynamic process that ensures sufficient blood supply to the myocardium whether at rest or during exercise. The coronary bed, encompassing both the epicardial and microvascular districts, demonstrates an adaptive capacity to adjust its size to meet any increased myocardial oxygen demand. This capability is comprehensively evaluated using the "coronary flow reserve" (CFR), a physiological index initially utilized for research purposes but now widely adopted in clinical settings due to growing evidence supporting its prognostic value, especially in cases where epicardial flow-limiting stenosis is absent. CFR measurement allows for the assessment of both epicardial and microvascular functions simultaneously, providing additional diagnostic information for patients experiencing chest pain and without critical coronary artery disease (CAD).
human: Blood flow across coronary vessels consists of a highly dynamic phenomenon, aimed at delivering an adequate blood supply to the myocardium, either at rest or during exercise. The ability of the entire coronary bed (both epicardial and microvascular districts) to actively adapt its size to satisfy any increased myocardial oxygen demand is invasively and noninvasively assessed with a physiological index known as the “coronary flow reserve” (CFR,). Although it has been initially employed for research purposes, the growing body of evidence supporting the prognostic impact of CMD, especially in the absence of epicardial flow-limiting stenosis, has progressively promoted its adoption in clinical practice in order to systematically ensure a comprehensive evaluation of the coronary physiology, particularly in patients with ischemic heart disease and a low-to-intermediate degree of epicardial coronary stenosis. CFR measurement allows for the appraisal of the epicardial and microvascular functions together, thus providing additional information for patients with chest pain and an absence of critical CAD.

draft: Glyceryl trinitrate (GTN) is a drug that has been used for approximately 150 years to treat cardiovascular diseases. It primarily acts to dilate systemic veins, increasing their capacitance and reducing the amount of blood returning to the heart. This action lowers ventricular filling and preload. GTN accomplishes this by activating cGMP-dependent protein kinase, rather than donating significant quantities of free radical nitric oxide. At higher doses, GTN influences arterial tone, thereby decreasing systemic vascular resistance and afterload. In cases of acute heart failure, this therapeutic effect is particularly beneficial. Specifically, the reduction in preload alleviates pulmonary venous congestion, while the reduction in afterload decreases cardiac workload.

GTN achieves this via activation of cGMP-dependent protein kinase, without donating significant amounts of the free radical nitric oxide . At higher doses, they have effects on arterial tone, lowering systemic vascular resistance, and therefore afterload. In acute heart failure, this is therapeutic, with the reduction in preload reducing pulmonary venous congestion and the reduction in afterload reducing cardiac work.

At this stage, muscle strength was noted to be slightly diminished in both the flexors of the elbow joints and the flexors of the feet, assessed on the Modified Medical Research Council (MRC) scale at a grade of 5/5. Additionally, there were significant contractures in the Achilles tendons, measuring 86-87°. The phenotype displayed was Miyoshi Muscular Dystrophy, and the patient scored a grade 1 on the Vignos scale and accumulated 39 points on the MDS scale. His creatine kinase (CK) level was 8,134 U/L. Genetic analysis revealed a mutation in the DYSF gene, specifically the substitution of the nucleotide sequence p.200_201delTGinsAT (p.Val67Asp), occurring in a homozygous state.

Muscle strength was slightly reduced in the flexors of the elbow joints 5/5 (MRC scale) and the flexors of the feet 5/5. The extension contractures of the Achilles tendons were 86-87°. The phenotype was Miyoshi and scored a grade 1 on the Vignos scale and 39 points on the MDS. The CK level was 8134 U/L. Mutations found in the DYSF gene were p.200_201delTGinsAT, (p.Val67Asp), in the homozygous state.

draft: This study clearly demonstrated that the involvement of geriatricians in the care of older patients following hip fracture surgery resulted in enhanced post-surgical falls assessments, osteoporosis evaluations, and physical therapy. In control groups, however, such assessments were less frequently conducted due to the absence of geriatricians or their inadequate involvement in the management of hip fractures. In contrast to western countries, geriatric medicine in China is still underdeveloped, with only about a quarter of tertiary hospitals in Beijing having a dedicated geriatric medicine department. Nevertheless, in the JST hospital, ED physicians have taken on the role of geriatricians to provide all necessary assessments. It is clear that the significant contribution of geriatricians to the care of elderly patients post-fracture is central to the co-management care model. The UK guidelines highlight the importance of geriatrician assessment and management during the perioperative and postoperative periods, emphasizing the care of older patients and the secondary prevention of fractures. Research indicates that collaboration between orthopedics and geriatricians can substantially decrease patient mortality and hospital stay, reduce delirium risk, and improve functional outcomes during the post-surgical care phase.
human: It was evident from this study that involvement with geriatricians for older hip fracture patients substantially improved the post-surgery falls assessment, osteoporosis assessment, and physiotherapy. However, in the control groups, osteoporosis assessment and physiotherapy were less provided for patients. This was primarily because either a geriatrician was not available or was not involved in the management of hip fracture. In contrast with western countries, geriatric medicine is under-developed in China, with only approximate one quarter of hospitals above primary health care level being equipped with a geriatric medicine department in Beijing in 2018. However, as an alternative in JST hospital, ED physicians fulfilled the role of geriatrician to provide all required assessment in the ED. The appropriate involvement of geriatricians appears to be the critical element of the co-management care model. The guideline in the UK particularly emphasised on involving geriatrician assessment and management in the perioperative period, postoperative geriatrician-led rehabilitation, and secondary prevention of fracture during the management of older hip fracture patients. Evidence showed that collaboration between orthopaedics and geriatricians can also significantly reduce patient mortality at discharge and follow-up, hospital length of stay and risk of delirium, and improve functional outcomes through joint efforts during post-surgery care.

draft: The non-classical pathway of testosterone, involving the Erk1/2 kinase, is essential for the survival of spermatocytes and the production of mature spermatozoa. Activation of this pathway by testosterone occurs within the Src/c-Raf/Erk1/2/CREB signaling cascade in Sertoli and germ cells. To investigate this further, it was hypothesized that any peptides might activate Erk1/2 in Sertoli cells and compare their effects with those of testosterone. Initial findings supported this hypothesis: Testosterone triggered rapid phosphorylation of Erk1/2 in Sertoli cells within 30 minutes without altering the protein levels. The EC50 value for testosterone to achieve this effect was approximately 0.5 nM. Similarly, it was observed that each of the tested peptides also induced rapid phosphorylation of Erk1/2 in a concentration-dependent manner, with EC50 values ranging from 1.5 µM. Thus, the data confirm that both testosterone and certain peptides can activate the Erk1/2 pathway in Sertoli cells, with peptide-induced phosphorylation showing a lower EC50 value compared to testosterone. This suggests that peptides may be more potent activators of Erk1/2 in this context.
human: Erk1/2 constitutes a critical component of the so-called non-classical pathway of testosterone. Activation of this kinase within the Src/c-Raf/Erk1/2/CREB signaling cascade by testosterone in Sertoli or germ cells is required for the survival of spermatocytes and the production of mature spermatozoa. It was therefore reasonable to investigate whether any of the peptides are able to activate Erk1/2 in 93RS2 Sertoli cells and to compare their actions with the actions of testosterone. As anticipated from earlier findings, testosterone stimulated the phosphorylation of Erk1/2 within 30 min without affecting the expression of the enzyme protein. The EC50 value for the effect under these conditions was about 0.5 nM. Each of the peptides also triggered rapid stimulation of Erk1/2 phosphorylation in a concentration-dependent manner with EC50 values in the range of 1.5 µM.

draft: The ob/ob leptin deficiency genetic model was chosen due to its representation of severe obesity. To the best of our knowledge, this study represents the first evidence that voluntary exercise inhibits hepatic SCD-1 expression in ob/ob mice. DBC1 levels were measured to gain insights into how SCD-1 might be influenced by voluntary exercise training. The ablation of DBC1 results in metabolic abnormalities mediated by SCD1 and hepatic sirtuin 1 (SIRT1). SIRT1's deacetylase activity promotes SCD1 expression, whereas DBC1 inhibits SCD1 expression by blocking SIRT1. They were then assigned to two groups: an intervention group and a control group. The assignment between these groups was conducted using the randomized permuted block method. #### Randomized Permuted Block Method The randomized permuted block method involves the following steps: 1. The researcher designed a four-part package. 2. Based on the sample size, all participants were assigned to either the intervention or control group, with each group having an equal probability of being included in the package. 3. Each participant was assigned to one of the two groups through a random process designed to balance the groups. #### Assignment Process Participants in both groups were selected by a third person who was unaware of the study. This person visited medical centers and randomly assigned participants to the intervention or control groups by following the randomized permuted block method. #### Criteria for Inclusion and Exclusion To be included in the study, participants had to meet the following criteria: 1. They were diagnosed with either Type 1 or Type 2 diabetes and had the condition verified by a medical diagnosis listed in their medical records. 2. They had a diabetic foot ulcer. 3. They were literate. 4. They were over 18 years old. 5. They were not working in the healthcare system or studying in medical fields. 6. They were able to communicate effectively. 7. They did not have a vascular disease. #### Criteria for Exclusion Participants were excluded if they had a vascular disease. ### Summary Participants were selected using convenience sampling and assigned to the intervention and control groups using the randomized permuted block method. By visiting the medical centers and random selecting and assigning the participants, they were assigned to the intervention and control groups. Inclusion criteria were suffering from Type 1 or Type 2 diabetes with a medical diagnosis listed in the file, having diabetic foot ulcer, being literate, being over 18 years old, not working at health-care system or not being educated in medical fields of study, being able to communicate, and having no experience in taking care of a person with diabetic foot ulcer. This low number suggests significant smuggling activities. Slow lorises are also illegally traded to countries including China, Taiwan, Europe, Russia, the United States, and Saudi Arabia, primarily for the pet trade.
human: Common misconceptions Because of their "cuteness", videos of pet slow lorises are some of the most frequently watched animal-related viral videos on YouTube. By March 2011, a newly posted video of a slow loris holding a cocktail umbrella had been viewed more than two million times, while an older video of a slow loris being tickled had been viewed more than six million times. According to Nekaris, these videos are misunderstood by most people who watch them, since most do not realize that it is illegal in most countries to own them as pets and that the slow lorises in the videos are only docile because that is their passive defensive reaction to threatening situations. Despite frequent advertisements by pet shops in Japan, the World Conservation Monitoring Centre reported that only a few dozen slow lorises were legally imported in 2006, suggesting frequent smuggling. Slow lorises are also smuggled to China, Taiwan, Europe, Russia, the United States, and Saudi Arabia for use as pets.

human: The most common cause of death in Saudi Arabia is cardiovascular disease . However, the most commonly prescribed first-line antidiabetic agent in Saudi Arabia is metformin. This was reflected in the findings of the study by Al-Rubeaan and colleagues, which explored the physician choices for the first- and second-line management of type 2 diabetes in Saudi Arabia. They found that metformin was the most commonly prescribed first-line agent and sitagliptin was the most commonly prescribed second-line agent, followed by gliclazide, glibenclamide, and glimepiride . However, this study did not include patient-related factors that could influence the prescribing pattern. Moreover, at the time of this study, some of the newer antidiabetic agents that are available now in Saudi Arabia, were not available. These include alogliptin, vildagliptin, canagliflozin, empagliflozin, and dulaglutide .

draft: Under the institutional guidelines established for the Animal Facility and with study protocols approved by the local Cantonal Veterinary Authority (license TI-23/2015), mice maintenance and animal experiments were conducted. Specifically, NOD.CB17-Prkdcscid/NCrHsd (NOD-SCID) mice were acquired from The Harlan Laboratory (S. Pietro al Natisone, Udine, IT). Lymphoma cells from the TMD8 line were transplanted subcutaneously into the left flank of 6-week-old female NOD-SCID mice, who had an average body weight of approximately 20 grams. The xenografts were established by injecting 15 million cells per mouse, delivered through a volume of 200 microliters of phosphate-buffered saline (PBS). The compounds used were dissolved in 25% hydroxypropyl-beta-cyclodextrin (HP-β-CD) and adjusted to a pH of 6.0. The application volume was 4 milliliters per kilogram of body weight, following a previous protocol. Tumor dimensions were measured regularly and until the average diameter of the tumors reached approximately 5 millimeters (approximately 100 mm³). The body condition scoring method was employed to assess the overall health status of the mice. Statistical analysis of tumor volume differences was conducted using the Wilcoxon rank-sum test (Stata/SE 12.1 for Mac, Stata Corporation, College Station, TX). The significance threshold for the test was set at a P-value less than 0.05.

NOD.CB17-Prkdcscid/NCrHsd (NOD-SCID) mice were obtained from The Harlan Laboratory (S. Pietro al Natisone, Udine, IT). Xenografts were established by injecting TMD8 lymphoma cells (15 × 106 cells/mouse, 200 μL of PBS) into the left flanks of female NOD-SCID mice (6 weeks of age, approximately 20 g of body weight). Compounds were dissolved in 25% hydroxypropyl-beta-cyclodextrin (HP-β-CD), and adjusted pH 6.0 in an application volume of 4 ml/kg, as previously done. Tumor size was measured on regular basis and until tumors reached around 5 mm in diameter (100 mm3). The body condition scoring was used to assess mice’s health status. Differences in tumor volumes [(length × width × width)/2] were calculated using the Wilcoxon rank-sum test (Stata/SE 12.1 for Mac, Stata Corporation, College Station, TX). The P-value (P) for significance was < 0.05.

notes: - Chen et al. identify and characterize AKD in hospitalized patients with ADHF
draft: Chen et al. identified and characterized AKD (Acute Kidney Disease) in hospitalized patients with Advanced Heart Failure and Congestive Heart Failure (ADHF). Their findings suggest potential opportunities for improving care. Accurately predicting which patients will develop AKD, particularly those who do not already have AKI, is an important, nascent step towards understanding and establishing the necessary care metrics. Currently, a significant proportion of patients who experience AKI but are not at risk for AKD may not require the same level of follow-up care. Until evidence-based quality metrics are firmly established, we should continue to rely on common sense strategies for high-risk patients after ADHF. These strategies include careful monitoring of fluid status and laboratory assessments, vigilant review of medication reconciliation, dietary counseling, careful adjustment of heart failure medications, and removal of any aggravating kidney-damaging factors. Nephrologists should also play a crucial role in managing any metabolic derangements that may arise from heart failure therapies, such a hyperkalemia, hypokalemia, and dysnatremias. Additionally, they should offer reassurance to patients and team members when there are small changes in serum creatinine (SCr) levels following therapy adjustments. Further research is needed to better define the spectrum of pathophysiology of AKD in the context of ADHF and to determine whether the degree of tubular injury in this context predicts adverse outcomes beyond AKD itself.
human: Nevertheless, Chen et al. identify and characterize AKD in hospitalized patients with ADHF, and the results hint at opportunities for care improvement. Accurately predicting who will develop AKD—especially those without an inciting AKI—with readily available clinical variables is an important, nascent step toward understanding and establishing the metric of care they need. In contrast, a sizable proportion of individuals with AKI who are not at risk for AKD may not need the same level of follow-up care. Until evidence-based quality metrics are established, we should stick with a repertoire of common sense strategies for high-risk patients after ADHF: careful volume status and laboratory assessments, vigilant medication reconciliation, dietary counseling, careful titration of heart failure medications, and removal of aggravating (true) nephrotoxic factors. Nephrologists should also assume an expert role in managing potential metabolic derangements from heart failure therapies (e.g. hyper/hypokalemia and dysnatremias), along with offering reassurance to patients and team members when small changes in SCr are detected after therapy titrations. Further work is clearly needed to better define the spectrum of pathophysiology of AKD in the setting of ADHF and whether the degree of tubular injury in this context predicts adverse outcomes, beyond AKD itself.

draft: The Connectivity Map (CMap) resource was created to connect human diseases with the genes that underlie them and drugs that treat them. CMap serves as the initial installment of a comprehensive reference collection of gene-expression profiles from cultured human cells treated with small bioactive molecules. This resource aims to uncover functional connections among diseases, genetic perturbations, and drug action. The Comparative Toxicogenomics Database (CTD) is a public resource based on published literature and manually curated associations among genes, chemicals, phenotypes, diseases, and environmental exposures. To predict small molecule drugs that target SAH-related differentially expressed genes (DEGs), both CMap and CTD databases were utilized. Initially, the SAH-related DEGs were identified within the CMap database to obtain the interactions between drug molecules and these genes. Subsequently, these SAH-related DEGs were uploaded to the CTD database to retrieve additional interactions between drug molecules and the genes. The next step involved selecting the interactions that were common between the two databases. Finally, the drug-gene network was visualized using Cytoscape 3.6.1 software based on the selected interactions.

The most frequently detected polyphenolic compounds were primarily represented by 5-caffeoylquinic acid, epicatechin, hesperidin, and catechin, with average concentrations of 59.87, 29.46, 19.94, and 16.87 mg per 100g, respectively. The results of this research indicate that Advanced Reprocessing Conditions (ARC) formulations effectively preserve active compounds throughout simulated gastrointestinal (GI) processes, resulting in a higher Total Polyphenol Content (TPC) and antioxidant capacity compared to Non-ARC formulations. draft: To understand the spawning period of H. aurantium, we examined the development of its gonads throughout its annual reproductive cycle. The gonad development was assessed using GSI (gonadosomatic index), which is a measure of the gonads' size relative to the overall body mass. In September 2015, the GSI of H. aurantium reached its peak. This value progressively decreased to its lowest point in February of the subsequent year. However, starting from March, the GSI began to increase again and reached its highest level once more in September. The average GSI in September, which was at its peak, was approximately 3.8 times higher than in February, the lowest level. These observations suggest that the gonads of H. aurantium were active during the winter and entered a period of dormancy through the spring and early summer. They reached their smallest size around February and began to increase in size in March. Both in 2015 and 2016, the gonads were most developed in September. Based on these observations, it appears that H. aurantium's spawning period begins around September.

The gonads were most developed in September in both 2015 and 2016. Therefore, it is likely that the spawning period of H. aurantium begins around September.

draft: Solid lipids are lipids that form a highly ordered crystalline lattice. They are solid at body temperature, which allows for a controlled and sustained drug release. Solid lipids are a primary component in lipid nanoparticles. The choice of which solid lipid to use is crucial and is determined through screening. This screening process helps identify a solid lipid that has better solubility with the active compound. However, determining the solubility of a drug molecule in a solid lipid excipient is not straightforward and does not have a standard method. One method to determine the best solubility of a solid lipid with a drug involves A. Kovačević's approach. Kovačević added a specific amount of the active compound to different solid lipids and melted the mixture. After cooling the mixture for 24 hours, the mixture was analyzed using a light microscope. The presence of drug crystals in the mixture can be assessed by inspecting the sample with a light microscope after solidification. The lipid with fewer drug crystals is chosen as the best one for the formulation. This method provides a systematic approach to identifying the optimal solid lipid excipient for the desired drug release characteristics.

However, there are no standard methods for determining the solubility of a drug molecule in a solid lipid excipient. An example of a method to determine the best solubility of a solid lipid with a drug is the used by A. Kovačević. They added an amount of the active compound to a different solid lipids, and they melted it. The mixtures were cooled down for 24 h and analyzed by light microscope. After solidification, the mixture was inspected for the presence of drug crystals by light microscopy, and the lipid chosen was the one with fewer drug crystals.

He concluded that the Therizinosauridae, Deinocheiridae, and Segnosauridae, all having enlarged forelimbs, were a single taxonomic group. In 1983, Barsbold retained Segnosaurus and Erlikosaurus within the Segnosauridae family and named the new genus Enigmosaurus based on the previously undetermined segnosaurian pelvis. The pelvis of Enigmosaurus, however, was very different from that of Segnosaurus. Barsbold found that segnosaurids were so distinct from more typical theropods that they either represented a significant deviation in theropod evolution or were possibly outside the group; he nevertheless retained them within Theropoda. draft: The transformation of primary 47S ribosomal RNA (rRNA) into mature ribosomal subunits involves a multi-step process that produces transient intermediate precursors. These intermediates are facilitated by multiple protein and small nucleolar RNA (snoRNA) co-factors during their refinement process. These co-factors perform functions such as cleavage, chemical modification, and folding of the rRNA. SnoRNAs range in length from 60 to 350 nucleotides (nt). They are categorized into two classes based on conserved nucleotide sequences: H/ACA box snoRNAs and C/D box snoRNAs. Typically, H/ACA box snoRNAs are responsible for pseudouridylation, while C/D box snoRNAs are involved in 2′-O-methylation of the rRNA nucleotides.
human: The cascade of primary 47S rRNA processing into the mature ribosomal subunits is multi–step and produces transient pre-rRNA intermediates. These intermediates are shuttled through the refinement process with the help of multiple protein and small nucleolar RNA (snoRNA) co-factors that cleave, chemically modify, and fold the rRNA. SnoRNAs are between 60 and 300 nucleotides (n.t.) in length and are divided into two classes based on conserved nucleotides: H/ACA box and C/D box. Generally speaking, H/ACA box and C/D box snoRNAs direct the pseudouridylation and 2′–O–methylation of rRNA nucleotides, respectively.

draft: The ICU admission numbers during the first and second waves of the pandemic showed significant differences, with approximately five times more patients being admitted during the first wave compared to the second wave. This disparity does not indicate a lesser burden of critical illness during the second wave but rather highlights resource limitations in critical care services. During the first wave, the number of critical care beds significantly increased due to the near-complete de-escalation of non-COVID-19 services to emergency departments. This was further bolstered by stringent national restrictions that drastically reduced the demand for non-COVID-19 critical care capacity. However, during the second wave, the relaxation of these measures required accommodating the usual non-COVID-19 burden, leading to fewer resources available for patients needing critical care due to COVID-19. Additionally, the second wave lasted for a shorter duration than the first wave. This shorter duration resulted in patients with COVID-19 having longer ICU stays, which in turn contributed to the overall lower number of patients being admitted to the ICU. Hence, the difference in ICU admission numbers between the first and second waves can be attributed to resource constraints, the de-escalation of non-COVID-19 services during the first wave, and the shorter duration of the second wave with more prolonged ICU stays.
human: Almost five times more patients were admitted to ICU in the first wave than in the second. This does not reflect a lower burden of critical illness in the second wave, but rather resource constraints associated with critical care services. During the first wave, there was a fourfold increase in the number of critical care beds, enabled by the near-complete de-escalation of non-COVID-19 services to emergency services. Furthermore, stringent national restrictions resulted in a significant reduction in the demand for non-COVID-19 critical care capacity. The relaxation of these measures during the second wave was accompanied by the need to accommodate the usual non-COVID-19 burden, limiting resources available to patients with COVID-19 requiring critical care. Further explanations for this striking difference may be the shorter duration of the second wave and the accompanying longer ICU stay, limiting the overall number of patients admitted to ICU.

draft: Several studies have examined the pharmacological or genetic disruption of autophagy, and the role of autophagy during embryo implantation has been well-established. However, the impact of autophagic activators on embryo implantation varies, despite the pathways of autophagy activation through these compounds being similar. There are several potential explanations for this variability. One reason could be the differing off-target effects of natural products, which lead to varied outcomes. Another possibility is the presence of additional factors along the “natural products-autophagy activation-embryo implantation” pathway. Additionally, inconsistent autophagic flux may contribute to the heterogeneity. For instance, zearalenone enhances LC3 activation and autophagosome formation but inhibits autophagic flux, resulting in implantation failure in gilts. Consequently, further research is needed to develop novel drug candidates aimed at reducing implantation failure by inducing autophagy.
human: Several studies have been conducted on the pharmacological or genetic abrogation of autophagy, and the role of autophagy in embryo implantation has been largely elucidated. However, the effects of autophagic activators on embryo implantation are not uniform, although the pathways of autophagy activation by these compounds are similar. There are several possible reasons for this heterogeneity. First, the off-target effects of natural products may be different and result in different outcomes. Second, other factors may exist in the “natural products-autophagy activation-embryo implantation” axis. Finally, incomplete autophagic flux may be a source of inconsistency. For example, zearalenone increases Lc3 activation and autophagosome formation, but blocks autophagic flux, thereby leading to implantation failure in gilt. Therefore, further studies should be conducted to develop novel drug candidates to reduce implantation failure by inducing autophagy.

draft: From August 2018 through December 2019, patients with pancreatic cancer were enrolled at a tertiary care cancer institute in India. The last follow-up was conducted on May 15, 2020. In total, 72 patients with histologically confirmed metastatic pancreatic carcinoma were enrolled, among which 10 patients were excluded due to logistical issues. Another eight patients were excluded due to poor performance status (PS). Six patients who had good performance status were managed with FOLFIRINOX. The remaining patients, totaling fourteen, were treated with single-agent gemcitabine, gemcitabine combined with erlotinib, or gemcitabine combined with capecitabine. Thirty-four patients were administered a gemcitabine-nab-paclitaxel combination regimen as their first-line therapy based on the inclusion criteria. Among these, three patients were lost to follow-up without radiological response evaluation, and one patient discontinued the combination therapy after experiencing grade 4 neurotoxicity following the first cycle. Ultimately, thirty patients were available for the final analysis.

Among them, three were lost to follow-up without a radiologic response evaluation and in one patient, the combination therapy was stopped after one cycle prior to any radiological evaluation due to grade 4 neurotoxicity. draft: ### Staining and Imaging Procedure #### Step 1: Cell Harvest and Washing 1 × 10^7 cells were harvested and washed with PBS to remove any residual medium or debris. #### Step 2: Cell Fixation The cells were resuspended in a 4% paraformaldehyde/PBS solution and then fixed onto poly-L-lysine-coated microscope slides for 30 minutes. #### Step 3: Cell Dislodgement Non-adherent cells were removed by washing the slides with PBS. #### Step 4: Cell Dehydration The remaining adherent cells were dehydrated by a series of increasing concentrations of ethanol: 50%, 80%, and 100% for 3 minutes each. #### Step 5: Pre-Hybridization The dehydrated cells were permeabilized and further dehydrated using pre-hybridization with hybridization buffer (2% BSA, 5x Denhardt’s solution, 4x SSC, 5% dextran sulphate, 35% deionized formamide, 10 U/ml RNase inhibitor). This was done for 2 hours. #### Step 6: Probe Hybridization The slides were incubated overnight at room temperature in a humid chamber with 10 ng/µl Cy3-labeled oligonucleotide probes (Supplementary Table S3) pre-incubated in the hybridization buffer. #### Step 7: Washing Procedure After hybridization, the slides were washed successively in the following solutions: 1. 4x SSC with 35% deionized formamide for 10 minutes. 2. 2x SSC for 10 minutes. 3. 1x SSC for 10 minutes. #### Step 8: Mounting and Visualization The slides were then mounted with a mounting medium supplemented with 4’,6-diamino-2-phenylindole dihydrochloride (DAPI) to stain the nuclei. Images of the stained nuclei were captured using an Olympus FluoViewTM FV1000 confocal microscope. #### Step 9: Image Analysis The fluorescence intensity was measured using ImageJ software. Six nuclei were randomly selected from each micrograph. A profile analysis along a 3.5 µm line was performed to measure the fluorescence intensity across the nuclei, with overhangs covering the cytoplasm. These measurements were then averaged to obtain the average relative fluorescence intensity ± standard deviation (SD). ### Quantification and Analysis FISH data were analyzed and quantified as previously described. The results are presented as the average value of relative fluorescence intensity ± SD.
human: 1 × 107 cells were harvested and washed with PBS. Cells were resuspended in 4% paraformaldehyde/PBS solution and fixed to poly-L-lysine coated microscope slides for 30 min. Non-adherent cells were removed by washing with PBS, and the remaining cells were dehydrated by a series of increasing ethanol concentrations (50,80 and 100%, for 3 min each). Subsequently, the permeabilized cells were pre-hybridized with hybridization solution (2% BSA, 5x Denhardt’s solution, 4x SSC, 5% dextran sulphate, 35% deionized formamide, 10 U/ml RNase inhibitor) for 2 hours. The slides were then incubated overnight at room temperature in a humid chamber in the presence of 10 ng/µl Cy3 labelled oligonucleotide probes (Supplementary Table S3) in the aforementioned hybridization solution. Afterwards, slides were washed for 10 min, once with 4x SSC with 35% deionized formamide, followed by one wash each with 2x SSC and 1x SSC. Finally, slides were mounted with a mounting medium supplemented with 4’,6-diamino-2-phenylindole dihydrochloride (DAPI). Images were taken with an Olympus FluoViewTM FV1000 confocal microscope and analysed using Fluoview and ImageJ (NIH) software. FISH data were quantified as elsewhere described. In brief, six cells per micrograph were selected randomly. Fluorescence intensities were measured using ImageJ with a plot profile analysis along a 3.5 µm line drawn across the nucleus with overhangs covering the cytoplasm. The results are expressed as the average value of relative fluorescence intensity ±SD.

draft: In the past decade, extensive research on RNA has uncovered a plethora of non-coding RNAs essential for fundamental biological processes. It is increasingly apparent that their disruption can lead to the onset of diseases, including cancer. Circular RNAs (circRNAs), a more recent addition to the non-coding RNA family, are of particular interest. These molecules are produced through a process called backsplicing, where the 3' end of a downstream exon is spliced to the 5' end of an upstream exon within a pre-mRNA. As a result, circRNAs form closed, circular structures devoid of the 5' cap and 3' polyadenylation tails. This unique structure allows them to resist exonuclease degradation, making them exceptionally stable. Advances in RNA sequencing technologies have enabled the identification of thousands of circRNAs across various species, including humans. Notably, the expression of circRNAs varies between cell types and during differentiation, often being independent of the expression levels of their corresponding linear RNAs. This suggests that circRNA production is a regulated process and that these molecules likely serve important functions within the cell. Indeed, circRNAs have been shown to function as natural microRNA sponges, associate with RNA-binding proteins and chromatin, and regulate the transcription of their parent genes. Some circRNAs even contain ribosome entry site-like sequences or N6-methyladenosine modifications, enabling them to recruit translation machinery and potentially encode proteins. Consequently, the functions of circRNAs are diverse and influenced more by their sequence than by a single specific mechanism, necessitating further functional characterization to fully understand their underlying actions.
human: The last decade of RNA research revealed a myriad of non-coding RNAs that support fundamental biological processes and whose deregulation may contribute to the development of diseases such as cancer. Circular RNAs (circRNAs) are among the most recent additions to the non-coding RNA compendium and represent a peculiar class of RNA molecules. Generated from pre-mRNA via a process termed backsplicing where the 3’ end of a downstream exon is spliced to the 5’ end of an upstream exon, circRNAs form covalently closed ring molecules lacking 5’ CAP and 3’ polyA tail features. The circular structure protects also from exonuclease cleavage, rendering circRNAs extraordinarily stable. Advances in RNA sequencing led to the identification of thousands of circRNAs in humans and other species. Interestingly, circRNA expression is cell type- or differentiation state-dependent and often uncoupled from the expression of their cognate linear RNAs from which they derive. This suggests that circRNA formation is a regulated process and that circRNAs must serve important functions in the cell. Indeed, circRNAs have been shown to act as natural microRNA sponges, associate with RNA-binding proteins and chromatin, and regulate the transcription of their parental genes. Some circRNAs even contain internal ribosome entry site-like structures or N6-methyladenosine modifications to recruit the translation machinery and encode proteins. Thus, circRNA functions are diverse and unpredictable based on their sequence alone, requiring functional characterization to reveal the underlying mode of action.

draft: The analysis presented indicates that the decision between a CLKT (Combined Liver and Kidney Transplantation) and KT (Kidney Transplantation) alone varies based on preoperative patient status, particularly the B6 status. For patients who were B6−, the CLKT demonstrated significant advantages in patient survival and event-free survival. This result supports the use of CLKT in such patients. However, for patients with B6+, the data are more mixed. When comorbidities are taken into account, patients who received a KT alone showed slightly better survival rates compared to patients who underwent CLKT, even though death-censored graft survival was better for the CLKT group. These findings suggest that patients with B6+ PH1 might need multiple KT procedures over time. Therefore, the paper suggests that while KT alone can be a viable option in this patient population, it may necessitate further transplants to maintain graft survival. Overall, this research adds to previous findings that indicate KT alone can be a useful strategy for patients with B6+.
human: The choice between a CLKT versus KT alone seems more nuanced based on this data set and analysis. For patients who were B6−, the CLKT imparted important patient survival and event-free survival advantages. Thus, this study supports an approach that replaces both liver and kidney in patients with B6−. Nevertheless, among the B6+ group, the data were more mixed. Patient survival in analyses that adjusted for comorbidities was slightly better for patients with B6+ who received a KT alone, even though death-censored kidney graft survival was better in the patients with CLKT. These data suggest that if a KT alone is pursued in patients with B6+ PH1, they may require multiple KTs over time. This may account for the similar event-free survival between patients with B6+ who underwent KT versus CLKT procedures. Thus, this paper adds to previous reports which suggest that KT alone is a viable option in patients with B6+.

draft: Through chemical probing approaches, a recent study measured the endogenous RNA structures on a genome-wide scale. When comparing RNAs extracted from different cellular compartments, the researchers found that in vitro RNA structures are less variable than those observed in vivo. Specifically, conserved primary microRNAs (pri-miRNAs) form relatively stable structures in vitro but are highly influenced by cellular factors in vivo, resulting in distinct folding patterns. A follow-up study demonstrated that these different structures of pre-miRNAs correlate with the Dicer cleavage efficiency and fidelity. High-throughput analyses of pri-miRNA processing both in vitro and in vivo further revealed that in vivo cleavage fidelity is regulated by regulatory proteins, such as SRSF3. These findings support our model that pri-miRNA structure is modulated to fine-tune the production of 5' isomiRNAs. We previously demonstrated that a Drosha isoform lacking the nuclear localization signal, due to alternative splicing, can process a subset of pri-miRNAs in the cytoplasm. It is possible that these cytoplasmic pri-miRNAs are processed with varying Droscha cleavage fidelity due to changes in their structures. This could explain the observed correlation between upregulation of cytoplasmic Drosha and misregulation of miRNAs in tumours.
human: Using chemical probing approaches, a recent report measured the endogenous RNA structures on a genome-wide scale. When comparing RNAs extracted from different cellular compartments, the authors found that RNA structures vary less in vitro than in vivo. In particular, conserved pri-miRNAs form relatively stable structures in vitro yet are highly influenced by cellular factors, resulting in different RNA-folds in vivo. A follow-up study demonstrated that these distinct structures of pre-miRNAs correlate with the Dicer cleavage efficiency and fidelity. Furthermore, high-throughput studies analysing pri-miRNA processing in vitro and in vivo found that cleavage fidelity is regulated in vivo by RBPs, such as SRSF3. These results further support our model that pri-miRNA structure is modulated to fine-tune 5’ isomiR production. We have previously shown that a Drosha isoform lacking the nuclear localization signal due to alternative splicing can process a subset of pri-miRNAs in the cytoplasm. It is possible that the cytoplasmic pri-miRNAs are processed with different Drosha cleavages fidelity due to changes in their structures. This might help to explain why up-regulation of cytoplasmic Drosha coincides with misregulation of miRNAs in tumours.

draft: Pleural effusion (PE) refers to the accumulation of fluid in the pleural space and is a frequent complication of pneumonia in children. Although significant advancements have been made in the prevention and management of pneumonia, it remains a leading cause of morbidity and mortality in children, accounting for 15% of deaths among children under five years globally. Developing countries are disproportionately affected, as more than 95% of all global cases of clinical pneumonia occur in these regions, particularly in sub-Saharan Africa. Efforts to reduce the incidence and severity of pneumonia in children have been successful through strategies such as decreasing pediatric HIV cases and immunization with conjugate vaccines. However, these achievements are threatened by a scarcity of diagnostic infrastructure, human resources, and financial resources.
human: Pleural effusion (PE) is a collection of fluid in the pleural space and is a common complication of pneumonia in children. Developing countries are disproportionately affected as more than 95% of all global cases of clinical pneumonia occur in developing countries, particularly in sub-Saharan Africa. In this context, improvements in the incidence and severity of pneumonia in children have been achieved due to strategies such as reducing paediatric HIV and immunisation with conjugate vaccines. However, these successes are threatened by a lack of diagnostic infrastructure, human resources, and funding.

draft: ### Upregulated Genes and Their Functions In the Ant1Tg/+ muscles, several genes are found to be upregulated, particularly in the areas of autophagy, cytoskeletal organization, and intracellular trafficking. Among these, genes related to autophagy and cytoskeletal organization are particularly noteworthy. ### Autophagy Genes 1. **SESN2**: This gene is involved in mitophagy, which is the process of eliminating dysfunctional mitochondria. **Detection**: Mitochondria-specific structures were observed in Ant1Tg/+ muscles but not in control muscles (Figure F, 3Q, and 3R). 2. **STBD1**: This receptor is involved in the selective autophagy of glycogen. **Observation**: Similar to SESN2, glycophagic structures were observed in Ant1Tg/+ muscles (Figure S). ### Cytoskeletal Organization and Intracellular Trafficking Genes 3. **Arhgap33**: Encoding a sorting nexin family member, this gene is involved in vesicular trafficking. **Observation**: Vesicular structures of various morphologies were observed in Ant1Tg/+ muscles, including multivesicular vacuoles (Figure G and 3H) and multilamellar vesicles (Figure I, 3J, and 3T). 4. **Arhgef2**: Encoding a Rho-Rac guanine nucleotide exchange factor, this gene is also involved in vesicular trafficking. **Observation**: Similar vesicular structures were observed in Ant1Tg/+ muscles (Figure D). ### Transmission Electron Microscopy 5. **Transmission Electron Microscopy**: Further examination revealed the presence of various membranous structures including multivesicular vacuoles and multilamellar vesicles in the muscles of Ant1Tg/+ mice. The origin of these structures is yet to be further investigated. ### Summary In summary, Ant1Tg/+ muscles show upregulation in genes involved in autophagy (SESN2, STBD1) and cytoskeletal organization/intracellular trafficking (Arhgap33, Arhgef2). Notably, transmission electron microscopy confirmed the presence of various vesicular structures, including multivesicular vacuoles and multilamellar vesicles, suggesting a disruption in normal cellular processes due to the Ant1 gene overexpression. Further investigation into the origin of these membranous structures is needed to fully understand their significance.
human: Second, we found that numerous genes involved in autophagy, cytoskeletal organization, and intracellular trafficking are upregulated in Ant1Tg/+ muscles ( L and S7M). Among the most upregulated genes related to autophagy are Sesn2 and Stbd1. SESN2 activates mitophagy . In accordance with this, we detected mitophagic structures in ANT1Tg/+ but not control muscles ( F, 3Q, and 3R). STBD1 is a selective autophagy receptor for glycogen , consistent with the presence of glycophagy-like structures in the Ant1Tg/+ muscles ( S). Arhgap33 and Arhgef2 are the mostly activated genes in the cytoskeletal organization and intracellular trafficking gene group. These two genes encode a sorting nexin family member and a Rho-Rac guanine nucleotide exchange factor, respectively, which are involved in vesicular trafficking . Our transmission electron microscopy analysis also revealed the presence of many vesicular structures of various morphologies in Ant1Tg/+ muscles, which includes multivesicular vacuoles ( G and 3H) and multilamellar vesicles ( I, 3J, and 3T; D). The origin of these membranous structures is yet to be further investigated.

draft: On November 24, 2021, the Omicron variant was officially identified by the South African authorities. The first confirmed case occurred on November 9, 2021. Initial cases were identified as a possible new variant because they did not display the characteristic symptoms of anosmia (loss of smell) and dysgeusia (loss of taste), unlike the predominant Delta variant, which caused more severe symptoms. Upon discovery, the Omicron variant was flagged due to its atypical mildness and docile progression. Following these concerns, genome sequencing confirmed the presence of this new variant. The analysis revealed that the Omicron variant contains more mutations than the Delta variant, which continues to cause significant mortality on a global scale. Consequently, the World Health Organization designated the Omicron variant as a "variant of concern" due to its increased mutation count.
human: The Omicron variant was officially announced by the South African authorities on the 24th of November 2021, with the first confirmed sample of the infection being collected on the 9th of November 2021. The initial cases were flagged as a possible new variant due to the absence of anosmia and dysgeusia in the clinical presentation of the patients. At the time of Omicron’s discovery, the predominant variant circulating within South Africa was the Delta variant B.1.617.2 which typically presented with more severe and stark symptoms. The cases of this suspected new variant were flagged due to their mildness and very docile disease progression. Subsequent to the suspicions of the circulation of a new variant, genome sequencing was performed and the new variant was discovered. The initial findings of the mutations present in Omicron called for the WHO to label the variant as one of “concern”, due to it having more mutations than the Delta variant which is still causing thousands of deaths internationally.

draft: Muscle wasting, also known as muscle atrophy, is characterized by a reduction in the size of muscle fibers and overall muscle mass and strength. This condition can be observed due to several factors including physiological aging and various diseases, such as neuromuscular degeneration, cancer, sepsis, diabetes, and cardiac failure. Muscle wasting is typically associated with a higher rate of protein degradation compared to protein synthesis. Mitochondrial dysfunction has been identified as a significant contributor to muscle wasting, particularly in conditions known as mitochondrial myopathies. However, mitochondrial dysfunction is also proposed to play a role in the progressive muscle wasting that occurs during aging. Despite this, the specific mechanisms by which mitochondrial dysfunction contributes to muscle wasting and the relationship between these mechanisms and protein homeostasis are not fully understood. Interestingly, recent research suggests that reducing mitochondrial respiration or ATP export, along with increasing oxidative stress, has a minimal impact on muscle mass homeostasis during aging. These findings imply that mitochondria may affect muscle mass homeostasis through additional or distinct mechanisms beyond bioenergetic defects and oxidative stress.
human: Muscle wasting (or atrophy) is defined by reduction of myofiber size and muscle mass and strength. It occurs during physiological aging, as well as in many diseases including neuromuscular degeneration, cancer, sepsis, diabetes, and cardiac failure. Muscle wasting is generally attributed to excessive protein degradation relative to protein synthesis . Mitochondrial dysfunction is known to cause muscle wasting in mitochondrial myopathies . It is also proposed to play a role in the progressive muscle wasting process during aging . However, how mitochondrial dysfunction contributes to muscle wasting and whether it is mechanistically linked to the loss of protein homeostasis are unclear. Interestingly, accumulating evidence indicates that merely reducing mitochondrial respiration or ATP export, along with elevated oxidative stress, has little or limited effect on muscle mass homeostasis during aging . These observations raise the possibility that mitochondria may affect muscle mass homeostasis by mechanisms additional to or distinct from bioenergetic defect and oxidative stress.

draft: In a study utilizing a seven-point Likert scale (ranging from 1, indicating "not at all," to 7, indicating "to a large extent"), the responses were categorized into three groups: (1) small extent (responses of 1 to 3), (2) medium extent (response of 4), and (3) great extent (responses of 5 to 7). The results revealed substantial discrepancies between the perceptions of physicians and those of the general public concerning the role of physicians in mitigating health disparities. Specifically, the chi-square test (χ² = 13.40) indicated a statistically significant difference (p < 0.001). Regarding the general public's perspective, 41% (205 individuals) considered reducing health disparities to be of small importance to physicians, 48% (240 individuals) viewed it as of significant importance, and 11% did not specify their level of importance. On the other hand, the physician respondents were more nuanced in their responses. Approximately one-third (31%, or 310 individuals) categorized the role as small, 56% (560 individuals) as significant, and 13% (130 individuals) chose the middle ground. There were significant differences between the physicians’ perceptions and those of the general public regarding the physicians’ role in reducing health disparities (χ2 = 13.40; p < 0.001). Among the members of the public, 41% (n = 205) said that reducing health disparities was a physicians’ role to a small extent, 48% (n = 240) said that it was their role to a larger extent, and 11% chose the middle category. In contrast, about one-third of physicians (31%; n = 310) said it was their role to a small extent, 56% (n = 560) said it was their role to a large extent, and 13% (n = 130) chose the middle category.

draft: The passage discusses the critical importance of early flowering induction in perennial crops to enhance breeding efficiency. Despite some advancements in shortening the juvenile phase, there is a notable lack of research on genes that promote or terminate juvenility. In this study, significant correlations were identified between the expression levels of EjRAV1/2 and three flowering activator genes in loquat trees at various growth stages. Specifically, at the seedling stage, high levels of EjRAV1/2 were associated with low expressions of EjFT and EjSOC1s. Conversely, in fruit-bearing trees, high levels of EjFT and EjSOC1s were observed alongside low levels of EjRAV1/2. Similarly, in olive and antirrhinum, high levels of DeTEM or AmTEM genes were detected during the juvenile phase. To further validate the role of EjRAV1/2, transgenic Arabidopsis plants overexpressing EjRAV1 and EjRAV2 were generated using two different background ecotypes (Col-3 and tem2). The results showed that these plants delayed flowering and extended the juvenile phase significantly, with a marked decrease in the expression levels of flowering activator genes. The results from these experiments are consistent with previous studies on the overexpression of AtTEM1/AtTEM2 and DeTEM/AmTEM. Our findings indicate that EjRAV1/2 are essential regulators of prolonged juvenility and repress floral induction in loquat.
human: The long juvenile phase would severely reduce breeding efficiency of a perennial crop. Therefore, identifying targets to promote flower initiation at early stage became utmost important . Although a few flowering regulating genes have been reported to shorten the juvenile period , few studies were focused on the identification of candidate genes associated with the promotion or release of juvenility . In the current study, remarkable negative correlations were discovered between the expressions of EjRAV1/2 and three flowering activator genes in loquat trees at different growth stages. The abundant accumulation of EjRAV1/2 was related with the low expressions of EjFT and EjSOC1s at seedling stage, while high expression levels of EjFT and EjSOC1s and low levels of EjRAV1/2 were detected in fruit bearing trees. Similarly in olive and antirrhinum, high DeTEM or AmTEM gene expressions were detected during the juvenile phase . To further validate the functions of EjRAV1/2, we generated overexpressed EjRAV1 and EjRAV2 transgenic plants of Arabidopsis with two different backgrounds (Col-0 ecotype and tem2), and the flowering time of all the transgenic plants were delayed while the juvenile period prolonged strikingly with a sharp decline of expression levels of flowering activator genes . Our results were consistent with previous studies on the overexpression of AtTEM1/AtTEM2 and DeTEM/AmTEM . Here, the gene expression analyses and overexpression experiments revealed that EjRAV1/2 are vital regulators of prolonged juvenility and repress floral induction in loquat.

draft: ### Centronuclear Myopathies (CNM) Centronuclear myopathies (CNM) are a rare group of genetic congenital muscle disorders characterized by abnormal nucleus localization in skeletal muscle cells. Patients with CNM experience a gradual worsening of muscle weakness, breathing problems, cardiomyopathy, neuropathy, and intellectual disabilities over time. In severe cases, lung failure or infection can lead to early infant death. ### Genetic Basis and Forms Mutations in several genes have been identified for CNM. The most severe form, X-linked Centronuclear Myopathy (XL-CNM), is caused by loss-of-function (LoF) mutations in the myotubularin gene, MTM1. Three different autosomal dominant (AD) forms of CNM are linked to mutations in the following genes: DMN2, BIN1, and RYR1. ### Treatment Options Ionis Pharmaceuticals is conducting an investigational antisense oligonucleotide (ASO) therapy, IONIS-DMN2-2.5rx, in a phase I/II trial for the treatment of autosomal dominant Centronuclear Myopathy (AD-CNM) due to DMN2 mutations. This therapy accounts for 50% of all Centronuclear Myopathy patients. IONIS-DMN2-2.5rx targets the gene encoding dynamin 2 (DMN2), leading to abnormalities primarily in the distal lower leg muscle.

The most severe form is the X-linked CNM (XL-CNM), which is caused by LoF mutations in the myotubularin MTM1 gene, while three different genes, DMN2, BIN1, and RYR1, have been identified to cause an autosomal dominant CNM (AD-CNM) form. Ionis has an investigational ASO (IONIS-DMN2-2.5rx) in a phase I/II trial for the treatment of DNM2 AD-CNM, which accounts for 50% of all CNM patients. Numismatic expert and Missouri Historical Society director Eric Newman proposed such a coin to George H. Moore, a federal judge and president of the society, on April 24, 1952. By September 1952, correspondence had developed between Newman and Thomas B. Curtis, the Republican representative for Missouri's 12th district. Curtis was informed of a similar initiative by Louisianans, with Congressman Hale Boggs introducing a bill that had not garnered action during the 82nd Congress but was set to reintroduce in January 1953. draft: ### Explanation of Normalization Methods and Their Effects The study examined various normalization methods to ensure accurate clustering and discrimination of data samples. All tested normalization methods resulted in small quality control (QC) sample offsets, suggesting that raw data quality and adequate filtering in the Compound Discoverer software were appropriate. The original data set also showed appropriate quality with QC presence above 50% and a relative standard deviation (RSD) of ≤30% in quality control samples. When normalizing the data to total protein content, the gill and skin mucus samples did not cluster as clearly as they did without normalization. Importantly, normalization to total protein content slightly impaired the clustering between experimental groups compared to no normalization. Normalization by sum was found to be superior to normalization by protein content. However, the benzocaine and percussive stunning subgroups were not clearly separated in principal component analysis (PCA) score plots and hierarchical clustering dendrograms generated using the Euclidean distance, as indicated by the text. Normalization by median or median fold change provided more distinct clustering compared to normalization by sum. Specifically, these methods enabled clear separation of the mucus samples induced by benzocaine overdosing and percussive stunning. Additionally, they distinguished samples obtained following either benzocaine overdose or percussive stunning. The observed trends were further validated by creating supervised orthogonal partial least squares discriminant analysis (OPLS-DA) models. These models significantly discriminated between the two types of mucus and between the percussive stunning and benzocaine-treated sub-groups. The permutation test results, which consisted of 100 permutations, confirmed the lack of overfitting. The quality parameters of the constructed OPLS-DA models associated with the top-performing normalization methods (specifically normalization by median and median fold change) showed comparable levels of variance (R2Y) and predictability (Q2Y). Therefore, we selected the normalization by median approach to further investigate general metabolic variations between skin and gill mucus and dysregulation following anesthesia.

draft: In healthy individuals, NGAL is produced in minimal quantities by various organs. It is released from tissues and activated neutrophils and macrophages in response to cellular stressors such as ischemia, hypoxia, acute kidney injury (AKI), infection, inflammation, or neoplastic transformation. After glomerular filtration, NGAL undergoes reabsorption in the proximal tubule. Proximal tubule damage results in an elevated concentration of NGAL in the urine, whereas damage to the distal nephron increases its synthesis and release into the blood and urine. NGAL serves as a well-established diagnostic and prognostic marker for AKI and chronic kidney disease (CKD). The clinical utility of NGAL has been validated in systemic infections, particularly in urinary tract infections (UTI) among children. However, few studies have investigated the relationship between NGAL and the development of anemia in systemic infections, with only one report focusing on children. Given the frequent occurrence of UTI as a bacterial infection in children, further research into the connection between NGAL levels and anemia can aid in assessing the risk of infection-associated anemia (IA) and predicting the severity of IA in children suffering from UTI.

It is released from tissues and activated neutrophils and macrophages in response to cellular stress, such as ischemia, hypoxia, acute kidney injury (AKI), infection, inflammation or neoplastic transformation. NGAL undergoes glomerular filtration with subsequent reabsorption in the proximal tubule. Proximal tubule damage causes an increase in the concentration of NGAL in the urine, while damage to the distal part of the nephron causes increased synthesis and release of NGAL into the blood and the urine. NGAL is a well-known diagnostic and prognostic marker of AKI and chronic kidney disease (CKD). The clinical usefulness of NGAL has been demonstrated in systemic infections, including urinary tract infections (UTI) in children. So far, few studies investigating the relationship between NGAL and the occurrence of anemia in systemic infections have been published, including only a single report in children. Since UTI is one of the most common bacterial infections in children, investigation of the relationship between NGAL and anemia can contribute to the risk assessment of IA and prediction of the severity of IA in children with UTI.

Specifically, IL-18, a pleiotropic pro-inflammatory cytokine with abnormal expression in sepsis and a marker of inflammasome activity, serves as a reliable predictor for the outcome of critically ill septic patients. Additionally, IL-18 can activate neutrophils to induce reactive oxygen species (ROS) generation, damaging the vascular endothelium and basal membrane, thereby accelerating organ damage. Studies by Rogers and Mierzchala-Pasierb indicate that elevated levels of IL-18 in critically ill patients correlate with disease severity and predict increased mortality in the intensive care unit (ICU). Specifically, IL-18, a pleiotropic pro-inflammatory cytokine with abnormal expression in sepsis and a marker of inflammasome activity, has a documented value as a prognostic indicator for the outcome of critically ill septic patients. IL-18, a cytokine upstream of the inflammatory cascade reaction, induces the massive synthesis of inflammatory cytokines (TNF, IL-1β), which are the key mediators of sepsis-induced organ injury. These pro-inflammatory cytokines initiate the inflammatory responses involved in the progression of sepsis. Furthermore, IL-18 may also activate neutrophils to induce ROS generation, thereby damaging the vascular endothelium and basal membrane, eventually accelerating organ damage. IL-18 has been shown to be an effective indicator for monitoring treatment efficacy and patient recovery in patients with sepsis. Rogers et al. as well as Mierzchala-Pasierb et al. have shown that increased IL-18 levels in critically ill patients correlated with disease severity and predicted ICU mortality. Furthermore, besides the septic parameter, Wu et al. showed that NLRP3 inflammasome may sense lung alveolar stretch to induce the release of downstream pro-inflammatory cytokines, contributing to the mechanism of lung inflammatory injury during mechanical ventilation.

draft: ### Detailed Process for Ultrathin Section Preparation and Staining of Fresh Quadriceps Muscle Samples from Ant1Tg/+ Mice and Their Littermates #### Step 1: Sample Fixation (3-4 Ultrathin Sections per Sample) - Fresh quadriceps muscle samples were taken from two groups of mice: Ant1Tg/+ mice and their littermate controls. - Mice were aged one and two years old. - The samples were fixed using 4% glutaraldehyde in a buffer solution (0.1 M cacodylate buffer, pH 7.2) at room temperature for two hours. - The samples were then fixed again using 1% osmium tetroxide in the same buffer solution at room temperature for one hour. #### Step 2: Specimen Dehydration - The fixed samples were dehydrated through successive ethanol and propylene oxide solutions: - 50% ethanol - 70% ethanol - 90% ethanol - 100% ethanol #### Step 3: Specimen Embedding - The dehydrated specimens were embedded in Luft's Araldite 502 embedding medium. - This medium was used to solidify the muscle samples and serve as a foundation for thin section cutting. - The specimens were embedded for thin section preparation, which involved cutting the muscle samples into ultrathin sections. #### Step 4: Ultrathin Section Staining - The ultrathin sections were stained using: - Ethanolic Uranyl Acetate - Reynold’s Lead Citrate #### Step 5: Examination and Imaging - The stained ultrathin sections were examined using a transmission electron microscope (JOEL JEM1400). - High-resolution images were acquired using a Gaten DAT-832 Orius camera to capture the ultrastructural details of the muscle samples. ### Summary The process involved the fixation of muscle samples from Ant1Tg/+ mice and their littermates using glutaraldehyde and osmium tetroxide, followed by dehydration and embedding steps. Ultrathin sections were then stained and examined under a transmission electron microscope to observe the ultrastructure of the muscle tissue.

The specimens were dehydrated in 50%, 70%, 90%, 100% ethanol and propylene oxide, before being embedded in Luft's Araldite 502 embedding medium (Electron Microscopy Sciences, Hatfield, PA) and cut into thin sections. The ultrathin sections were then stained with ethanolic uranyl acetate and Reynold’s lead citrate (Polysciences). The samples were examined with a JOEL JEM1400 transmission electron microscope and images were acquired with a Gaten DAT-832 Orius camera.
