draft: The pharmacist profession must adapt to the evolving market changes affecting other health sectors. The education of pharmacists, through carefully planned curricula, must adapt to meet the ever-changing needs of the workforce and prepare them to embrace advancements in the field. To this end, it is essential to update undergraduate pharmacy education and training programs to reflect both present and future needs. A comprehensive and clear view of the goals is needed in higher education institutions (HEIs) to optimize the strategic planning and decision-making process of curricular development. To gain a deeper understanding of the context, we propose to approach the issue from three different perspectives: 1. **International Recommendations:** We consider the International Pharmaceutical Federation (FIP) Development Goals framework, the Pharmacy Education in Europe (PHARMINE) project, and the Quality Assurance in European Pharmacy Education and Training (PHAR-QA) for international perspectives. 2. **National Changes Required:** We examine the changes encouraged by Hungarian professional organizations over the past decade. 3. **Graduates' Perceptions:** We analyze the views of novice Hungarian pharmacists to gain insight into current educational experiences. The goal of this study is to explore the process of change and identify relevant objectives through the interpretation of novice Hungarian pharmacists' views. By doing so, we aim to make prospective recommendations for updating pharmacy education in Hungary.
human: The pharmacist profession needs to recognize and adapt to the market-oriented changes also affecting other health sectors today. Pharmacy education through strategically planned curricula must provide educational outcomes that serve ever-changing workforce needs and allow flexible adaptation to advancements in pharmacy . To update national undergraduate pharmacy education and training program, a comprehensive and clear view of both present and future goals is needed in higher education institutions (HEI) to optimize the strategic planning and decision-making process of a curricular development. For a better understanding of the context, we propose to address the issue from three different perspectives, (a) The international recommendations upon professional development and pharmacist education by the International Pharmaceutical Federation (FIP) Development Goals framework , the Pharmacy Education in Europe (PHARMINE) project and the Quality Assurance in European Pharmacy Education and Training (PHAR-QA) , (b) The national changes required in pharmacy education, Hungarian professional organizations have been encouraging during the past decade and, (c) graduates’ perceptions of pharmacy education. The goal of this study is to explore the process of change and identify relevant objectives through the interpretation of novice Hungarian pharmacists’ views and to make prospective recommendations for updating pharmacy education in Hungary.

draft: The valence states of the elements in the Porous NVP/C composites were evaluated using X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS). Specifically, the Vanadium (V) 2p signals were observed at binding energies of approximately 517 and 524 eV, corresponding to the V 2p3/2 and V 2p1/2 states, respectively. These peak positions align well with the previously reported values for sodium (Na) and vanadium (V) in compounds such as Na3V2(PO4)3 or Li3V2(PO4)3, confirming the trivalent state of vanadium (V3+) in the Porous NVP/C composites, as expected from the theoretical composition of Na3V2(PO4)3. The Sodium (Na) 1s signal at ~1071 eV is characteristic of sodium ions in the vanadium phosphate structure. The Oxygen (O) 1s signal was detected at ~531.2 eV, while the Phosphorus (P) 2p signal at ~133.4 eV indicates the presence of the phosphate (PO4)3− group. Given that the average binding energy of the oxide-based O 1s peak is typically ~528.5 eV, the higher binding energy observed for the Porous NVP/C composites can be attributed to more covalent characteristics of the P-O bonds. Additionally, the P 2p signal at ~129 eV without any other peaks demonstrates that phosphorus exists in the form of the phosphate (PO4)3− group rather than the phosphide group. Based on these XPS results, the synthesis of the Porous NVP/C composites was successfully achieved as intended. To further confirm the chemical composition, Inductively Coupled Plasma Atomic Emission Spectroscopy (ICP-AES) was utilized. The results showed that the atomic percentages of Na and V were 0.857 and 0.573, respectively, leading to an assumed calculated chemical composition of Na2.99V2(PO4)3, which closely matches the expected theoretical composition.

In addition, the O 1s signal at 531.2 eV and the P 2p signal at ~133.4 eV were attributed to the oxygen and phosphorous atoms of the (PO4)3− phosphate group. Considering that the O 1s peak of the oxide-based material is generally located at ~528.5 eV, the higher binding energy of O 1s peak for the Porous NVP/C composites can be understood as more covalent characteristics of P-O bonds. draft: The findings suggest that TbNup144, unlike TbNup62 and TbNup53a, is essential for the proper segregation of the nucleus. However, the specific function of TbNup144 during karyokinesis remains unclear. Regarding TbNup158, its effect on the cell cycle is only partially understood. While the relative ratios of the G1 and G2/M phases are similar to those observed in TbNup62 and TbNup53a RNAi cell lines, an increase in the sub-G1 phase was noted, as evidenced by microscopy (Fig. S3A). The enrichment in the sub-G1 phase is attributed to zoid cells (1K0N) (Fig. S3B & C). Notably, the proportion of annexin-positive cells is significantly lower in the TbNup158 RNAi cell line compared to the TbNup144 RNAi cell line (Fig. S4). This observation suggests that the influence of TbNup158 on cell cycle progression is delayed or indirect, as well as concurrent with the growth defect observed. The impact of TbNup144 silencing on the cell cycle progression is minimal compared to TbNup144, indicating that this is not an incidental effect of RNAi or a broader destabilization of the nuclear pore complex. A deeper investigation is required to elucidate the precise molecular mechanism by which TbNup144 affects nuclear division, which may be crucial for understanding the regulation of the cell cycle in these medically important parasites.
human: These results indicate that TbNup144, but not TbNup62 or TbNup53a, is necessary for regular segregation of the nucleus, but its exact role during karyokinesis remains unknown. In the case of TbNup158, the effect on the cell cycle was somewhat intermediate. Although the relative ratio of G1 and G2/M phases was similar to that observed in TbNup62 and TbNup53a RNAi cell lines, we did notice an enrichment in the sub-G1 phase (Supplementary Fig. S3 B&C). These were most likely the zoid cells (1K0N) (Supplementary Fig. S3A), also observed by microscopy. However, the population of annexin-positive cells was significantly lower in the TbNup158 RNAi cell line than in the TbNup144 (Supplementary Fig. S4). This suggests that the effect of TbNup158 on cell cycle progression was considerably delayed or indirect, concurrent with the delayed growth defect observed in this cell line. The impact of silencing FG-Nups on the cell cycle was minimal compared to TbNup144, indicating that this is not an incidental effect of RNAi or a more global destabilization of the NPC. A more comprehensive investigation is needed to better understand the detailed molecular mechanism behind the role of TbNup144 in nuclear division, which may be a key point in the cell cycle regulation of these medically important parasites.

draft: The study observed that both oxidative stress and inflammation were present in T2DM patients with vitamin D deficiency. These are well-established cardiovascular disease (CVD) risk factors. To investigate the interaction between malondialdehyde (MDA) and ferric reducing-ascorbate plasmanate (FRAP) and their connection with high-sensitivity C-reactive protein (hs-CRP), the researchers studied these interactions. Adjusting for body mass index (BMI) and statin use, significant associations were found between oxidative stress and inflammation in T2DM patients with vitamin D deficiency. A South Indian study reported that oral vitamin D supplementation of 60,000 IU/week for eight weeks significantly reduced serum MDA levels and improved the total antioxidant status in T2DM patients with vitamin D deficiency. Meta-analyses of randomized controlled trials examining the effects of vitamin D supplementation on diabetic patients have shown that vitamin D supplementation attenuates both inflammation and oxidative stress by improving the antioxidant status. This improvement is achieved through modifying adipokine concentrations and reducing pro-inflammatory cytokines such as TNF-α and natriuretic peptides, while also decreasing blood pressure. The biological activity of vitamin D is primarily due to its interaction with a nuclear vitamin D receptor (VDR), which regulates the transcription of genes coding for NADPH oxidase, an enzyme that catalyzes the conversion of oxygen into superoxide. Additionally, this interaction suppresses TNF-α-induced nuclear factor kappa B (NF-κB) activation, thereby preventing further oxidative and inflammatory modifications.

draft: The study included phase I and phase II clinical trials that were initiated and concluded between 2003 and 2017. These studies aimed to evaluate the clinical efficacy of DNA therapeutic vaccines that expressed HPV E6 and E7 oncoproteins for treating cervical intraepithelial lesions of grades 2 and 3. These lesions could either be newly diagnosed or recurrent, and in some cases, they were followed by conization or loop electrosurgical excision procedure. The study population comprised female patients aged 18 years or older who had histopathologically confirmed Cervical Intraepithelial Neoplasia (CIN) grades 2 and 3, and the lesions were confirmed to be caused by HPV 16 and/or HPV 18 based on Polymerase Chain Reaction (PCR) amplification results. The primary outcomes of the review focused on the following: 1. **Lesion Regression:** The efficacy of the treatment was assessed based on the regression of the lesions. 2. **Viral Load Reduction:** The reduction in the level of virus present in the lesions was considered. 3. **Immunogenicity:** The study also evaluated the immunogenic response, specifically focusing on the induction of cytotoxic CD8+ T cells that are specific to HPV E6 and E7 proteins. 4. **Adverse Events (AEs):** The incidence and nature of any adverse events occurring after vaccination were also documented. In summary, the research aimed to assess the clinical efficacy of DNA therapeutic vaccines against cervical intraepithelial lesions grades 2 and 3, considering their impact on lesion regression, viral load reduction, immunogenic response, and safety.

draft: Substrate binding to P450s, despite its broad substrate versatility, is a highly regulated process. This regulation occurs through interactions that take place within the enzyme's active site. These interactions typically cause conformational changes in the enzyme structure, which in turn close the active site around the substrate. The structural dynamics of the P450 enzyme primarily involve changes in specific secondary structural elements. These changes bring the active site closer to the substrate. As a result, the axial water ligand attached to the heme iron is displaced, and the heme iron changes its spin state to a higher spin. This process reduces the accessibility of the active site to the external environment. Binding is considered productive when the architecture and chemistry of the active site align with the substrate's chemistry and geometry. When the enzyme's structure and chemistry fit the substrate, the enzyme becomes highly efficient in catalyzing the reaction. The overall catalytic efficiency of the P450 enzyme thus depends on the frequency at which this fitting or alignment occurs.
human: Notwithstanding the wide substrate versatility, substrate binding to P450s is a finely regulated event. Regulation is achieved through enzyme-substrate interactions established within the active site that often activate conformational transitions. The structural dynamics of P450s mainly consist of the rearrangements of specific secondary structural elements that close the active site around the substrate, promoting the displacement of the axial water ligand from the heme iron that switches to the high spin-state, and minimizing the access to the external environment. Productive binding occurs when the architecture and the chemistry of the catalytic chamber fit the chemistry and the geometry of the substrate. The overall catalytic efficiency of the enzyme depends on the frequency of the achievement of this state.

draft: Amazing Stories Quarterly was a significant U.S. science fiction pulp magazine published from 1928 to 1934. It was established by Hugo Gernsback, who had earlier founded Amazing Stories, the first science fiction magazine, in April 1926. Initially, Amazing Stories had successfully published annual editions, selling well. Gernsback’s subsequent decision to launch a quarterly magazine stemmed from the success of these annuals. The inaugural issue of Amazing Stories Quarterly, dated Winter 1928, featured a reprint of H.G. Wells' "When the Sleeper Wakes," published in 1899. However, following the publication of Gernsback’s own novel, "Ralph 124C 41+," in the Winter 1929 issue, the magazine largely ceased reprinting full-length novels. Gernsback experienced financial troubles in early 1929 and lost control of both Amazing Stories and Amazing Stories Quarterly. Subsequently, T. O’Conor Sloane took over as editor. The magazine faced financial challenges by 1932 and began publishing irregularly, concluding with the issue dated Fall 1934. Several notable authors contributed to Amazing Stories Quarterly, including Stanton A. Coblentz, Miles J. Breuer, A. Hyatt Verrill, and Jack Williamson. Critical assessments of the magazine's fiction vary. Brian Stableford views several of the novels as important early science fiction works, while Everett Bleiler notes that the majority of the stories were of lower quality. Milton Wolf and Mike Ashley, however, offer a more positive perspective, suggesting that Sloane’s contributions during the early 1930s were among the best in the burgeoning genre.
human: Amazing Stories Quarterly was a U.S. science fiction pulp magazine that was published between 1928 and 1934. It was launched by Hugo Gernsback as a companion to his Amazing Stories, the first science fiction magazine, which had begun publishing in April 1926. Amazing Stories had been successful enough for Gernsback to try a single issue of an Amazing Stories Annual in 1927, which had sold well, and he decided to follow it up with a quarterly magazine. The first issue of Amazing Stories Quarterly was dated Winter 1928 and carried a reprint of the 1899 version of H.G. Wells' When the Sleeper Wakes. Gernsback's policy of running a novel in each issue was popular with his readership, though the choice of Wells' novel was less so. Over the next five issues, only one more reprint appeared: Gernsback's own novel Ralph 124C 41+, in the Winter 1929 issue. Gernsback went bankrupt in early 1929, and lost control of both Amazing Stories and Amazing Stories Quarterly; associate editor T. O'Conor Sloane then took over as editor. The magazine began to run into financial difficulties in 1932, and the schedule became irregular; the last issue was dated Fall 1934. Authors whose work appeared in Amazing Stories Quarterly include Stanton A. Coblentz, Miles J. Breuer, A. Hyatt Verrill, and Jack Williamson. Critical opinions differ on the quality of the fiction Gernsback and Sloane printed: Brian Stableford regards several of the novels as being important early science fiction, but Everett Bleiler comments that few of the stories were of acceptable quality. Milton Wolf and Mike Ashley are more positive in their assessment; they consider the work Sloane published in the early 1930s to be some of the best in the new genre.

draft: Adult stem cells are present in most tissues and possess the unique ability to differentiate when needed throughout an individual's entire life cycle. This ability is rooted in the stem cell's unique capability for self-renewal, which involves dividing to produce both a daughter stem cell and a daughter cell that begins the differentiation process. The stem cell's distinct property is attributed to its local environment, known as the niche, which supports the stem cell. The niche serves as a local environment that houses stem cells and influences their behavior. Specifically, a daughter cell within the niche's influence area maintains stemness and does not differentiate further. Conversely, a daughter cell that falls outside this niche's area of influence loses its stemness and begins the process of differentiation. Furthermore, stem cells are attached to niche cells and are influenced by signaling molecules from these niche cells. This interaction ensures the stem cells remain in their undifferentiated state until they are needed for differentiation.
human: Adult stem cells are present in most tissues and provide differentiated cells when needed throughout an animal’s entire life . This ability is realized through a stem cell’s unique capability for self-renewing cell division, in which it divides to simultaneously generate a daughter stem cell and a daughter cell that initiates differentiation . This unique property of stem cells is provided by the niche, a local environment that houses stem cells: a daughter cell within the niche’s area of influence maintains stemness and does not undergo differentiation, while one outside the niche loses stemness and starts differentiation . Accordingly, stem cells are attached to niche cells and influenced by signaling molecules from them.

draft: ### Development and Properties of Porous NVP/C Composite The goal of this study was to develop a composite material consisting of a nitrogen-containing polyvinylamine (NVP) and carbon. This composite material was designed to have a porous structure. The strategy employed chelating interactions between NVP precursors and poly(vinylalcohol) (PVA) to achieve this porous structure. ### Advantages of the Porous Structure The porous structure of the composite material offers several significant electrochemical advantages: 1. **Enhanced Interfacial Electrical Conductivity and Sodium Ion Transfer**: The thin and uniform carbon coating on the NVP particles improves the interfacial electrical conductivity and enhances the transfer of sodium ions. This results in a more efficient sodium ion transport within the composite. 2. **Prevention of Aggregation**: The carbon coating also helps to prevent the aggregation of NVP particles, ensuring that the particles respond uniformly. This uniform response is crucial for maintaining consistent performance during electrochemical processes. 3. **Increased Surface Area**: The porous carbon framework provides a larger surface area, which increases the number of active redox sites on the composite material. This enhanced surface area contributes to better performance by increasing the overall active redox capacity of the composite. ### Electrochemical Performance The Porous NVP/C composite exhibits excellent electrochemical properties when used as a cathode material for sodium-ion batteries (SIBs). These properties are further investigated in the following sections to understand their specific characteristics and contributions. ### Study on Carbon Layer Characteristics To investigate the electrochemical properties of the Porous NVP/C composite, the characteristics of the carbon layer were studied using the conventional simple carbon-coating method. Specifically, the following properties were examined: 1. **Porosity**: Understanding the porosity of the carbon layer helps to determine the effective electrode volume and the amount of active material accessible to the electrolyte. 2. **Specific Surface Area**: The specific surface area of the carbon layer provides insight into the amount of active surface area per unit mass of the composite. This is crucial for determining the overall capacity of the composite. 3. **Coating Layer Thickness**: Measuring the thickness of the carbon coating layer allows for a detailed analysis of how the thickness affects the composite's performance. By examining these characteristics, the study aimed to elucidate the factors that contribute to the outstanding electrochemical properties of the Porous NVP/C composite

The advantages of the porous structure are related to the formation of an interconnected carbon framework and forming isolated NVP particles embedded in the porous carbon matrix. In detail, the Porous NVP/C composite had potential electrochemical advantages: (i) the thin and homogeneous carbon coating layer on NVP particles enhanced the interfacial electrical conductivity and sodium ion transfer; (ii) the suppression of NVP particle aggregation facilitated the uniform response of the particles; and (iii) the porous carbon framework provided a larger surface area that increased the active redox surface of the composites. Consequently, the Porous NVP/C composite exhibited outstanding electrochemical properties as cathode material for SIBs. In this study, in order to study the improvement of electrochemical properties, the characteristics of the carbon layer such as the porosity, specific surface area, and the coating layer thickness were investigated with the conventional simple carbon-coating method.

draft: ### Thorium Isotopes and Properties #### General Information - **Isotopes**: There are seven naturally occurring isotopes of thorium, but none are stable. - **Primary Isotope**: 232Th is the most abundant naturally occurring isotope of thorium. It occurs in significant quantities. - **Half-Life**: 232Th has a very long half-life of approximately 14.0 billion years, which is about three times the age of the Earth and even longer than the age of the universe. #### Atomic Weight - **Atomic Weight**: The atomic weight of 232Th is 232.0377±0.0004. #### Terrestrial Composition - **Characteristics**: Thorium has a characteristic terrestrial isotopic composition. - **Nuclear Subshell**: The stability of 232Th is attributed to its closed nuclear subshell, which includes 142 neutrons. #### Decay Chain - **4n Decay Chain**: The decay of 232Th initiates the 4n decay chain, also known as the thorium series. - **Chain Components**: The thorium series includes isotopes with a mass number divisible by 4, ranging from 228Ra to 208Pb. - **Decay Process**: The chain begins with the decay of 232Th to 228Ra and terminates at 208Pb. Any sample of thorium or its compounds contains traces of these isotopes. - **Nuclear Decay**: Thorium nuclei are susceptible to alpha decay because the strong nuclear force cannot overcome the electromagnetic repulsion between protons. #### Usefulness of Daughter Nuclides - **Chemical Purification**: Thorium samples can be chemically purified to extract useful daughter nuclides. - **Application**: These daughter nuclides, such as 212Pb, are used in nuclear medicine for cancer therapy. - **227Th**: Another isotope of interest, 227Th, can also be used in cancer treatments through targeted alpha therapies. #### Rare Decay Processes - **Fission**: Thorium nuclei can undergo rare processes including spontaneous fission, which is very infrequent. - **Half-Life**: The partial half-life for this process is over 1021 years. - **Evidence**: The evidence for spontaneous fission comes predominantly from 232Th. ### Summary - **Isotopes**: Thorium has seven naturally occurring isotopes, but 232Th is the most abundant. - **Properties**: It exhibits a long half-life and is part of the 4n decay chain. - **Usefulness**: Thorium and its daughter nuclides, particularly 212Pb and 227Th, have applications in nuclear medicine and cancer therapy. - **Rare Decay**: Thorium can occasionally undergo spontaneous fission, but this occurs very infrequently. Its stability is attributed to its closed nuclear subshell with 142 neutrons. Thorium has a characteristic terrestrial isotopic composition, with atomic weight 232.0377±0.0004. It is one of only four radioactive elements (along with bismuth, protactinium and uranium) that occur in large enough quantities on Earth for a standard atomic weight to be determined. Thorium nuclei are susceptible to alpha decay because the strong nuclear force cannot overcome the electromagnetic repulsion between their protons. The alpha decay of 232Th initiates the 4n decay chain, or thorium series, which includes isotopes with a mass number divisible by 4. This chain of consecutive alpha and beta decays begins with the decay of 232Th to 228Ra and terminates at 208Pb. Any sample of thorium or its compounds contains traces of these daughters, which are isotopes of thallium, lead, bismuth, polonium, radon, radium, and actinium. Natural thorium samples can be chemically purified to extract useful daughter nuclides, such as 212Pb, which is used in nuclear medicine for cancer therapy. 227Th (alpha emitter, 18.693 days half-life) can also be used in cancer treatments such as targeted alpha therapies. 232Th also very occasionally undergoes spontaneous fission rather than alpha decay, but at a much lower rate than uranium-238 and all natural fission products and evidence come predominantly from it. Its partial half-life for this process is very long at over 1021 years.

In contrast, both dwarf lemurs and fork-marked lemurs are considered more distantly related. Fork-marked lemurs are either a sister group to all cheirogaleids or more closely related to the sportive lemurs (Lepilemur). Although Mirza, Microcebus, and Allocebus form a clade within Cheirogaleidae, the three lineages diverged during a relatively narrow timeframe. Consequently, the relationships within this clade are complex and may evolve with further research. All three clades are believed to have diverged at least 20 million years ago (mya), although an mtDNA-based estimate places the divergence between Mirza and Microcebus at approximately 24.2 mya. The divergence between the two recognized species of giant mouse lemur is estimated to have occurred around 2.1 mya.

draft: On admission, the following clinical and laboratory data were evaluated: age in months, sex, the onset and duration of fever in days before admission, results of urinalysis and urine culture, complete blood count (CBC), serum neutrophil gelatinase-associated lipase (NGAL), C-reactive protein (CRP), procalcitonin (PCT), and creatinine (Cr) levels. Urine specimens were collected via bladder catheterization. A urinary tract infection (UTI) diagnosis was confirmed based on the presence of pyuria alongside a positive urine culture. Pyuria was defined as the presence of ≥ 5 white blood cells per high-powered field in a centrifuged urine specimen. Significant bacteriuria was determined by pure bacterial growth of ≥ 50,000 colony-forming units (CFU) per milliliter or ≥ 10,000 CFU per milliliter, depending on the concurrent presence of fever and pyuria. Fever was defined as a body temperature of at least 38.0°C within a 24-hour period following presentation.

draft: Several 5’ isomiRs resulting from alternative Drosha cleavages have diverse biological functions. For instance, we have demonstrated that the 5’ isomiRs of miR-9-5p, produced from pri-miR-9-1, regulate a distinct set of target mRNAs in low-grade gliomas. Additionally, another study has highlighted the critical role of miR-9-3p in hippocampal synaptic plasticity and memory. It is conceivable that the 5’ isomiR of miR-9-3p also plays a functional role in brain cells, where its expression is differently regulated. Our research shows that Drosha cleavage fidelity decreases in multiple cancers, leading to an increased number of miRNAs with altered 5’ ends and seed sequences. This observation has prompted us to hypothesize that during tumorigenesis, Drosha processing is altered to generate 5’ isomiRs that affect tumour progression. Our findings indicate that pri-miRNA-associated regulatory proteins (RBPs) modulate 5’ isomiR production by influencing the structure of the pri-miRNA. This suggests one possible underlying mechanism. It is possible that only a subset of the aberrantly produced 5’ isomiRs in tumours have functional significance. Future research identifying oncogenic or tumour suppressive 5’ isomiRs will provide further insights.

Another study has shown that miR-9-3p has a critical role in hippocampal synaptic plasticity and memory. It is possible that the 5’ isomiR of miR-9-3p also plays a functional role in brain cells where it is differentially expressed. Here, we find that Drosha cleavage fidelity decreases in multiple cancers, resulting in numerous miRNAs with altered 5’ ends and seed sequences. Our findings show that pri-miRNA-associated RBPs promote or inhibit 5’ isomiR production by modulating the pri-miRNA structure, providing one possible underlying mechanism. Future studies identifying oncogenic or tumour suppressive 5’ isomiRs will provide additional insights.

draft: This systematic review presents the results of phase I and phase II clinical trials investigating the treatment of patients with histopathologically confirmed cervical intraepithelial neoplasia (CIN) associated with human papillomavirus (HPV) 16 or 18 using DNA therapeutic vaccines. Six studies have documented immunological responses through lesion regression, viral clearance, and enhanced T-cell responses following the administration of five different DNA vaccines—GX-188E (both phases), VGX-3100, pNGVL4a-CRT/E7 (detox), pNGVL4a-Sig/E7 (detox)/HSP70, and MEDI0457. These vaccines encode for either non-oncogenic E6/E7 or both, alongside chaperonin proteins such as HSP70 and calreticulin to enhance antigen presentation by antigen-presenting cells and subsequent MHC class I processing and presentation. The vaccines were generally well-tolerated by patients, resulting in only mild systemic and local side effects, such as grades 1 or less. MEDI0457 incorporated the same plasmid formulation as VGX-3100 but also included plasmids encoding for IL-12.
human: This systematic review summarizes the findings of phase I and phase II clinical trials investigating the treatment of patients with histopathologically diagnosed CIN associated with HPV 16 or/and HPV 18 with DNA therapeutic vaccines. Six studies have demonstrated immunologic response in the form of lesion size regression, viral clearance, and increased T cell response of five different DNA vaccines–GX-188E (phase I and phase II), VGX-3100, pNGVL4a-CRT/E7 (detox), pNGVL4a-Sig/E7 (detox)/HSP70, MEDI0457. Vaccines were plasmid DNA encoding for either non-oncogenic E6/E7 or both, and chaperonin proteins such as HSP 70 and Calreticulin for the enhancement of the uptake by antigen-presenting cells, and MHC class I processing and presentation. MEDI0457 had the same plasmid formulation as VGX-3100 combined with plasmid encoding IL-12. All vaccines were well tolerated by patients, leading to only grade 1 or less systemic and local side effects.

draft: To date, various genome-wide association studies (GWAS) have been conducted to identify susceptibility loci for coronary artery involvement in Kawasaki disease (KD), utilizing a very small number of patients with both KD and coronary artery anomalies (CAA). No overlapping genetic loci were detected from these GWAS. Our study identified five rare coding variants in five different genes associated with coronary artery involvement (CAA) in patients with KD. None of these five genes have previously been reported to be linked to susceptibility to KD or CAA. The gene MMP8 encodes a member of the matrix metalloproteinase (MMP) family of proteins, which are involved in maintaining the structure and function of coronary vascular walls. Increasing numbers of studies have reported elevated expression, activity, or protein levels of MMPs in KD. MMP8 expression levels are significantly elevated in KD patients before intravenous immunoglobulin (IVIG) therapy and decrease after its administration. Additionally, MMP8 is highly abundant in patients with IVIG-resistant KD, suggesting that MMP8 may serve as a potential biomarker for identifying KD patients at highest risk for coronary artery involvement and potentially benefiting from additional anti-inflammatory therapy.
human: To date, several GWAS have been performed to identify susceptibility loci for coronary artery formation in KD, using a very limited number of patients with KD and CAA. No overlapping genetic loci were detected from these GWAS. In this study, we identified five rare coding variants in five genes associated with CAAs in KD. None of these five genes, except for MMP8, have been reported to be associated with susceptibility to KD or CAAs in KD. MMP8 encodes a member of the matrix metalloproteinase (MMP) family of proteins, which may be involved in maintaining the structure and function of coronary vascular walls. An increasing number of studies have indicated elevated expression, activity, or protein levels of MMPs in KD. MMP8 expression levels are significantly upregulated in KD before IVIG treatment and decrease after undergoing IVIG treatment. MMP8 is also highly abundant in IVIG-resistant KD, suggesting that this is a potential biomarker for identifying those KD patients at highest risk for CAAs, and who may benefit from additional anti-inflammatory therapy.

human: It is well known that the body generates an adaptive immune response by recognizing the epitopes of pathogenic bacteria to resist the invasion of foreign pathogens. Therefore, the acquisition of epitopes is a very important stage in the diagnosis of diseases, understanding of immune protection mechanisms, and vaccine development. In this study, we identified two novel B-cell epitopes from HspA and detected the antibody expression profiles of these epitope peptides in an H. pylori-naturally-infected population. Our findings provide a basis for further study on the role of HspA in immune response and immune prevention caused by H. pylori infection.

draft: The management of chronic periprosthetic joint infection (PJI) predominantly involves the use of temporary antibiotic-loaded cement spacers during two-stage procedures; however, there are instances where authors perform two-stage revision hip arthroplasty without the use of a temporary spacer in the initial stage. Hipfl et al. studied a total of 135 hip PJI cases. Specifically, 28 patients had a femoral bone loss categorized as Paprosky type ≥3A, which was further divided as follows: 14 patients were classified as Paprosky type 3, 11 patients as type 3B, and 3 patients as type 4. The researchers reported an infection rate of 25% (7 out of 28 patients) for those with a femoral bone loss type ≥3A. Additionally, the reinfection rate was 8.4% (9 out of 107 patients) among those with femoral bone defects rated less than 3A according to the Paprosky classification. The discrepancy in these rates can be attributed to insufficient debridement of the osteolytic proximal femur and the retention of devitalized bone with biofilm residues. The authors avoided the use of antibiotic-laden cement spacers in cases with complex and severe proximal femur bone defects due to high mechanical complications, including dislocation, periprosthetic fractures, and spacer fractures.

draft: ### Intravenous Nitrate Effects on Myocardial Oxygen Usage and Efficiency #### Hemodynamic Effects in Fluid Overloaded Heart Failure Despite the beneficial hemodynamic effects of intravenous nitrate in patients with fluid overloaded heart failure, studies in healthy, euvolemic humans have shown unusual results. These studies indicate that intravenous nitrate increases myocardial oxygen usage, even when cardiac workload remains unchanged or decreases. This observation implies that more ATP is being utilized to sustain the same or reduced cardiac work, suggesting a decrease in cardiac efficiency. #### ATP Usage and Efficiency The increased ATP usage to maintain the same or reduced cardiac workload implies that more ATP is being generated for the same amount of work. This reduction in cardiac efficiency suggests that the heart is working harder to meet its increased oxygen demand, even though the workload on the heart itself might be stable or decreasing. #### Mitochondrial ATP Production and Mechanism Further investigation into the mechanism behind these effects reveals that nitric oxide (NO) generated by intravenous nitrate inhibits complex IV (also known as the cytochrome c oxidase) of the electron transport chain. This inhibition of complex IV leads to a reduction in ATP production through oxidative phosphorylation. Consequently, the heart is required to use more ATP to maintain its normal function, even though the workload has decreased. #### Interaction with Preload and Frank-Starling Mechanism Preload, or ventricular stretch, plays a crucial role in the normal operation of the Frank-Starling relationship. When preload is reduced due to intravenous nitrate, it compromises the optimal stretch necessary for the Frank-Starling relationship. This reduction in preload could potentially further reduce cardiac efficiency, especially if the patient was initially in a euvolemic state (i.e., a state of normal fluid volume). #### Implications for Human Studies While these effects have been observed in animal models, their impact on humans has not been thoroughly investigated. However, understanding the mechanisms in humans would provide valuable insights into the true effects of intravenous nitrate, particularly in euvolemic patients who might be more sensitive to the preload reduction caused by nitrate. ### Conclusion In summary, intravenous nitrate, despite its beneficial hemodynamic effects in fluid overloaded heart failure, paradoxically increases myocardial oxygen usage and reduces cardiac efficiency. This is due to the inhibition of oxidative phosphorylation by nitric oxide, which increases ATP usage without a corresponding increase in workload. The

In addition to this, it is reported in animal models that GTN causes nitric oxide-induced inhibition of complex IV of the electron transport chain, resulting in inhibition of mitochondrial ATP production by oxidative phosphorylation . draft: Nontuberculous mycobacteria (NTM) are ubiquitous organisms that are usually not associated with infection in individuals with a healthy immune system. They primarily affect the lungs and the lymph nodes, with the cervical region being the most frequently involved. Musculoskeletal involvement by NTM infection is rare, but when it does occur, the most common sites of involvement are the hands and wrists. Diagnosis of NTM infections can be challenging, leading to frequent misdiagnosis. These infections are often mistaken for bacterial or inflammatory tenosynovitis, which can result in inappropriate and ineffective treatments. This can lead to delayed diagnosis and prolonged treatment regimens. We report a case of NTM tenosynovitis affecting the hand, which was initially misdiagnosed as inflammatory tenosynovitis. Consequently, the patient was treated with multiple anti-inflammatory and immunosuppressant medications without experiencing any improvement.
human: Nontuberculous mycobacteria (NTM) are ubiquitous organisms that rarely cause infection in immunocompetent individuals. The primary site of involvement is the lungs, followed by lymph nodes (primarily cervical), and skin. Musculoskeletal involvement by NTM infection is rare and the most commonly reported sites are the hands and wrists. These infections are difficult to diagnose and are often misdiagnosed as bacterial or inflammatory tenosynovitis which often results in delayed or unwarranted treatments. We report a case of NTM tenosynovitis of the hand which was misdiagnosed as inflammatory tenosynovitis and as such was treated with multiple anti-inflammatory and immunosuppressant medications without improvement.

draft: Deborah Lupton posits that in the medical encounter, both physicians and patients collaborate to achieve mutual benefits. To improve the patient's health, both must manage the uncertainties inherent in any medical situation. These uncertainties shape their interaction, preventing a straightforward explanation based on dominance or exploitation. Patients are often more focused on the aspects of care that they believe will most benefit them, particularly the medical component. Conversely, physicians, despite possessing scientific knowledge, are also acutely aware of the uncertainties within the medical field. This awareness influences their interaction and necessitates a collaborative approach between both parties. Therefore, physicians emphasize the humaneness aspect to facilitate the interaction.
human: Deborah Lupton argues that in the medical encounter, physicians and patients work together to produce results that benefit them both. To improve the patient’s health, they must cope together with the uncertainty that characterizes any medical encounter. The uncertainty experienced by both patient and physician partly shapes their interaction, and this cannot be reduced to a simple explanation in terms of domination or exploitation. Thus, patients might be more interested in what they perceive will most benefit them (the medical component). In contrast, even physicians who feel they possess accurate scientific knowledge are aware of the uncertainties inherent in the medical professions, perhaps even more so than the patient. This awareness shapes the interaction, demanding collaboration between doctor and patient. Thus, physicians emphasize the aspect of humaneness, in order to improve the interaction.

draft: This study acknowledges several limitations. Primarily, as a cross-sectional study, it is challenging to conclusively establish the causal and temporal relationships between household type, energy intake, and physical activity (PA) level. Additionally, approximately 9.2% of the households in this study consist of single-person households. However, in Korea, this proportion stands at 30.2%. Consequently, there is a need to collect more data on single-person households in the future. Another limitation is the inadequate correction of socioeconomic factors such as financial status, education level, and marital status, as compared to studies examining the effects of income and education level on health-related behaviors. Despite these limitations, the findings might enhance the reliability of the results and could be generalized to a national trend based on data from the Korea National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (KNHANES). Furthermore, the study's limitations include a lack of detailed information on energy intake, such as eating habits and behaviors, and micronutrient data. Therefore, future research is needed to analyze detailed data on energy intake between single and multi-person households. Importantly, this study holds significance in that it is the first to examine physical activity (PA) level and energy intake according to household type and the presence of metabolic syndrome (MetS) in middle-aged men, unlike studies that focused on elderly and female subjects.

Approximately 14% to 24% of women who had high-grade cervical lesions identified through colposcopy biopsies had lower-grade lesions identified during LEEP procedures. A study also found that when the overestimation rate for high-grade lesions was 16.3%, CIN 2 from the biopsy was the only statistically significant risk factor for CIN 1 or less in LEEP specimens. draft: In 2012, the International Union for Conservation of Nature (IUCN) assessed both Coquerel's giant mouse lemur and the northern giant mouse lemur as endangered, following previous listings as vulnerable. Both species are currently experiencing a decline in population due primarily to habitat destruction, driven by slash-and-burn agriculture and charcoal production. Additionally, they are hunted for bushmeat. A population report published by the World Wildlife Fund (WWF) in 2010 indicated that both species were found outside the boundaries of the protected area PK32-Ranobe. This area was granted temporary protection status in December 2008 and is co-managed by the WWF. However, its forests were not included in the protected area due to existing concessions for mining activities. Both lemurs were initially protected in 1969 when they were categorized under Malagasy law as Class A under the African Convention on the Conservation of Nature and Natural Resources. This regulation prohibited hunting and capture without authorization, granted only for scientific or national purposes. In 1973, they were also protected under CITES Appendix I, a regulation that strictly controls their trade and prohibits commercial activities. While enforcement remains inconsistent, giant mouse lemurs are also protected under Malagasy law. These lemurs are rarely kept in captivity, yet they breed easily. In 1989, the Duke Lemur Center held more than seventy percent of the captive population (45 of 62 individuals). At this time, the Duke Lemur Center was coordinating a captive breeding program for Coquerel's giant mouse lemur, with all individuals at American facilities originating from six animals imported from the Ambanja region in 1982. As of 2009, the International Species Information System (ISIS) registered only six remaining individuals in the United States and Europe, all reclassified as northern giant mouse lemurs and considered a non-breeding population. By 2015, only a single female was recorded. These findings highlight the ongoing threats facing both Coquerel's giant mouse lemur and the northern giant mouse lemur, emphasizing the need for continued conservation efforts.

draft: Goodman Beaver is a fictional character who originates from comics by American cartoonist Harvey Kurtzman. Goodman Beaver is an innocent and optimistic character akin to the protagonist in Voltaire's "Candide," often oblivious to the moral decay and decadence surrounding him. His stories served as vehicles for social satire and pop culture parody. Kurtzman created Goodman Beaver's initial appearance alone, but after that, his stories were co-written by Kurtzman and drawn by Will Elder. Goodman Beaver first appeared in a story within Harvey Kurtzman's "Jungle Book" in 1959, and his most famous stories were those created in collaboration by Kurtzman and Elder between 1961 and 1962 for the "Help!" magazine, edited by Kurtzman himself. These stories reflect Kurtzman's signature satirical style from his work on "Mad" in the 1950s, although they also featured more pointed, adult-oriented satire. The artwork, notably by Will Elder, was more refined and detailed, filled with visual gags. One of the most famous of Goodman Beaver's stories is "Goodman Goes Playboy" from 1962. This story parodies Hugh Hefner's hedonistic lifestyle through the lens of Archie comics characters, and Hefner threatened legal action. The case was settled out of court, with the copyright for the story eventually transferred to Archie Comics. Hefner found the strip amusing despite its target. Kurtzman and Elder later developed a female version of Goodman Beaver for Playboy magazine, titled "Little Annie Fanny," which ran from 1962 to 1988.

draft: ### Impact of the COVID-19 Pandemic on Cancer Care In 2020, the global community faced significant challenges due to the spread of the COVID-19 pandemic. While the situation showed some signs of improvement by 2021, the end of this health crisis remains uncertain. The primary focus of healthcare systems has been on preventing contamination and transmission of the virus, with a significant emphasis on the treatment of patients infected with the virus. #### Impact on Cancer Care 1. **Healthcare Focus**: The health system's primary goal has been to protect against the spread of the virus. This has led to a prioritization of patients infected with the virus over those suffering from chronic diseases like cancer. 2. **Decrease in Cancer Treatment**: The global decrease in cancer treatment has been significant. While the exact reasons for this decrease are not fully understood, it is clear that the pandemic has impacted the availability and accessibility of cancer treatments. 3. **Impact on Cancer Services**: The pandemic has also led to a reduction in cancer diagnosis, screening, and treatment. This includes various forms of cancer care such as chemotherapy, radiation therapy, and surgery, as well as palliative care for patients with advanced or terminal cancer. #### Research Insights Studies have shown that the delay in cancer treatment can have severe consequences. A delay of approximately two months in cancer treatment is associated with a loss of life expectancy ranging from zero to seven years. This underscores the critical importance of maintaining timely access to cancer care during such times of crisis. ### Summary The year 2020 highlighted the significant challenges posed by the COVID-19 pandemic, particularly in the context of cancer care. The focus on protecting against the spread of the virus has led to a decrease in cancer treatment and a reduction in cancer services. Research indicates that even a slight delay in cancer treatment can result in substantial losses in patient life expectancy. As a result, it is crucial to ensure continued access to cancer care and support during health crises like the pandemic.

Second, the sample was exclusively comprised of prostitutes from Tabriz city, thereby limiting the study's generalizability to other cities and communities. Studies should be conducted in prisons and in other cities, particularly among community groups, such as adolescents, to prevent high-risk behaviors. draft: To develop a surrogate for microvascular function that relies on measurement-independent parameters such as absolute flow and pressures, and is not influenced by epicardial resistance, autoregulation principles, or myocardial mass, the concept of microvascular resistance reserve (MRR) was proposed by De Bruyne et al. as a novel index of microcirculatory function. Similar to the fractional flow reserve (FFR) concept, the MRR is defined as the ratio of resting to hyperemic microvascular resistances, providing a quantitative assessment of potential microvascular resistance reduction in response to a hyperemic stimulus. Generally, the MRR is expressed as the ratio of capillary flow reserve (CFR) to FFR, with driving pressures factored into the correction. However, the specific cut-off values for the MRR and its clinical and prognostic significance compared to other indexes of microvascular function are yet to be firmly established.
human: In order to outline a surrogate of microvascular function that is based on the operator-independent measurements of the absolute flow and pressures, as well as one that is unrelated to the epicardial resistance, the autoregulation principle, and the myocardial mass and, therefore, that is specific to coronary microcirculation, the microvascular resistance reserve (MRR) was proposed by De Bruyne et al. as a novel index of the microcirculatory function. In an analogy to the FFR concept, the MRR has been described as the ratio between the resting and hyperemic microvascular resistances, theoretically depicting a quantitative assessment of the extent of the potential microvascular resistance decrease resulting from a hyperemic stimulus. In its general form, the MRR can be expressed as the ratio of the CFR to the FFR, corrected for the driving pressures. However, the MRR cut-off values, as well as the clinical and prognostic relevance of the MRR compared to the other existing indexes of microvascular function, are not yet currently established.

draft: ### Obesity and Its Associated Conditions Obesity is a growing health issue globally and is linked with insulin resistance and type 2 diabetes. This condition arises from an imbalance between lipid storage and oxidation in the liver. Stearoyl-CoA desaturase (SCD) is a rate-limiting enzyme that catalyzes the synthesis of monounsaturated fatty acids and plays a significant role in body adiposity. An impairment in SCD1 function helps mice avoid obesity. Additionally, reducing SCD1 expression is essential for the metabolic actions of leptin in the liver. ### Key Points and Functions of SCD 1. **Role of SCD in Fatty Acid Synthesis**: - SCD is a rate-limiting enzyme in the biosynthesis of monounsaturated fatty acids. - It catalyzes the conversion of stearoyl-CoA to monounsaturated fatty acids such as oleic acid. 2. **Implication of SCD in Obesity**: - An imbalance between lipid storage and oxidation in the liver is crucial for the development of obesity. - SCD1, the enzyme that catalyzes this process, is central to body adiposity. 3. **Effect of SCD1 Impairment**: - Loss of SCD1 function prevents mice from becoming obese. - This indicates that SCD1 plays a significant role in adiposity. 4. **Connection with Leptin**: - SCD1 downregulation is an essential component of the metabolic actions of leptin in the liver. - This highlights the importance of SCD1 in the regulation of adiposity through leptin action. ### Summary Obesity, linked with insulin resistance and type 2 diabetes, involves an imbalance in lipid storage and oxidation in the liver. Stearoyl-CoA desaturase (SCD) serves as a key enzyme in the synthesis of monounsaturated fatty acids and is crucial in body adiposity. The impairment of SCD1 function prevents obesity in mice. Furthermore, SCD1 regulation is essential for the liver's leptin-mediated metabolic actions, emphasizing its importance in adiposity.

draft: Advancements in renewable energy generation, encompassing solar, wind, and geothermal systems, have spurred improvements in large-scale energy storage systems (ESS) for more efficient use. Lithium-ion batteries (LIBs), noted for their high energy density, have been a reliable option but are constrained by the finite reserves of lithium and rising costs. This limitation necessitates the development of more cost-effective and sustainable systems. Rechargeable sodium-ion batteries (SIBs) are emerging as the most promising next-generation battery systems due to the earth-abundant sodium resources. However, SIBs face significant challenges, particularly sluggish ion mobility and structural degradation during sodium ion insertion and removal. To overcome these issues and ensure reliability and sustainability, it is crucial to identify suitable cathode materials. Among these, layer-structured transition metal oxides (NaxTMO2) and poly-anion-based phosphate materials (such as sodium vanadium phosphate (Na3V2(PO4)3, NVP)) are attracting attention for their superior electrochemical performance.
human: Rapid advancements in renewable energy generation, including solar, wind, and geothermal systems, have encouraged the improvements in large-scale energy storage systems (ESS) for their efficient utilization. Lithium ion batteries (LIBs) have been considered as one of the most reliable ESS due to their high energy density. However, the growing concern about the limited reserve of lithium resources and an increase in price restricts the use of LIBs in the large-scale ESS, because they need inexpensive and efficient systems to have reliability and sustainability. Rechargeable sodium ion batteries (SIBs) have recently been regarded as the most promising candidates as next-generation rechargeable battery systems by virtue of the earth-abundant distribution of sodium resources. However, the electrochemical properties of SIBs have exhibited several drawbacks that are mainly originated from sluggish ion mobility and severe structural degradation during the insertion/de-insertion of sodium ions because of the larger ionic radius of sodium ions compared with that of lithium ions. Therefore, it is a top priority to find suitable host materials for SIBs with reliable electrochemical properties. Among various cathode materials including layer-structured transition metal oxide (NaxTMO2) and transition metal hexacyanoferrate, poly-anion type phosphate-based materials such as sodium vanadium phosphate (Na3V2(PO4)3, NVP) have attracted attention due to their reliable electrochemical properties.

draft: Segnosaurus stood out among therizinosaurs due to its unique dentary structure, where the hindmost part was toothless while the front two-thirds housed the teeth. Specifically, Segnosaurus had 24 alveoli in the dentary, similar to those of Jianchangosaurus but differing from the nearly fully toothed dentaries of Erlikosaurus, which possessed 35 alveoli. The tooth row of Segnosaurus was inset and separated by a shelf that was present on the outer side, a feature common to all derived therizinosaurs. However, this shelf was confined to the rear portion of the dentary, and the raised rim that demarcated it was not as pronounced as in Erlikosaurus. A notable feature of Segnosaurus was the low ridge positioned between the fifth and fourteenth alveoli, dividing the dentary into two nearly equal sections. This ridge was flanked above by a row of foramina, consistent with those found in Jianchangosaurus and Alxasaurus. In contrast, in Erlikosaurus, this row was placed directly alongside the ridge and on the side of the dentary. The Meckelian groove, located on the inner side of the mandible, was positioned further down than in Erlikosaurus and maintained a consistent depth until the thirteenth tooth position. Beyond this point, the groove widened. The lower jaw elements, including the splenial, surangular, angular, and prearticular bones, were notably different from those of other therizinosaurs, being gracile and linear, contributing to the distal part of the hemimandible being elongated and almost rectangular. The surangular bone was long and sword-shaped, while the angular bone had a wing-like shape. The prearticular bone was narrow and curved, and the splenial bone was thin and triangular in outline. The external mandibular fenestra, an opening on the outer side of the mandible, was larger than in Erlikosaurus because the surangular was shallow throughout its length.
human: Segnosaurus was distinct among therizinosaurs in that the hindmost part of the dentary was toothless. The teeth were restricted to the front two-thirds of the dentary, which bore 24 alveoli (tooth sockets) in a manner similar to Jianchangosaurus but different from Erlikosaurus, in which nearly the entire dentary was toothed, bearing 31 alveoli. The tooth row of Segnosaurus was inset and demarcated by a shelf on the outer side as it was in all derived (or "advanced") therizinosaurs. Unlike in other related taxa, the shelf was restricted to the hind part of the dentary and the raised rim that defined it was not as pronounced. Segnosaurus was unique in having a low ridge rising between the fifth and fourteenth alveoli that divided the dentary into two almost-equally sized front and hind parts. Just above this ridge, the dentary was pierced by a row of foramina as in Jianchangosaurus and Alxasaurus, which became less regular by the region around the mandibular symphysis, where the two halves of the mandible met at the front. This row was instead directly in line with and on the side of the ridge in Erlikosaurus. The Meckelian groove that ran along the inner side of the mandible, was placed further down than in Erlikosaurus and had a consistent depth until the thirteenth tooth position, whereafter it widened. The lower jaw elements behind the dentary (the splenial, surangular, angular, and prearticular bones) were distinct from those of other therizinosaurs, being gracile and linear, and contributing to the hind part of the hemimandible being elongate and almost rectangular. The surangular was long and sword-shaped, the angular was wing-like in shape, the prearticular was narrow and curved, and the splenial was thin and triangular in outline. The external mandibular fenestra, an opening at the outer side of the mandible, was larger than that of Erlikosaurus because the surangular was shallow from top to bottom.

draft: The physician traits were categorized into two groups—technical and professional skills versus non-technical interpersonal skills and humaneness—by researchers (KD, ND, and YGB) through a grounded theory approach. Grounded theory aims to uncover or develop theory from data that are systematically collected and analyzed. Initially, emerging codes are shared among the researchers and a face-to-face meeting is held to organize the list of codes. Once the researchers agree on these codes, the data are further analyzed until no new codes or categories emerge. Following this, a list of attributes was distributed to 16 experts from various fields including medicine, nursing, psychology, and sociology. Each expert was asked to categorize each attribute as either a technical/professional skill or a non-technical interpersonal or humaneness skill. If there was disagreement, further discussions were conducted via conference calls until complete consensus was achieved.
human: The physician traits were coded into the two categories (technical and professional skills vs. non-technical interpersonal skills and humaneness) by researchers (KD, ND, and YGB) using a grounded theory approach. Grounded theory sets out to discover or construct theory from data, systematically obtained and analyzed using comparative analysis. The emerging codes are circulated among researchers and the list of codes is sorted in a face-to-face meeting. Once the researchers agree on the developed codes (to ensure fidelity) the data are further analyzed until conceptual saturation is reached, that is, no new codes or categories are generated. After this phase, the list of attributes was distributed to 16 experts from medicine, nursing, psychology, and sociology, who were asked to indicate whether they thought each attribute belonged to the category of technical/professional skills or non-technical interpersonal and humaneness skills. When there was disagreement, the data were further discussed in conference calls until complete consensus was reached.

They provide the framework for designing experiments aimed at testing these theories. Theories are entertained until they have been subjected to various attempts to disprove them. Despite the inability to definitively prove the truth of a theory, the value of scientific theories lies in their ability to explain phenomena and reliably predict relationships among variables, particularly causal relationships. These relationships have the power to significantly impact our environments and ourselves for the better. The process of scientific discovery does not offer a definitive answer on what constitutes "better." Such judgments are subjective and influenced by societal norms. human: How do we move from our reliance on serendipity to scientific discovery through theory? Theories serve as instruments of action by providing the framework for designing experiments aimed to challenge their assertions. We entertain theories as long as attempts to falsify them have failed; however, multiple theories can often explain the same experimental results. Although it may not be possible to ascertain the “truth” of any theory, the value in our theories lies in their explanatory power and ability to reliably predict relationships among variables, especially causal relationships, which lend the power to change our environments and ourselves for the better. Science offers no help in deciding what is better, which must be determined subjectively, influenced by societal norms, but a consensus can often be reached. The determination that cigarette smoking causes lung cancer, among other health problems, has led to successful campaigns to reduce cigarette smoking and its associated health problems.

draft: The passage discusses ongoing confusion and debate regarding the use of Critical Care Transport (CCT) teams for patient transfers. It clarifies that CCT is typically reserved for high-acuity patients being transferred between Intensive Care Units (ICUs) and is conducted by specialist CCT teams. Internationally, CCT is associated with specific criteria, including the need for CCT-related qualifications. However, in South Africa (SA), there are currently no specific criteria or postgraduate qualifications to capacitate local Emergency Care Teams (ECs) for conducting CCTs. Participants indicated that their undergraduate training primarily focused on managing routine primary response calls and did not adequately prepare them for performing CCTs upon graduation. To summarize, the key points are: 1. International practice involves CCT for high-acuity patients and is performed by specialist teams. 2. SA lacks specific criteria or postgraduate qualifications for ECs to conduct CCTs. 3. Undergraduate training in SA does not adequately prepare ECs for CCTs.

In SA, there are currently no set criteria or postgraduate qualifications focusing on capacitating local EC providers to conduct CCTs. draft: Autophagy is a vital mechanism for maintaining cellular balance and energy levels. It occurs through at least three distinct forms: macroautophagy, microautophagy, and chaperone-mediated autophagy. Macroautophagy, the primary autophagic pathway, involves the formation of autophagosomes that collect cellular material, which then fuses with lysosomes for the breakdown of the material. Conversely, in microautophagy, lysosomes directly engulf cytoplasmic cargo and process it. Chaperone-mediated autophagy, a unique feature of mammalian cells, involves a specific recognition process. This begins with a cargo recognition complex composed of heat shock protein 70 (Hsp70) in the cytosol and a cargo translation complex, lysosomal-associated membrane protein type 2A (Lamp2A), at the lysosome membrane. Hsp70 binds to a specific sequence on the substrate protein, and the complex is then directed to Lamp2A on the lysosome membrane. Substrate proteins are then directed to the lysosomal lumen, where they are degraded through a channel formed by Lamp2A.
human: Autophagy plays an important role in maintaining cellular homeostasis and energy levels. There are at least three forms of autophagy that depend on the cargo delivery system to the lysosome: macroautophagy, microautophagy, and chaperone-mediated autophagy . Macroautophagy, which is the primary autophagic pathway, refers to the formation of autophagosomes to collect cellular material, which subsequently fuses with lysosomes to break down the material. In contrast, in microautophagy, lysosomes directly engulf cytoplasmic cargo and degrade the material. Chaperone-mediated autophagy, which is unique to mammalian cells, involves a cargo recognition complex in the cytosol (heat shock protein 70 chaperone, Hsp70) and a cargo translation complex at the lysosome (lysosomal-associated membrane protein type 2A, Lamp2A). Hsp70 recognizes and attaches to a specific motif sequence in substrate proteins, and then the complex is delivered to Lamp2A in the lysosome membrane. The substrate protein is translocated to the lysosomal lumen for degradation by a lysosomal channel formed by Lamp2A.

draft: Cross-validation was employed to assess the initial performance of the algorithm. Our cross-validation approach utilized a 'leave one user out' strategy: our training database consisted of N users, each with one or more measurements. The 'leave one user out' method was repeated N times, with one iteration for each user. In each iteration, all measurements from a specific user were utilized for testing, while the data from the remaining N-1 users were used to optimize the algorithm's parameters. Subsequently, scores for all measurements were computed based on the algorithm trained on data that did not include any measurements from the tested user. The overall method's sensitivity and specificity were calculated at every possible classification threshold and visualized via the receiver-operator characteristics (ROC) curve. Finally, the optimal classification threshold was determined at the point where the area under the ROC curve (AUC) was maximized, balancing sensitivity and specificity equally. Posteriorly, positive and negative predictive values (PPV and NPV) were estimated—the first based on the prevalence of atrial fibrillation (AF) within the studied sample and the second based on an expected AF prevalence of 10% in individuals aged 65 years and older. Positive likelihood ratios (PLR) and negative likelihood ratios (NLR) were also calculated. The datasets underlying this research can be shared upon reasonable request to the corresponding author.
human: Cross-validation was used to estimate the preliminary accuracy of the algorithm. Our implementation of cross-validation was based on the ‘leave one user out’ approach: we assume our training database contains N users with one or multiple measurements each; the ‘leave one user out’ process is repeated N times, with one iteration per every user; at each iteration, all measurements from a specific user are to be used for testing, while the data from the rest of N − 1 users is used to optimize (train) the algorithm’s parameters. Eventually, the scores for all measurements are computed based on an algorithm trained on data that did not contain a single measurement of a tested user per each iteration. The overall method sensitivity and specify were computed at all possible classification thresholds and were visualized via the receiver-operator characteristics curve. Ultimately. the recommended classification threshold was selected at the point of maximal balanced accuracy ([sensitivity + specificity]/2). Lastly, positive and negative predictive values (PPV and NPV) were also estimated—once on the prevalence of AF within the studied sample set, and second based on an expected AF prevalence of 10% in the population aged ≥65 years. Positive likelihood ratio (PLR) and negative likelihood ratio (NLR) were also estimated. The data underlying this article will be shared on reasonable request to the corresponding author.

draft: To investigate the involvement of microRNAs in renal ischemic injury (IRI), we screened several candidate microRNAs that might be associated with the renal IRI process, including miR-329, miR-144, miR-25-3p, miR-290, and miR-205. We conducted qRT-PCR assays to quantify the levels of these five microRNAs in normal and IRI kidney tissues. The results indicated that the expression level of miR-144 in renal IRI tissues was higher compared to the normal level, while the expression level of miR-25-3p was significantly reduced, and the changes in the other three microRNAs were not statistically significant. To further validate these findings, we performed in vitro experiments using NRK-52E cells, which were subjected to hypoxia-reperfusion (H/R) treatment. Compared to the control group, the expression level of miR-144 was upregulated in NRK-52E cells exposed to H/R treatment, while the expression level of miR-25-3p was significantly decreased.

The results showed that the expression level of miR-144 in renal IRI was increased compared to the normal level, while the expression level of miR-25-3p was significantly downregulated and the changes in the other three microRNAs were statistically insignificant . In addition, we verified this result via in vitro experiments. Compared with the control group, the expression level of miR-144 was upregulated in NRK-52E cells subjected to the H/R treatment, while the expression level of miR-25-3p was significantly downregulated .

The results show that 28% of patients experienced PTSD, 31% had depression, 20% displayed obsessive-compulsive symptoms, and 40% experienced insomnia. Of those affected, 56% scored pathologically on at least one of these symptoms. These figures were notably more prevalent among females and individuals with a history of psychiatric illness, even when baseline inflammatory parameters were similar. Anxiety and depression were found to correlate with these outcomes.

draft: Lipids play a crucial role in maintaining immune homeostasis and have significant potential for treating various disorders. Their full capacity as standalone immunomodulators or adjuvants is just beginning to be realized. This review focuses on three classes of lipids: two naturally occurring fatty acids (PUFAs and SCFAs), and adjuvant lipids designed to modulate the immune system. These lipids can promote immune activation or suppression within specific tissues and at precise times. This effect stems from the unique structure of lipids, which enables them to partition and selectively concentrate in various microenvironments. We then summarize the mechanisms, effects, and their roles in disease. While naturally occurring lipids can induce either a pro-inflammatory or anti-inflammatory immune response, adjuvant lipids are specifically engineered to promote immune activation.
human: Lipids are important mediators of immune homeostasis and may be leveraged for treating a range of disorders. Their full potential as stand‐alone immunomodulators or adjuvants is only now beginning to be realized. In this review, we focused on three classes of lipids—two naturally occurring FAs: PUFAs and SCFAs, and adjuvant lipids for immune modulation, in which they might promote the activation or suppression of immune cell subsets in a spatially and temporally controlled manner. This effect is derived from the inherent structure of lipids, which is suited to partition and selectively accumulate in tissue microenvironments. We then summarized the mechanism, effect, and their role in disease. While the naturally occurring lipids can result in a pro‐ or anti‐inflammatory immune response, adjuvant lipids are designed to promote immune activation.

Hospitals will require less space, as most medical care will be provided outside the hospital. Consequently, there will be an increase in waiting areas, reflecting the trend of more care being administered in various settings rather than exclusively within hospitals. Therefore, hospital design must adapt to these evolving trends, new care models, and the needs and preferences of patients. ### Healthcare Practices and Regulations: Geographical Perspectives #### Belarus In Belarus, infrastructure planning is primarily based on demographic needs. This approach ensures that healthcare facilities are well-suited for the population they serve. #### Ukraine Ukraine has stringent regulations for medical equipment. All medical equipment must be subject to mandatory local registration to ensure safety and quality. #### Tajikistan The country has a strategic plan in place. Specifically, the number of hospitals in Ryun province, towns, and villages is expected to decrease by 30%. However, no representatives from the Luciolinae subfamily have been detected in the stomach contents of R. chiwen. The distinction between lampyrine and lucioline fireflies, according to the limited literature, appears to be based on the presence of biogenic detergents (BDs). It is therefore hypothesized that R. chiwen selectively consumes fireflies that possess BDs, known as "BD fireflies," and avoids those without, referred to as "non-BD fireflies." Typically, snakes use chemical cues to distinguish edible from non-edible prey. Consequently, it is assumed that R. chiwen employs a chemical method to differentiate between BD and non-BD fireflies, suggesting that BDs serve as chemical cues to identify toxic prey. draft: In September 1775, during the early stages of the American Revolutionary War, Colonel Benedict Arnold led a force of 1,105 Continental Army troops in an expedition from Cambridge, Province of Massachusetts Bay, towards Quebec City. This campaign was part of a coordinated two-pronged assault on the British Province of Quebec, and it traversed the wilderness that is now Maine. The second prong of the campaign came from Lake Champlain, led by Richard Montgomery. The expedition faced immediate complications as soon as it departed the final colonial outposts in Maine. The portages along the Kennebec River proved to be strenuous, with boats frequently leaking, causing significant issues with gunpowder and food supplies. More than one-third of the troops returned before reaching the high ground between the Kennebec and Chaudière rivers. The area between these heights was a swampy labyrinth of lakes and streams, and the journey to the Saint Lawrence River was further complicated by inclement weather and inaccurate maps. Many of the troops had little experience navigating rapids, which led to the destruction of additional boats and supplies on their descent. By the time Arnold reached the settlements above the Saint Lawrence River in November, his forces had dwindled to 600 men, severely malnourished and having covered a distance of 350 miles (560 km), significantly longer than originally anticipated. On November 13 and 14, Arnold's forces crossed the Saint Lawrence with the assistance of local French-speaking inhabitants. They attempted to lay siege to Quebec City but were unsuccessful. They retreated to Point-aux-Trembles until Montgomery arrived to lead another unsuccessful assault on the city. Arnold was promoted to brigadier general for his efforts in leading the expedition. The route taken by Arnold through northern Maine has since been listed as the Arnold Trail to Quebec on the National Register of Historic Places, and several geographical features in the region bear names of expedition participants.

This further supports the role of SMAD4 in HNSCC tumorigenesis. #### Epithelial-Mesenchymal Transition (EMT) and TGF-β The SMAD4 gene plays a crucial role in EMT, where TGF-β functions as a transcriptional repressor of E-Cadherins, which are activated by the SMAD4 gene. E-Cadherins are essential for epithelial cell adhesion and proper tissue architecture. TGF-β, through this mechanism, prevents the epithelial-to-mesenchymal transition, thereby suppressing tumorigenesis. #### Genetic Mutations and Syndromes Germline mutations in the SMAD4 gene are linked to juvenile polyposis syndrome, a condition characterized by the presence of multiple polyps in the colon. Additionally, frequent deletions in the loci 18q, where the SMAD4 gene protein is located, and heterozygous loss of SMAD4 have been found to be associated with cancer development. Approximately 61.12% of oral squamous cell carcinoma cases have been observed to have a loss of SMAD4 protein. #### SMAD1 and SMAD2 Pathways Alterations in SMAD1 are linked to melorheostosis, an osteogenesis imperfecta-like disorder, and osteopoikilosis, a skin condition. These diseases are associated with protein metabolism and immune responses. Specifically, SMAD1 alterations are linked to the Th1 differentiation pathway. Studies have shown that alterations in SMAD2 and SMAD4 are associated with TGF-β-mediated invasion of epithelial cells. #### SMAD2 and SMAD4 in Pancreatic Cancer Smad2 overexpression in tumor-derived missense mutations has been found to promote TGF-β-mediated invasion of MDCK (Madin-Darby canine kidney) cells.
