draft: Mesklin is a fictional planet crafted by Hal Clement and featured prominently in his hard science fiction works, starting with his 1954 publication of "Mission of Gravity." Clement's essay, titled "Whirligig World," offers insight into the meticulous design he employed to create the planet, which, according to a 1953 object hypothesized to exist in the 61 Cygni system, may represent an extrasolar planet. The planet is notable for its unique properties resulting from a strong gravitational force in conjunction with its rapid rotation. This interaction gives rise to a gradient in perceived gravity, ranging from 3 g at the equator to a staggering 665 g at the poles. The world hosts a diverse array of life forms, including an intelligent centipede-like species known as the Mesklinites. Mesklin is regarded as a paradigmatic example of worldbuilding in hard science fiction, where the structure aligns with known scientific principles and facts. Despite being vastly different from Earth, the Mesklinites are often perceived as resembling humans in their behavior, even if their physical appearance differs. Mesklin itself frequently emerges as the primary focus of the narrative in "Mission of Gravity."
human: Mesklin is a fictional planet created by Hal Clement and used in a number of his hard science fiction stories, starting with Mission of Gravity (1954). Alongside the novel's original 1953 serialization in Astounding Science Fiction, Clement published an essay titled "Whirligig World" on how he designed the planet to have the properties he wanted. The idea came from an object that was at the time believed to exist in the 61 Cygni system, and which might represent an extrasolar planet. The planet is distinctive for the interaction of its strong gravity with the centrifugal force due to its fast rotation, giving it a gradient in the perceived force of gravity from 3 g on the equator to 665 g on the planet's poles. It is inhabited by native lifeforms, including an intelligent centipede-like species, the Mesklinites. Mesklin is considered a prototypical example of hard science fiction worldbuilding, an exotic milieu that nevertheless accords with known facts and laws of physics. While the planet itself is vastly dissimilar to Earth, its inhabitants are commonly regarded as noticeably humanlike in behavior, if not in appearance. Mesklin itself is sometimes viewed as the main character of Mission of Gravity.

draft: Captain Broke led a party of 20 men aboard Chesapeake, arriving at the ship's head. They encountered limited resistance from the crew, who had largely retreated below deck. The only significant combat occurred with the ship's contingent of marines. The British forces swiftly overcame the resistance; only nine men were injured out of the initial 44. During the engagement, Captain Broke sustained a severe head wound when struck with a sword while fighting on the forecastle. Shortly after, Shannon's crew hoisted their flag in surrender. The capture of Chesapeake transpired within just fifteen minutes, from the initial exchange of gunfire to the final flag hoist. Estimates regarding the number of casualties on Chesapeake vary widely. Captain Broke's post-battle report from July 6th states that 70 men were killed and 100 wounded. Other contemporary sources, however, place the death toll between 48 and 61, and the number of wounded ranges from 85 to 99. Discrepancies in the casualty figures could be attributed to the fact that some sailors succumbed to their wounds post-battle. Shannon's accounts of the engagement show fewer discrepancies, with 23 men killed and 56 wounded. Despite his injuries, Captain Broke ordered the ships repaired and set course for Halifax, Nova Scotia. During the journey, Captain Lawrence succumbed to his wounds and was laid to rest in Halifax with full military honors. The dead crewmen from Chesapeake were interred on Dead Man's Island in Nova Scotia. Captain Broke survived his wounds and was later elevated to the peerage as a baronet.

draft: Mitochondria are multifunctional organelles, and their abnormalities can disrupt multiple processes unrelated to oxidative phosphorylation (OXPHOS). These disruptions primarily affect protein import, proteostatic signaling, metabolic remodeling, toxic metabolite accumulation, apoptosis, phospholipid synthesis, calcium homeostasis, redox balance maintenance, iron-sulfur cluster/heme biosynthesis, inflammation, cell-non-autonomous signaling, and epigenetic regulation. Our recent studies have shown that various forms of mitochondrial damage, such as intra-mitochondrial protein misfolding and a reduction in protein quality control, can directly trigger cytosolic proteostatic stress and cell death. This phenomenon is referred to as mitochondrial precursor overaccumulation stress (mPOS). mPOS is characterized by reduced protein import and the toxic accumulation of unimported mitochondrial precursors/preproteins in the cytosol. Additionally, other studies have uncovered cellular responses to defects in the mitochondrial protein import machinery. In yeast, for example, mitochondrial protein import stress activates various cytosolic mechanisms, including the Unfolded Protein Response (UPRam) activated by the mistargeting of proteins, mitochondrial protein Translocation-Associated Degradation (mitoTAD), and mitochondrial Compromised Protein import Response (mitoCPR). These adaptive responses stimulate proteasomal degradation of unimported proteins and the removal of clogged preproteins from the mitochondrial surface. Cytosolic chaperone genes are also activated to counteract proteostatic stress in the cytosol. Furthermore, mitochondrial protein import stress can induce the nuclear and mitochondrial translocation of specific cellular factors to reprogram gene expression and restore cellular homeostasis. Despite these findings, the specific occurrence of mPOS in animals, how mammalian cells respond to mPOS in vivo, and the relationship between mPOS and anti-mPOS signaling affecting tissue-specific homeostasis and function, such as skeletal muscle, remain to be determined.
human: Mitochondria are multifunctional. Mitochondrial abnormalities have been shown to affect cell fitness and survival by disrupting many processes that are not directly related to oxidative phosphorylation (OXPHOS). These processes include, but are not limited to, protein import, proteostatic signaling, metabolic remodeling, toxic metabolite accumulation, apoptosis, phospholipid synthesis, calcium homeostasis, redox balance maintenance, iron-sulfur cluster/heme biosynthesis, inflammation, cell-non-autonomous signaling, and epigenetic regulation . Our recent studies demonstrated that various forms of mitochondrial damage, including intra-mitochondrial protein misfolding and reduced protein quality control, can directly trigger cytosolic proteostatic stress and cell death, a phenomenon named mitochondrial precursor overaccumulation stress (mPOS) . mPOS is characterized by reduced protein import and the toxic accumulation of unimported mitochondrial precursors/preproteins in the cytosol. Other studies uncovered cellular responses to defects in the mitochondrial protein import machinery. In yeast, mitochondrial protein import stress activates different cytosolic mechanisms including the Unfolded Protein Response activated by mistargeting of proteins (UPRam), mitochondrial protein Translocation-Associated Degradation (mitoTAD), and mitochondrial Compromised Protein import Response (mitoCPR). These adaptive responses stimulate proteasomal degradation of unimported proteins and the removal of clogged preproteins on the mitochondrial surface . Genes encoding cytosolic chaperones are also activated to counteract proteostatic stress in the cytosol . Furthermore, mitochondrial protein import stress also induces the nuclear and mitochondrial translocation of specific cellular factors to reprogram gene expression and restore cellular homeostasis . Currently, it is yet to be determined as to whether mPOS occurs in animals, how mammalian cells respond to mPOS in vivo, and whether mPOS and anti-mPOS signaling affect the homeostasis and function of specific tissues such as the skeletal muscle.

draft: The overall morphology of titanium gypsum (TG) is irregular and granular. EDS results indicate that titanium gypsum has significant signals for calcium (Ca), oxygen (O), sulfur (S), and fluorine (F). Specifically, the fluorine signal is notably more prominent than in pure gypsum (PG). This observation is consistent with X-ray fluorescence (XRF) results. After bioleaching, Rhodotorula (Rho) cells have attached to the surface grooves of TG, but no obvious colloidal materials have been detected, confirming that Rho cells' growth and secretion on TG have been inhibited. Previous studies have shown that under high stress, Rhodotorula cells resist harmful substances in their environment through division and reproduction. This may also impact the production of cell secretions. In TG with Rhodotorula (TG + Rho), the main elements remain calcium (Ca), oxygen (O), sulfur (S), and fluorine (F). Compared to TG without Rhodotorula (TG5-Rho), there is a significant increase in phosphorus (P) content. The positions of phosphorus (P), fluorine (F), and sulfur (S) in the figure are highly consistent, confirming that calcium phosphate fluoride (Ca5(PO4)3F) is the primary mineral formed. The presence of Rhodotorula in TG significantly increases the release of fluorine (F) from PG/TG and promotes the formation of stable phosphorus minerals containing F. This action is beneficial in reducing the direct harm of fluorine ions (F−) to the environment after PG/TG application.

draft: A diagnosis of acute psychosis was made, and the patient was subsequently administered 4 mg of lorazepam and 5 mg of haloperidol. The patient showed rapid improvement and ceased requiring antipsychotic treatment thereafter. Her mental state remained stable for four days. Upon the patient's readmission on the fifth day, a low dose of daily prednisone, 2.5 mg, was reintroduced. The patient immediately exhibited symptoms of agitation, anxiety, and insomnia once more. The low-dose prednisone was discontinued, and the patient's symptoms immediately subsided without the use of antipsychotic drugs. The patient had Sheehan's syndrome, which required hydrocortisone to replace the missing hormone. Re-administration of prednisolone with hydrocortisone led to an improvement in her mental state. A slow titration of prednisolone from 5.0 mg in the morning over six days, while gradually tapering off hydrocortisone, was performed. By the end of the case, the patient was on a daily dose of prednisone 7.5 mg, free of both psychotic symptoms and signs of adrenal insufficiency.
human: A diagnosis of acute psychosis was made, and she was started on lorazepam 4 mg and haloperidol 5 mg. The patient showed rapid improvement from psychosis and thereafter no longer required antipsychotic treatment. Her mental state remained stable for four days. On the fifth day of hospital readmission, a low dose of daily prednisone 2.5 mg was re-administered. The patient immediately showed symptoms of agitation, anxiety, and insomnia once again. The low-dose prednisolone was held, and the symptoms disappeared immediately the following day without the use of antipsychotic drugs. Hydrocortisone was administered in this patient as it directly replaces the much-needed missing hormone for Sheehan’s syndrome. Re-administration of prednisolone with the added hydrocortisone showed improvement to her mental state, and a slow titration of prednisolone to 5.0 mg in the morning over six days while tapering off of hydrocortisone occurred. At the conclusion of the case, the patient was on a daily dose of prednisone 7.5 mg without psychotic symptoms or signs of adrenal insufficiency.

draft: We have successfully produced a composite material featuring NVP particles homogeneously dispersed within a porous carbon matrix through a PVA-assisted sol-gel fabrication method. This porous NVP/C composite consists of NVP particles (with particle sizes ranging from ~30 to 100 nanometers) embedded uniformly within a porous and thin carbon network. The porous carbon matrix serves multiple critical roles: it acts as a barrier to prevent particle aggregation, facilitates sufficient electron conduction pathways to overcome NVP's inherently low electronic conductivity, and offers a larger surface area for interacting with an electrolyte solution. The distinctive electrochemical properties of the porous NVP/C composite are clearly demonstrated by its superior performance compared to the NVP/C composite, showing an excellent rate capability (a discharge capacity of 68 mAh g−1 at 50 C) and retaining approximately 99% of its initial discharge capacity even after 100 cycles at a rate of 1 C. Consequently, the polymer-assisted sol-gel processes for phosphate cathode materials offer a method for fabricating porous carbon networks and cathode particle composites that significantly promote efficient electron conduction and ion transfer.
human: We have successfully fabricated a composite, in which NVP particles were homogeneously dispersed in a porous carbon matrix by adopting a PVA-assisted sol-gel fabrication method. The Porous NVP/C composite contained NVP particles (~30–100 nm of particle size in diameter) that were uniformly embedded in a porous and thin carbon network. The porous carbon network played multiple roles in the composite: it acted as barrier to prevent particle aggregation, provided sufficient electron conduction pathways that enabled overcoming the inherently low electronic conductivity of NVP and also provided a larger surface area for contacting an electrolyte solution. The merits of the porous structure formation were well demonstrated by its outstanding electrochemical properties of the Porous NVP/C composite when compared with that of the NVP/C composite. The Porous NVP/C composite exhibited a superior rate capability (discharge capacity of 68 mAh g−1 at 50 C) and also maintained ~99% of its initial discharge capacity at 1 C even after 100 cycles. Therefore, the polymer-assisted sol-gel processes for phosphate cathode materials can provide a method for fabricating porous carbon networks and cathode particles composites that promote efficient electron conduction and ion transfer.

draft: Synthetic biology holds significant potential for various applications, yet companies actively involved in this field are underrepresented in many European countries and especially in Germany. Currently, only a few startups in Germany and across Europe use synthetic biology approaches to replace traditional chemical production with bio-based methods. The startup ecosystem in Germany, and Europe more broadly, faces significant challenges in terms of financing opportunities, business training, and regulatory support, particularly outside of therapeutic areas. This scarcity has resulted in a limited number of German startups focused on synthetic biology, whereas the US and the UK are home to numerous synthetic biology startups. For instance, in Germany, only 1.5% of the 6 billion euros invested in biotechnology startups in 2019 went into synthetic biology ventures. Funding support for their expansion phase is also lacking, making it particularly difficult for startups, especially in the life sciences sector, to thrive. In the US, investment in synthetic biology surged from approximately 4 billion dollars between 2016 and 2020, followed by China with around 200 million dollars, the UK with 160 million dollars, France with approximately 60 million dollars, and Switzerland with around 35 million dollars. In contrast, Germany received only 10 million dollars for biotechnology (which includes synthetic biology) investments. One of the major German industrial players in the life sciences sector, Bayer, has recognized the emerging human challenges and the transformative potential of the "Bio Revolution," including synthetic biology. Since 2015, the Leaps by Bayer program has invested over one billion dollars to address these challenges. Currently, the program supports 23 companies developing health products and 22 dedicated to agriculture. The majority of these supported companies are based in the US, with a few in Canada, Israel, and Europe. Only one German startup, which is developing an app for medical symptom assessment, has received support. One significant factor limiting the development of synthetic biology in Germany is the scarcity of infrastructure for technology transfer and appropriate funding for startups. Additionally, another critical issue is the focus on basic research by academic groups in Germany, rather than the practical applications of this research.

draft: The current understanding of noncoding RNAs linked to CRISPR systems indicates that they often form secondary structures. Rfam currently catalogues 64 families of direct repeats and one family of tracrRNAs. However, there is still significant diversity within crRNAs and tracrRNAs that existing models fail to capture. It is plausible that other essential noncoding RNAs, which have not yet been identified, are also involved in CRISPR-Cas systems. These RNAs, similar to their counterparts, may also adopt secondary structures. Furthermore, substantial diversity in the structures of crRNAs and tracrRNAs remains unidentified. Expanding our models will be beneficial for characterizing and identifying these structures within genomes. There is precedent for regulatory RNAs being embedded in coding regions of bacterial genomes. However, since most attention is directed towards intergenic regions, regulatory RNAs that overlap genes can often go unnoticed. This oversight is particularly relevant from a genetic engineering standpoint, as gene optimization might disrupt the structure and function of essential overlapping noncoding RNAs. Motivated by this consideration, we have developed methods to predict candidate structured RNAs and integrated coding regions into our analyses. Although comparative genomics approaches have not yet been widely applied to Cas operons and CRISPR systems at large scale, such approaches have proven useful in predicting candidate structured RNAs within microbial communities.
human: All of these noncoding RNAs associated with CRISPRs have been shown or predicted to form secondary structures. Currently, there are 64 families of direct repeats and one family of tracrRNAs in Rfam. More diversity exists within crRNAs and tracrRNAs that existing models do not capture. It is likely that other noncoding RNAs exist that play essential roles in CRISPR-Cas systems that have yet to be discovered, and these noncoding RNAs may also form secondary structures. Additionally, there likely exists substantial diversity in structures within crRNAs and tracrRNAs that have yet to be identified. Building additional models would be beneficial both to characterize the structures as well as better search for them in genomes. There is also precedence for regulatory RNAs being embedded in bacterial coding regions. Because most of the focus is on intergenic regions, regulatory RNAs that overlap genes tend to be overlooked. However, this is an important consideration from a genetic engineering perspective; perhaps upon codon optimization of a Cas gene, for example, the structure and function of an essential overlapping noncoding RNA is disrupted. This perspective motivated us to predict candidate structured RNAs and include coding regions in our analyses. draft: In his inaugural term (1851–1853), Kentucky's eighth district elected John C. Breckinridge to represent the state in the U.S. House of Representatives. This district, known as the "Ashland district," was typically won by the Whigs by margins of around 600 to 1,000 votes, having been represented by Whigs since 1828. No Democrat had served in the district since that period. During the campaign, Breckinridge faced Leslie Combs, a War of 1812 veteran and former state legislator. The two campaigned together, with Breckinridge's persuasive oratory contrasting sharply with Combs' straightforward approach. Despite carrying only three of the seven counties, Breckinridge's victory was bolstered by a decisive two-to-one margin in Owen County. He secured 54% of the vote and won the election with a narrow margin of 537 votes.

A Democrat had not represented it since 1828, and in the previous election no Democrat had sought the office. Breckinridge's opponent, Leslie Combs, was a popular War of 1812 veteran and former state legislator. As they campaigned together, Breckinridge's eloquence contrasted with Combs' plainspoken style. Holding that "free thought needed free trade", Breckinridge opposed Whig protective tariffs. He only favored federal funding of internal improvements "of a national character". Carrying only three of seven counties, but bolstered by a two-to-one margin in Owen County, Breckinridge garnered 54% of the vote, winning the election by a margin of 537.

The KNCSP data comprised demographic characteristics, a history of endoscopy, and medical history through questionnaires; endoscopic, biopsy, and comprehensive cancer screening results; and screening sites and providers. Screening results were considered positive if endoscopic results indicated possible gastric cancer, early gastric cancer, or advanced gastric cancer, or if biopsy results showed low-grade dysplasia, high-grade dysplasia, suspicious gastric cancer, or gastric cancer. Interval gastric cancer was identified when participants received a diagnosis code for gastric cancer (International Classification of Diseases, 10th revision, C16.xx) within a year of endoscopic screening, irrespective of screening results. Consequently, the detection period for interval cancer was defined as "within one year" of negative screening results. The KNCSP data included demographic characteristics, a brief history of endoscopy, and medical history using questionnaires; endoscopy, biopsy, and comprehensive cancer screening results; and screening sites and providers. We defined screening results as positive if endoscopic results were recorded as possible gastric cancer, early gastric cancer, or advanced gastric cancer, or if biopsy results were recorded as low-grade dysplasia, high-grade dysplasia, suspicious gastric cancer, or gastric cancer. We tracked and checked interval gastric cancer cases up to 31 December 2017 by linking individual medical records from the National Health Insurance Sharing Service-National Health Information Database (NHIS-NHID). We defined interval gastric cancer when participants received a diagnosis code for gastric cancer (International Classification of Diseases, 10th revision, C16.xx) within one year of endoscopy screening (negative screening results). Missed cancer is an important component of interval cancer that determines screening quality. Therefore, the observation period to detect interval cancer was defined as “within one year” of negative screening results. Interval cancer was found by additional examinations performed at different centers from the screening program for various reasons, including symptom development.

draft: ### Comparison of Limb Proportions Unlike galagos, which have legs significantly longer than their arms, slow lorises have limbs of nearly equal length. This is reflected in their intermembral index (ratio of arm to leg length), averaging around 89. This means that the forelimbs are slightly shorter than the hind limbs, similar to the slender lorises. ### Limb Length and Proportions Slow lorises have arms and legs that are relatively longer compared to their bodies. However, their extremities are more stout compared to the slender lorises. The limbs' specialized adaptations allow the slow lorises to grasp branches effectively. ### Specialized Limb Adaptations 1. **Muscular Arrangement in Hands and Feet:** The slow lorises have a unique muscle arrangement in their hands and feet that allows them to tightly grasp branches. Their thumb diverges at nearly 180° from the rest of the fingers. The hallux, or the big toe, is positioned at an angle between perpendicular and slightly backward. This allows for a strong grasp, enabling them to maintain their grip for extended periods. 2. **Thick and Powerful Thumbs:** The sturdy thumb of the slow lorises serves as a clamping mechanism. When the digits three, four, and five grasp the opposite side of a tree branch, their hands and feet appear like a pincer, providing a firm grip. 3. **Sturdy Extremities:** The thick and powerful extremities of the slow lorises help them maintain a strong grip for hours without losing sensation. This is due to the presence of a rete mirabile, a network of capillaries that ensures sustained sensory function. ### Similarities with Other Species Both slender and slow lorises have relatively short feet. Additionally, they share the same specialized claw on the second toe of each foot, a feature common among lemurs. ### Metabolic Characteristics Slow lorises have an unusually low basal metabolic rate, approximately 40% of the typical value for placental mammals of their size. This low metabolic rate is comparable to that of sloths. The cause of this low metabolic rate is believed to be related to the elimination of toxic compounds from their diet, particularly a high-calorie, year-round available diet. ### Dietary Adaptations Slow lorises consume a diet that is high in calories and year-round available. This diet includes Gluta bark, which can be toxic to humans. The low metabolic rate allows them to efficiently process this toxic bark, minimizing the risk of poisoning.
human: Unlike galagos, which have longer legs than arms, slow lorises have arms and legs of nearly equal length. Their intermembral index (ratio of arm to leg length) averages 89, indicating that their forelimbs are slightly shorter than their hind limbs. As with the slender lorises, their arms are slightly longer than their body, but the extremities of slow lorises are more stout. Slow lorises have a powerful grasp with both their hands and feet due to several specializations. They can tightly grasp branches with little effort because of a special muscular arrangement in their hands and feet, where the thumb diverges at nearly 180° from the rest of the fingers, while the hallux (big toe) ranges between being perpendicular and pointing slightly backwards. The toes have a large flexor muscle that originates on the lower end of the thigh bone, which helps to impart a strong grasping ability to the hind limbs. The second digit of the hand is short compared to the other digits, while on the foot, the fourth toe is the longest. The sturdy thumb helps to act like a clamp when digits three, four, and five grasp the opposite side of a tree branch. This gives their hands and feet a pincer-like appearance. The strong grip can be held for hours without losing sensation due to the presence of a rete mirabile (network of capillaries), a trait shared among all lorises. Both slender and slow lorises have relatively short feet. Like nearly all lemuriforms, they have a grooming claw on the second toe of each foot. Slow lorises have an unusually low basal metabolic rate, about 40% of the typical value for placental mammals of their size, comparable to that of sloths. Since they consume a relatively high-calorie diet that is available year-round, it has been proposed that this slow metabolism is due primarily to the need to eliminate toxic compounds from their food. For example, slow lorises can feed on Gluta bark, which may be fatal to humans.

draft: A comprehensive review of the local Care Coordination System (CCT) reveals its significant shortcomings and the need for substantial reform. The management of high-acuity patients in resource-constrained healthcare environments often results in suboptimal patient care, compassion fatigue, and strain on interprofessional relationships. While Care Coordination Teams (CCTs) are crucial for such environments, the lack of a contextually relevant definition and potential curriculum deficiencies in undergraduate Emergency Care (EC) programs negatively impact the experiences of EC providers who undertake CCTs. Recognizing Care Coordination as a specialized area is an essential first step towards addressing the frustrations and challenges faced by these providers. Unless the industry improves the experiences, frustrations, and lack of acknowledgment of those involved in CCT, a constant turnover of staff will occur. This is particularly problematic in an educational landscape where undergraduate EC programs inadequately prepare graduates to confidently undertake CCTs and where the required confidence and competencies are developed gradually through experience.

The anatomical features of the TMJ show variations among individuals and are influenced by multiple factors related to the shape and functional load of the bones. A strong association exists between the form and function of the mandible and condyle among patients with various types of malocclusion. ### Studies and Data Availability Several studies have evaluated the circularity of the condyle in both symptomatic and asymptomatic samples, comparing them in patients with normal occlusion and those with different types of malocclusion. Subsequently, orthodontists, prosthodontists, and oral surgeons are involved in the formulation of the treatment plan. The orthodontists play a crucial role in assessing the position of the condyle, which can be significant for two primary purposes: diagnosing TMJ dysfunctions and differentiating body positions of the mandible that affect the diagnosis and treatment. ### Evaluation of Condyle Morphology To explore this further, studies have been conducted to evaluate the morphology of the condyle in patients with Angle's Class I, Class II, and Class III malocclusions. draft: The Chesapeake was a 38-gun wooden-hulled, three-masted heavy frigate of the United States Navy, one of the original six frigates authorized by the Naval Act of 1794. Designed by Joshua Humphreys to serve as the young navy's capital ships, the Chesapeake was originally planned as a 44-gun vessel. Delays, material shortages, and budget constraints necessitated a reduction to 38 guns by builder Josiah Fox. Launched on December 2, 1799, from the Gosport Navy Yard, the Chesapeake began its service during the Quasi-War with France and continued into the First Barbary War. On June 22, 1807, the Chesapeake faced a confrontation with HMS Leopard of the Royal Navy, which fired upon the ship for refusing to allow British boarding for deserters. This event, the Chesapeake–Leopard affair, infuriated the American public and government, precipitating the War of 1812. As a consequence, the United States initiated the Embargo Act of 1807 against the United Kingdom. Early in the War of 1812, the Chesapeake made a patrol and captured five British merchant ships before being taken by HMS Shannon off Boston, Massachusetts, on June 1, 1813. The Royal Navy subsequently converted the captured Chesapeake into HMS Chesapeake, which served until it was broken up in 1819. Some of the pine deck planking from the Chesapeake was incorporated into the Chesapeake Mill in Wickham, England.

Chesapeake was originally designed as a 44-gun frigate, but construction delays, material shortages and budget problems caused builder Josiah Fox to alter his design to 38 guns. Launched at the Gosport Navy Yard on 2 December 1799, Chesapeake began her career during the Quasi-War with France and later saw service in the First Barbary War. On 22 June 1807, she was fired upon by HMS Leopard of the Royal Navy for refusing to allow a search for deserters. The event, now known as the Chesapeake–Leopard affair, angered the American public and government and was a precipitating factor that led to the War of 1812. As a result of the affair, Chesapeake's commanding officer, James Barron, was court-martialed and the United States instituted the Embargo Act of 1807 against the United Kingdom. Early in the War of 1812, she made one patrol and captured five British merchant ships. She was captured by HMS Shannon shortly after sailing from Boston, Massachusetts, on 1 June 1813. The Royal Navy took her into their service as HMS Chesapeake, where she served until she was broken up and her timbers sold in 1819. Some of the pine deck planking was incorporated into the Chesapeake Mill in Wickham, England.

draft: Helicobacter pylori (H. pylori), a spiral-shaped, microaerophilic, Gram-negative bacterium that infects the stomach of nearly half the world's population, has been categorized by the International Agency for Research on Cancer (IARC) as a group I carcinogen. Highly linked to chronic active gastritis, peptic ulcers, lymphoma of the mucosa-associated lymphoid tissue (MALT), and gastric adenocarcinoma, H. pylori infection typically occurs during childhood and, if untreated, can persist for life. Current treatment strategies rely on a combination approach involving triple or quadruple therapies consisting of antibiotics, proton pump inhibitors, and bismuth compounds, spread over a period of 10 to 14 days. However, the eradication rate of H. pylori has been declining worldwide, coinciding with a surge in clarithromycin resistance across multiple countries over the past decade. Moreover, reports of antibiotic-resistant strains, rising treatment costs, poor patient compliance, and a significant recurrence rate of the infection are the primary factors contributing to the ineffectiveness of broad-scale H. pylori treatment control. Therefore, research into the immune response and protective mechanisms against H. pylori is essential for overcoming current treatment limitations and developing more effective strategies for the prevention and treatment of H. pylori infection.

draft: Compared to most other gastropods, L. canarium exhibits an atypical locomotion technique that is unique to the Strombidae family. This peculiar style of movement was first detailed by American zoologist George Howard Parker in his 1922 publication. Initially, the animal propels its posterior end by inserting the sickle-shaped operculum into the substrate. Subsequently, it extends its foot forward and propels the shell ahead through a motion described as "leaping." Burrowing behavior, characteristic of strombid gastropods, involves the animal sinking itself into the substrate. For L. canarium, this behavior is a series of specific movements: probing, shoveling, and retraction. Probing involves pushing the anterior portion of the foot into the substrate to create a foothold. Next, shoveling entails using the elongated proboscis to push the substrate. Finally, retraction involves moving the shell along an anterior-posterior axis to settle the substrate around it. Following this, a dorsal portion of the dorsal shell is typically still visible, despite the animal's soft parts and the ventral surface being buried. Gastropods, in general, exhibit a strong escape response to stimuli, such as the presence of a predator nearby. This response involves the perception of stimuli and a subsequent escape motion. The perception of environmental chemical stimuli, such as those originating from food or other organisms, can be mediated by sensory organs like the osphradium. For L. canarium, the perception of a predator can occur through chemoreception or vision, given the developed visual senses of strombid gastropods. The presence of a predator can significantly affect L. canarium's movement, increasing the frequency of leaps.
human: Behaviour Compared to most other gastropods, L. canarium has an unusual means of locomotion that is common only among the Strombidae. This curious series of maneuvers was originally described by American zoologist George Howard Parker in 1922. The animal initially fixes the posterior end of the foot by thrusting the point of its sickle-shaped operculum into the substrate. Then, it extends its foot forward, lifting the shell and throws it ahead in a motion that has been described as "leaping". Burrowing behaviour, in which an individual sinks itself entirely (or partially) into the substrate, is frequent among strombid gastropods. The burrowing behaviour of L. canarium consists of a series of movements characteristic of the species. There are three consecutive movements: first is probing, where the animal pushes the anterior portion of the foot into the substrate to gain a hold; next is shovelling, where it pushes the substrate with its long, extensible proboscis. Retraction is the final movement, where it moves the shell along an anterior-posterior axis to settle the substrate around it. Once burrowed, part of the dorsal shell is usually still visible (although the ventral surface and the animal's soft parts are buried). The escape response in gastropods—the perception of stimuli (for example, the presence of a predator nearby) and a subsequent escape motion—is a frequent target of behavioural studies. In gastropods, the perception of environmental chemical stimuli originating, for example, from food or other organisms is possibly mediated by sensory organs such as the osphradium. In the case of L. canarium, the perception of a predator can occur through chemoreception or vision (a well-developed sense in strombid gastropods). The presence of a predator can significantly alter the movement pattern of L. canarium, inducing an increase in the frequency of leaps.

draft: Starting in the 1970s, following the emergence of resistance to DDT, various organophosphate (OP) and carbamate (CB) insecticides like Malathion, Fenitrothion, Bendiocarb, and Propoxur were used as alternatives in mosquito control studies. Bioassay results indicated that all populations of Culex pipiens from the Mediterranean and Aegean regions are resistant to both OP and CB insecticides. This resistance can be attributed to the extensive use of OP and CB insecticides, particularly Malathion, for agricultural pest control. This intensive use leads to significant selection pressure in agricultural areas. Additionally, similar to Culex pipiens populations in Turkey, high levels of insecticide resistance have been reported in populations from neighboring countries including Iran, Russia, and Greece. For example, in some parts of Greece, resistance to Temephos and Deltamethrin has been observed. Similarly, in the center of Moscow, resistance to Fenitrothion, DDT, Dieldrin, Propoxur, Bendiocarb, Malathion, Deltamethrin, Permethrin, Lambda-cyhalothrin, Etofenprox, and Cyfluthrin was documented. These findings suggest that widespread use of OP and CB insecticides, especially Malathion, in agricultural pest control has led to significant resistance in various Culex pipiens populations across multiple countries.

draft: Several authors propose that depression arises from dysfunctional neurogenesis in brain regions responsible for emotion and cognition. This hypothesis is grounded in the observed correlation between lower levels of brain-derived neurotrophic factor (BDNF) and higher incidences of depressive symptoms. By examining existing research on the connection between BDNF blood concentrations and depression, we can find sufficient evidence to support this association. Patients with depression exhibit lower serum and plasma BDNF levels compared to healthy controls. Thus, many studies have identified BDNF as a potential biomarker for depression. Our study did not find significant differences in plasma BDNF concentrations among patients with depression and healthy controls, nor did it identify any correlations between BDNF levels and depression scale scores. These studies should be interpreted cautiously, as they present mixed results, have small sample sizes, are subject to systematic publication errors, and exhibit varying patterns of BDNF measurement. When considering these factors, especially the different sampling methods that can affect BDNF levels, the interpretation of BDNF's relationship with depression is complicated. Overall, the relationship between peripheral blood BDNF and depression remains unclear, and further careful validation is needed. At this stage, the blood BDNF value is not recommended for use as a biomarker in clinical practice.

draft: Patient Two is a 52-year-old female with a chronic obstructive pulmonary disease history. Due to significant osteoarthritis affecting her left hip, she underwent a primary total hip replacement arthroplasty. She has had previous hip prostheses revisions over the past five years. On initial presentation, the patient exhibited a productive fistula on the posterior thigh, with a C-reactive protein (CRP) level of 63.2 mg/L. Radiographic examination revealed diffuse osteomyelitis of the proximal femur and femoral stem rupture. Cultures from CT-guided periprosthetic samples and draining material tested negative, thus no antibiotic treatment was administered preoperatively. A one-stage revision arthroplasty was performed using a large prosthetic system: the Megasystem-C stem Link® (Hamburg, Germany) and the G7® acetabular system with freedom constrained liner (Zimmer Biomet, Delaware, USA). Four of the seven periprosthetic soft tissue samples cultured Staphylococcus epidermidis, and both femoral and acetabular bone samples were also positive for S. epidermidis. Histological analysis showed less than five polymorphonuclear leukocytes (PMNs) per high-power field in five fields observed at 400× magnification. The patient received extended empiric antibiotic coverage with meropenem and linezolid, which was initiated 15 minutes before surgery. The antibiotic coverage was changed to linezolid after identifying the microorganism, and she completed six weeks of treatment. Following her four-year follow-up, the patient exhibited no clinical or laboratory signs of infection, and radiographic examination did not reveal loosening or signs of infection.

draft: In early postnatal development, synapses onto mouse pyramidal neurons organize themselves into clusters. This process continues to refine over development and cannot occur without spontaneous activity. Experiments that block specific signaling molecules and their receptors suggest that a family of signaling molecules known as neurotrophic factors are involved in this organization. Computational modeling indicates that the interactions among these neurotrophic factors can implement a local plasticity rule that generates synaptic clustering. Poorly synchronized synapses weaken, while well-synchronized synapses become stable. As the animal develops and engages with more complex environments through sensory input, the complexity of the plasticity mechanism increases over time. Although the prevalence of relevant neurotrophic factors diminishes with age, there is evidence that the local plasticity rule is operative in adult animals, likely mediated by different sets of interacting molecules. This similarity suggests that the foundational principles of synaptic plasticity remain consistent throughout adult life, providing a basis for more adaptable forms of plasticity.

draft: The primary methods for surgical SVASD repair include the two-patch technique and the Warden procedure. Under the two-patch technique, both the ASD and the right atriotomy are closed using a patch. In contrast, the Warden procedure involves dividing the superior vena cava (SVC) above the anomalous pulmonary veins and anastomosing it to the right atrial appendage. The residual segment of the SVC that receives the anomalous pulmonary venous drainage is then baffled to the ASD. Surgical repair generally yields good outcomes with low rates of morbidity or mortality. A retrospective analysis of 115 SVASD patients who underwent surgical repair showed that 77% experienced symptomatic improvement. Preoperative pulmonary artery pressures were found to be a significant factor; patients with higher preoperative pressures experienced a reduced reduction in symptoms. Postoperative complications, such as sinus node dysfunction or stenosis of the pulmonary veins or SVC, were uncommon.

draft: ### Explanation of Total Mesorectal Excision (TME) in Rectal Cancer #### Introduction Total mesorectal excision (TME) is a crucial procedure in the treatment of rectal cancer. Its primary purpose is to reduce the incidence of local recurrence. The mesorectum, also known as the adipose and lymphatic tissues surrounding the rectum, forms the basis of TME. #### Historical Context In 1982, Heald et al. introduced the concept of TME to decrease the postoperative local recurrence rates. They reported a significant reduction in local recurrence, with an improvement from a postoperative local recurrence rate of 38% to a rate of 2.6% in 1986. #### Early Studies and Initial Observations Subsequent studies have further confirmed the effectiveness of TME. In 1986, a report stated that the local recurrence rates were significantly lower at 3-11%, compared to the original operative method. However, the exact local recurrence rate varied among different studies, with some studies showing local recurrence rates as high as over 10%. #### Variability in Recurrence Rates The discrepancies in local recurrence rates across various studies suggest that the quality of the TME procedure might be a significant factor. #### Impact of TME Quality A study that differentiated TME quality into three grades (complete, nearly complete, and incomplete) found that the group with incomplete TME showed a statistically higher local and distant recurrence rate compared to the group with complete TME. This indicates that the quality of TME directly impacts the outcome. #### Conclusion Studies consistently demonstrate that the better the quality of TME, the lower the local recurrence rate. Therefore, TME is essential for reducing local recurrence in rectal cancer patients.
human: In rectal cancer, total mesorectal excision (TME) is a necessary procedure for reducing local recurrence. The mesorectum is the adipose and lymphatic tissues encircling the rectum. The TME procedure sharply dissects the avascular plane between the parietal fascia and the visceral fascia covering the mesorectum. In 1982, Heald et al. suggested the concept of TME to reduce postoperative local recurrence. A local recurrence of 2.6% in rectal cancer after TME was reported in 1986. Subsequently, numerous studies reported a low local recurrence after TME of 3%–11%, comparable with the original operative method in which local recurrence reached 38%. However, local recurrence after TME was very different in each study, and there was over 10% local recurrence after TME in some studies. The possibility of inappropriate TME may have caused different local recurrence rates to emerge. In a study that classified TME quality into three grades (complete, nearly complete, and incomplete), the incomplete TME patient group showed a statistically higher local/distant recurrence rate than the complete TME patient group. As many studies report, the better the quality of TME, the better the oncological outcome.

draft: The Longest Common Subsequence (LCS) problem is a fundamental issue in computer science. Given two strings, X and Y, the LCS problem involves identifying the longest subsequence that is common to both strings. This problem is particularly relevant in genomics, where it is analogous to alignment algorithms used for measuring the dissimilarity between sequences. The LCS algorithm has proven to be highly effective in compressing DNA sequences, a significant utility in scenarios where large amounts of data need to be shared or stored in limited storage resources. Tabulation is a method that involves solving a problem by first filling a table and then deriving the solution to the original problem from the results contained within this table.

Moreover, it has shown efficient results in compressing sequences of DNA, which is of major utility when large data needs to be shared or stored in limited storage resources. Tabulation is an approach where we solve a problem by first filling up a table, and then computing the solution to the original problem based on the previous results in this table.

draft: The Laevistrombus canarium, also known as the large dog-conch, has edible flesh and is widely consumed in many coastal regions of Southeast Asia. This species is of significant economic importance and is considered one of the most valuable fishery resources in these areas. Locals living along the seashores rely on it as a staple food source. This fishery resource is found in many countries in Southeast Asia, where it is commonly fished. Despite its ornamental value, the L. canarium shells are traditionally used by local fishermen as sinkers for fishing nets. Studies conducted between 2008 and 2009 indicated that overexploitation and overfishing of L. canarium have led to significant depletion in various regions. Malacologists and ecologists recommended reducing exploitation rates to maintain the natural resource's availability. The difficulty in finding large individuals of L. canarium has become more pronounced in several regions where it occurs. Initiatives in Phuket, a province in southern Thailand, aim to increase depleted natural populations of L. canarium. To achieve this, local authorities are considering reintroducing cultured individuals into seagrass beds. The objective is to encourage fishermen not to collect younger, smaller individuals that have not yet reproduced, thereby helping to restore the natural population. Furthermore, researchers from Taiwan have been developing aquaculture methods to mass-produce L. canarium for human consumption. This initiative aims to mitigate the impact on naturally occurring populations of the species. In summary, Laevistrombus canarium, a valuable fishery resource, faces threats due to overexploitation. Efforts are underway to sustain its natural populations through reintroduction and aquaculture methods.

draft: In the context of acute coronary syndrome (ACS), the assessment of coronary microcirculation has been thoroughly investigated. Complications such as chronic microcirculatory disease (CMD) and chronic microvascular occlusion (CMVO) frequently occur in up to half of patients who undergo primary percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) despite the success of the procedure. Specifically, in patients presenting with ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI), primary PCI can achieve epicardial reperfusion but fails to restore myocardial perfusion in a significant portion of cases—known as "no-reflow" syndrome. This phenomenon is quantified using the TIMI flow grade, a numeric index that assigns scores from 0 to 3 to the degree of vessel opacification (0: no flow, 3: normal flow). The mechanisms underlying impaired flow after PCI are diverse and include distal embolization, ischemia-reperfusion injury, and the inherent susceptibility of coronary microcirculation to injury. The prognostic significance of CMVO in ACS has been well-documented: patients with STEMI complicated by CMVO have a markedly increased risk of death and rehospitalization due to heart failure compared to those who achieve optimal myocardial reperfusion. It appears that a comprehensive evaluation of microvascular resistance offers a valuable method to identify patients who are more prone to postprocedural microvascular injury. Even in the absence of overt CMVO, it has been observed that postprocedural microvascular resistances correlate with more extensive myocardial damage and a higher incidence of adverse events at follow-up. These findings suggest that the index of microcirculatory resistance (IMR) may serve as an early diagnostic marker for CMD and as a measure of the efficacy of invasive treatment.
human: Coronary microcirculation has also been extensively assessed in the setting of an ACS. CMD and CMVO, a well-known complication of coronary interventions in the presence of a high thrombotic burden, occur in up to half of the patients undergoing otherwise successful primary PCI. In fact, in a variable proportion of patients presenting with a STEMI ranging from 5% to 50%, primary PCI achieves epicardial coronary artery reperfusion but not myocardial reperfusion, a condition known as “no-reflow”. This phenomenon is quantitatively described with the TIMI flow grade, a numeric index attributing a 0 to 3 score to the vessel opacification (0 = no flow, 3 = normal flow). Mechanisms underlying any degree of impaired flow after PCI vary, and include distal embolization, ischemia-reperfusion injury, and the individual predisposition of coronary microcirculation to injury. The prognostic relevance of CMVO in ACS has been well established: patients with STEMI complicated by CMVO show a significantly higher incidence of death and rehospitalization for heart failure than those with optimal myocardial reperfusion. Therefore, a comprehensive assessment of microvascular resistance seems to be a further legitimate method to identify the cohort of patients more susceptible to postprocedural microvascular injury. Moreover, even in the absence of evident CMVO, postprocedural microvascular resistances correlate with more extensive myocardial damage, and potentially with a higher incidence of adverse events at follow-up, thus suggesting that the IMR may play an essential role as an early diagnostic marker for CMD, as well as a measure of invasive treatment efficacy.

draft: Our findings are not unexpected, given Georgia's unique fauna that spans both Europe and Asia, and its proximity to the Middle East. Geographically located at the heart of this rich biodiversity corridor, Georgia's impressive diversity of coronaviruses (CoVs) can be partly attributed to its relatively modest territory (69,705 square kilometers). This high CoV diversity also predicts a similar degree of CoV richness for unexplored countries surrounding it. We observed that all the bat species found in Georgia that tested positive for CoVs have broad geographic distributions across Eurasia, parts of Africa, and the Americas. Remarkably, Georgia's CoVs share a recent common ancestry with CoVs found in widely distributed bat species across Eurasia and the Americas. This empirical observation suggests that CoVs associated with mammals may exhibit complex transmission dynamics within sympatric bat communities, possibly reflecting the susceptibility of multiple bat species to infection. Recent modeling efforts have assessed the global risk of bat-associated zoonotic diseases. Some of these studies suggest that Western Asia, particularly the region that includes Georgia, is a hotspot for the presence of BetaCoVs with pandemic potential, outside of Southeast Asia, Western Europe, and Central Asia.

draft: ### Multidisciplinary Training for COVID-19 and Its Impact Several studies have investigated multidisciplinary training processes related to Personal Protective Equipment (PPE) usage, swab testing accuracy, and the fundamentals of COVID-19. These studies collectively discuss the role of education in various aspects of prevention, diagnosis, and treatment of the disease. #### Khan and Kiani's Study - **Objective**: To assess the rate of preparedness and perceived safety among medical and non-medical health personnel before and after an interventional training course. - **Training Methodology**: The intervention was a simulation-based course that included various scenarios such as: - PPE usage - Methods of sampling (polymerase chain reaction tests and blood tests) - Biosafety guidelines and protocols in hospitals - Disinfection protocols (hand and surface) - **Evaluation**: Post-intervention, participants demonstrated an improvement in their perceived preparedness for patient care and safety. This improvement was statistically significant (P < 0.05) compared to pre-intervention scores. - **Conclusion**: The trainings based on simulation were found to have a positive role in improving staff readiness and handling capabilities for managing COVID-19. #### Mileder et al.'s Study - **Objective**: Similar to Khan and Kiani's study, this multidisciplinary training aimed to prepare healthcare personnel, including emergency medical assistants and physicians. - **Training Methodology**: A one-day curriculum was developed, incorporating: - Theoretical knowledge - Technical skills - Simulation-based training - **Evaluation**: The training was evaluated using the Objective Structured Clinical Examination (OSCE). - **Learning Effects**: Participants achieved a mean score of 98.6%. - **Success Rate**: Participants achieved a success rate of 97.8% in dealing with COVID-19 scenarios. - **Conclusion**: The training was found to be effective in preparing participants to handle COVID-19 cases successfully. ### Summary Both studies demonstrated the effectiveness of simulation-based training in improving healthcare personnel's preparedness and skills related to handling COVID-19. The methodologies were methodologically similar, with both studies emphasizing the integration of theoretical and practical training elements.
human: There were some articles that investigated multidisciplinary training processes including the education about PPE usage, swab testing accuracy, and fundamentals of COVID-19; these studies discuss the role of education in prevention, diagnosis, and treatment. The aim of Khan and Kiani's study was to assess the rate of preparedness and perception of safety among medical and non-medical health personnel, before and after the interventional training course. The deployed simulation-based course consisted of different scenarios including some essential matters including PPE usage, the methods of sampling (polymerase chain reaction tests and blood test), biosafety guidelines and protocols in the hospital, and disinfection protocols (hand and surface). Simulated scenarios were used, and mannequins were employed. Post-intervention, the participants’ perceived rate of preparedness for patient care and safety was improved and had a significant difference compared to the pretest (P < 0.05). The researchers concluded that the trainings based on simulation had a positive role in staff preparedness and perceptions in handling and management of COVID-19. Mileder et al. also conducted a multidisciplinary study which was methodologically similar to the study of Khan and Kiani. The 1-day curriculum consisted of theoretical, technical, and simulation-based training. Patient communication and identification, nasal swab testing approaches, and donning and doffing PPEs were taught to emergency medical assistants and a physician. To examine learning effects, the objective structured clinical examination was utilized (mean rate = 98.6%). Based on the results, the training was helpful in preparing participants to deal with COVID-19 (success rate = 97.8%).

draft: Several critical factors—such as nuclear and histologic grade, lymph node status, tumor size, mitotic activity index, cellularity index, and the mean and standard deviation of nuclear area—have been identified as significant predictors of prognosis in breast carcinoma. Additional research indicates that morphometric measurements enhance the accuracy of predicting outcomes related to lymph node status and tumor size. Studies have shown that mitotic activity index (MNA) is notably higher in tumors of postmenopausal women compared to those of premenopausal women, as well as in patients with lymph node-positive tumors versus those with negative lymph nodes. Additionally, MNA values are typically greater in tumors measuring over 3 cm compared to those less than 3 cm. Research also reveals significant differences in prognosis between various clinical stages, histological grades, and histological types of tumors. Notably, there are significant correlations between MNA and histological grades, standard mitotic indices, and tumor size.

draft: The discovery and function of U8 snoRNA, a unique component of the small nucleolar ribonucleoprotein (snoRNA) family, date back to 1984. It is one of the few C/D box snoRNAs that are essential for the cleavage of pre-rRNA, particularly in vertebrates, and not for 2′-O-methylation. To date, this snoRNA has been found exclusively in vertebrates. While a yeast homolog of U8 has not yet been identified, a putative candidate in C. elegans, known as CeR-2, suggests the presence of related snoRNAs in nematodes. The importance of U8 in this context was highlighted when mutations in SNORD118, which encodes U8, were discovered to cause a disease known as LCC. Similarly, in 2016, mutations in SNORD118/U8 were found to cause calcifications and cysts. The exact mechanism by which these mutations lead to the formation of these calcifications and cysts remains unclear. More recently, white matter disease resembling LCC, also known as Alopecia Neuro Endocrine disease, was observed in a patient. This disease is also classified as a ribosomopathy, suggesting a common presentation of these pathologies.

Recently, white matter disease similar to LCC has been observed in a new Alopecia Neuro Endocrine disease patient, also a ribosomopathy, suggesting at least some common presentation of disease.

draft: In 1993, Peculis and Steitz demonstrated the primary role of U8 snoRNA in the pre-60S rRNA processing pathway. They conducted their research using Xenopus laevis oocytes, employing RNAase H depletion of U8 in conjunction with microinjection of antisense deoxyoligonucleotides (ASOs) for stimulation. Their experiments revealed that the reduction of U8 snoRNA led to a decrease in the processing of both the internal transcribed spacer regions and the 3′-end of the 28S rRNA coding region. This resulted in the identification of novel pre-rRNA intermediates, indicating that alternative processing pathways are available but are not typically utilized. Subsequent work by Peculis and Steitz in 1994 further confirmed that 5′-end processing of 5.8S rRNA and the 3′-end processing of 28S rRNA are linked through the action of U8 snoRNA.

draft: This passage describes the synthesis method of the Zn-abietate complex, utilizing Na-abietate as an intermediate. Pinus elliottii var. elliottii resin serves as the primary reactant, selected for its low cost, abundance, antibacterial properties, and regional reforestation value. The reaction process consists of two stages. Initially, 164.0 grams of purified resin from Pinus elliottii var. elliottii resin are mixed with 21.67 grams of 20% sodium hydroxide (NaOH) dissolved in 200 milliliters of deionized water. This mixture is stirred at 90°C for three hours, during which all reaction water is evaporated, leaving behind a hygroscopic salt (Na-abietate). Subsequently, in the second stage, 30.1 grams of Na-abietate (0.0933 moles) are dissolved in 50 milliliters of deionized water, and this solution is cooled. Another solution is prepared with 9.0 grams of zinc sulfate (ZnSO4.7H2O, 99% purity) dissolved in 30 milliliters of deionized water. These two solutions are then mixed dropwise under stirring and cooled in an ice bath. The substitution reaction leading to the formation of Zn-abietate occurs immediately. The final complex is washed with deionized water, vacuum filtered, and dried at 70°C for five hours. Afterward, it is mechanically ground and sieved to achieve the desired granulometry for pigment application. The resulting powder exhibits a light yellow hue and possesses hydrophobic properties. The stoichiometric ratio for the formation of the Zn-abietate complex in the second stage is 3:1 (Na-abietate:Zn2+).

draft: Based on our knowledge, this represents the inaugural WES (Whole Exome Sequencing) study investigating the genetic association between KD (Kjer-Larsen Syndrome) and CAA (Coats' Disease). Through this study, we identified several rare coding-risk variants potentially linked to KD and CAA, but we were unable to confirm the significance of these selected SNPs (Single Nucleotide Polymorphisms) in a replication study. The low frequency of these SNPs was a primary contributor to this outcome. Another reason for the lack of significant replication in our study can be attributed to sample selection bias. To enrich for potential causal variants at the WES stage, we selected more severe cases of KD compared to the replication stage. For instance, patients with medium-sized or giant aneurysms accounted for 6.3% of the WES samples versus 1.7% of the replication samples, and we also observed higher rates of IVIG (intravenous immunoglobulin) resistance (50.3% compared to 22.5%), recurrence (14.5% compared to 5.5%), and a family history of KD (6.3% compared to 1.9%). Consequently, more variants linked to these severe phenotypes might have been identified during the WES stage. However, when combining the WES data with replication results, statistically significant associations were detected. WES is a powerful technique for identifying protein-coding variants, which are easier to annotate and assign to potential biological functions, thereby helping to pinpoint causative genes. However, functional variants are often rare. Therefore, large sample sizes are typically necessary to detect loci with exome-wide significance, especially for highly polygenic traits such as those we studied; yet, we were able to sequence only a small number of samples, particularly for children with CAA. Both common and rare variant association approaches are highly underpowered in small sample sizes. Consequently, our conclusions are tentative and preliminary, and further studies with larger sample sizes are necessary to confirm our findings and elucidate the functional roles of the newly identified genes and variants in KD pathogenesis.

Another reason for lack of significance in a replication study can be partly due to sample selection bias. To enrich for possible causative variants in the WES stage, we selected more severe KD cases than in the replication stage, such as patients with medium-sized or giant aneurysms (6.3% in WES samples vs. 1.7% in replication samples), IVIG resistance (50.3% vs. 22.5%), recurrence (14.5% vs. 5.5%), and family history (6.3% vs. 1.9%). Therefore, more variants that result in these severe phenotypes may have been discovered in the WES stage; however, in combined analysis of WES and replication data, statistically significant associations were detected. WES is a powerful technique for identification of protein-coding variants, which are more straightforward to annotate for biological functions and help to pinpoint causative genes; however, functional variants are more likely to be rare. Therefore, large sample sizes are usually required to detect loci with exome-wide significance, particularly for highly polygenic traits; however, we were only able to sequence a small number of samples, particularly in the case of children with CAA. Both common and rare variant association approaches are drastically underpowered to detect associations in small samples. Thus, our conclusions are tentative and preliminary, and further studies with large sample size are necessary to confirm our findings, as well as the functional role of the newly identified genes and variants in KD pathogenesis.

These approaches are known as **Bottom-Up (Tabulation)** and **Top-Down (Memoization)** Dynamic Programming (DP) techniques. ### Bottom-Up (Tabulation) Approach The Bottom-Up approach starts from the initial state or the bottom of the problem and gradually builds up to the desired state or the top. Here's a step-by-step breakdown: 1. **Initialization**: Begin by initializing the solution for the smallest sub-problem or the base case. For example, if solving a sub-problem involves a sequence of states, start with the first state. 2. **Building the Solution**: Work your way up the sequence, starting from the first state and moving towards the last. In each step, compute the required sub-problems based on previously computed sub-problems. 3. **Final Solution**: By the end of this process, the solution for the entire sequence or the target state is computed. ### Top-Down (Memoization) Approach The Top-Down approach, also known as Memoization, is a recursive method where we start from the topmost or the target state and gradually work our way down to the base states: 1. **Recursive Computation**: Begin by computing the value of the topmost state. If the state's value has already been computed and stored, the function directly returns the stored value. 2. **Recursive Calls**: For each sub-problem, compute the value and store it. If the sub-problem has already been computed, return the stored value. 3. **Base Case**: Move towards the base state by solving sub-problems recursively. Each sub-problem's value is computed once and stored to avoid redundant calculations. ### Comparison of Approaches The choice between Tabulation and Memoization depends on the specific problem and the constraints. Here are the key differences: - **Processing Time**: Tabulation generally shows a lower processing time compared to Memoization due to its iterative nature. It processes each sub-problem sequentially, whereas Memoization uses a more recursive and potentially more complex structure. - **Implementation**: Tabulation involves filling a table from the bottom up, starting from the initial state. draft: Development and Design of the Aston Martin Rapide: Development on the Aston Martin Rapide began in 2005 under the guidance of Marek Reichman, who was appointed as the lead design director by Ulrich Bez, the CEO of Aston Martin. Before taking his role, Reichman had studied the characteristics of Aston Martin's cars and made several sketches for a four-door concept. Ulrich Bez gave Reichman the design brief in May, and development immediately commenced. Reichman, along with a team of clay modellers, developed the initial project within seven weeks. By August to December, a team of twenty-six engineers, led by Reichman and Ian Calnan, the general manager of prototype operations, built a full-scale prototype. The prototype was completed on December 22, 2005, and made its debut at the 2006 North American International Auto Show in January. In November 2008 and April 2009, Aston Martin released the first official images of the production version of the Rapide. The car made its debut at the 2009 International Motor Show in Germany in September. Production of the Aston Martin Rapide officially began on May 7, 2010, at a facility owned by Magna Steyr, an automobile manufacturer based in Graz, Austria. In the middle of 2012, Aston Martin ended its production arrangement with Magna Steyr, six years earlier than expected. Production halted temporarily in May 2011 due to declining demand for luxury saloons and in response to reduced sales. In June 2011, Aston Martin reduced the annual production output from 2,000 to 1,250 units. To address the declining production and align it with sales, Aston Martin received a £1.6 million funding package from the British government's Regional Growth Fund. This funding was part of an agreement between the government and private industry to invest £200 million in the economy. In 2012, Aston Martin moved the production of the Rapide to Gaydon, a village in Warwickshire. The production of the Aston Martin Rapide was conducted at Gaydon until the car was discontinued in 2020.

draft: The renin-angiotensin-aldosterone system (RAAS) is prominently over-activated in conditions such as cardiovascular diseases (CVDs) and hypertension (HTN). The activation of RAAS leads to increased levels of angiotensin II (Ang II), its primary effector peptide, in both circulating and tissue levels. Elevated oxidative stress markers have also been observed in patients with heart failure (HF), and these levels are correlated with circulating Ang II levels. Ang II induces hypertrophy, which can be partially attenuated by delphinidin, an anthocyanidin. This effect is indicative of reduced activity in the key signaling pathways extracellular signal-regulated kinases 1/2 (ERK1/2), mitogen-activated protein kinases (MAPK), and c-Jun N-terminal kinase (JNK). Furthermore, pretreatment with delphinidin significantly reduces the levels of hydrogen peroxide (H2O2) and reactive oxygen species (O2•−) in these patients. This is consistent with reduced activity of NADPH oxidase (Nox), particularly Nox2.
human: Among the pathways being over activated in CVDs and HTN, is the renin-angiotensin-aldosterone system (RAAS). Activation of RAAS and as a consequence, increased circulating and tissue levels of its primary effector peptide, angiotensin II (Ang II), are among the most prominent processes observed in HTN. Alongside, oxidative stress markers were shown to be elevated and correlated with circulating AngII levels in HF patients. Ang II-mediated hypertrophy was observed to be attenuated by delphinidin (an anthocyanidin), which was reflective of reduced activation of extracellular signal-regulated kinases 1/2) (ERK1/2), mitogen-activated protein kinases (MAPK) and c-Jun N-terminal kinase (JNK). Additionally, reports indicate that pretreatment with delphinidin, significantly reduced both H2O2 and O2•−, which was reflective of reduced NADPH oxidase (Nox) activity, particularly Nox2.

draft: Ewing sarcoma (ES) is a type of cancer characterized by small, round cells found in various parts of the body. It primarily affects children and teenagers but can affect people of all ages. ES can develop in either the bone (skeletal ES) or soft tissue (extra skeletal, extraosseous ES), though it is more common in bones. Extraosseous Ewing sarcoma (EES) represents a significant portion of all Ewing sarcoma cases, accounting for 16–31% of all cases. The most common sites for EES are the chest wall, paravertebral region, extremities, buttocks, and retroperitoneum. EES is known for its rapid growth and tendency to form metastases, which typically occur in the lungs and bones. Patients with Ewing sarcoma frequently experience localized, intermittent, or varying intensity pain. This pain may sometimes be accompanied by a visible or palpable mass at the affected site. When the condition is in its advanced or metastatic stage, patients may exhibit nonspecific symptoms such as fatigue, weakness, fever, anaemia, and signs of inflammation, including weight loss. These nonspecific symptoms can sometimes mimic other diseases, leading to a significant delay in the diagnosis of EES, which might even be confused with traumatic haematoma.

draft: The research reveals strong evidence supporting the notion that women directors can play a significant role in assisting companies in managing sustainable practices and addressing social responsibilities in an ethical manner. Given the higher prevalence of unethical behavior in emerging economies, it is recommended that policymakers and regulators in China, as well as in other Asian and European countries, further improve and legislate gender quotas for women on corporate boards. This move is expected to enhance the internal corporate governance mechanisms of these firms and contribute to the achievement of social and environmental goals. However, the transition process is fraught with numerous challenges. These obstacles include the dismissal of women from informal networks, a hostile corporate culture, and prejudice against women in leadership roles. To surmount these hurdles, it is essential for policymakers to develop training programs that empower women with the skills needed to thrive in the business environment and foster a competitive environment conducive to their career advancement.

notes: - we demonstrate that tumor cell-derived NAMPT promotes the expansion of MDSCs
draft: In this study, we illustrate that tumor cells-derived nicotinamide phosphoribosyltransferase (NAMPT) enhances the expansion of myeloid suppressor cells (MDSCs), thereby diminishing T-cell mediated antitumor immunity. Our research also introduces the first PROTAC (Proteolysis Targeting Chimera) that degrades iNAMPT (intracellular NAMPT) and diminishes the secretion of eNAMPT (extracellular NAMPT). This approach effectively blocks both enzymatic and non-enzymatic functions of NAMPT. PROTAC A7 demonstrates superior efficacy compared to existing NAMPT enzymatic inhibitors in syngeneic mouse tumor models. Altogether, our findings position PROTAC A7 as a viable approach for both enzymatic and non-enzymatic NAMPT intervention, offering new therapeutic strategies in cancer immunotherapy.
human: In this study, we demonstrate that tumor cell-derived NAMPT promotes the expansion of MDSCs, thus dampening the T cell-mediated antitumor immunity likely via an enzymatic activity independent function. We also reported the first PROTAC that degrades iNAMPT and diminishes eNAMPT secretion, thus blocking both enzymatic and non-enzymatic function of NAMPT. PROTAC A7 exhibits superior efficacy to reported NAMPT enzymatic inhibitors in syngeneic mice tumor models. Together, our findings provide PROTAC A7 as an applicable approach for both enzymatic and non-enzymatic NAMPT intervention, informing new therapeutic strategies in cancer immunotherapy.

draft: Laevistrombus canarium is characterized by a heavy shell with a rounded outline. Its adult shell length ranges from approximately 29 mm (1.1 inches) to 71 mm (2.8 inches). The outer surface of the shell is generally smooth, with only barely visible spiral lines and occasional varices on the spire. Unlike other species in the genus Strombus, the stromboid notch on the outer lip is inconspicuous. When viewed from the ventral side (with the anterior end pointing downwards), a normal adult dextral shell of this species features the stromboid notch as a shallow, secondary anterior indentation to the right of the siphonal canal. The siphonal canal itself is straight, short, and ample, and the columella is smooth, without any folds. Adult specimens of Laevistrombus canarium have a moderately flared, posteriorly protruding outer lip that is considerably thickened and entirely free of marginal spikes or plicae. The body whorl is roundly swollen at the shoulder, with a few anterior spiral grooves. The shell exhibits a medium-to-high cone-shaped spire, with at least five delicately furrowed whorls. The shell color can vary from golden yellow to light yellowish-brown to grey. The underside of the shell is often paler than the top or entirely white. In some cases, mature specimens may display a metallic-grey or golden-brown gloss on the margin of the outer lip and the callus. A zigzag network of darker lines is occasionally visible on the outer surface of the shell. The periostracum, the outermost layer of the shell, is yellowish-brown and usually thick, reticulated, and fimbriated over the sutures. The corneous operculum, which forms the outer margin of the shell, is dark brown and typically has the typical shape of the family Strombidae: a slightly bent sickle with seven or eight weak lateral serrations.
