draft: The onset latency of the pN and BP was calculated using a jackknife-based procedure to mitigate inaccuracies in onset latency measurements from a noisy single-subject ERP. Specifically, this method involves computing a jackknife subsample score \( S_i \) for each participant. This score is derived by temporarily excluding a participant \( i \) and calculating the onset latencies \( \text{pN} \) and \( \text{BP} \) from the grand-average waveform of the remaining \( n-1 \) participants. The onset latency is determined by identifying the first time point at which the amplitude is statistically significantly higher than the baseline period, using paired t-tests and peak electrodes \( Fpz \) and \( CPz \) for \( \text{pN} \) and \( \text{BP} \), respectively. This procedure is repeated for each subject to generate subsample scores \( S_1, S_2, \ldots, S_{12} \) for each group and condition. These scores are then used to estimate the standard error of the grand-average latency and for statistical analysis. Additionally, to address the low variability introduced by the jackknife procedure and to correct for the factorial ANOVA design, we applied a correction factor \( Fc = F/(n-1)^2 \) as suggested by Ulrich & Miller. This adjustment ensures that the corrected ANOVA on the subsample scores is equivalent to the one on the original values. Considering the higher signal-to-noise ratio in group averages compared to individual waveforms, this method is found to be more accurate than methods that use individual waveforms for analysis.
human: The onset latency of the pN and the BP were also calculated using a jackknife-based procedure to avoid the inaccuracies of onset latency measurements computed from a noisy single-subject ERP. Accordingly, a jackknife subsample score S_i was computed for participants by temporarily omitting participant i and calculating the pN and BP onset in the grand-average waveform computed from the remaining n − 1 participant. The onset latency was calculated as the first time point that showed a statistically significant higher amplitude than the baseline period using paired t-tests, n − 1 participants at pN, and BP peak electrodes (Fpz and CPz, respectively). This procedure is repeated for each subject yielding the subsample scores S_1 … S_12 for each group and condition. The subsample scores for all 12 participants were then used to estimate the standard error of the grand-average latency and for statistical analysis. We also reduced the F value Fc = F/(n − 1)2 as proposed by Ulrich & Miller for factorial ANOVA designs to compensate the low variability of the jackknife procedure, and because the corrected ANOVA of the subsample scores is equivalent to the one of corresponding original values. Considering the higher signal-to-noise ratio of group averages than single participants, this method has been proved to be more accurate than methods of analysis using individual waveforms.

Through the ubiquitin-proteasome system (UPS), SERDs bind to and promote the polyubiquitination and degradation of the ERα receptor. Despite the current evaluation of several SERDs, fulvestrant is the first SERD to receive approval as a first-line ET. draft: We predict the minimum-free energy (MFE) of each primary microRNA (pri-miRNA)-16-1 variant and use this value as a measure of overall structural flexibility. Those pri-miRNA-16-1 variants that are less structured (more flexible) than the wild-type variant are processed by Drosha with alternative cleavage frequencies that are 2 to 6 times higher than those of the wild-type. This finding suggests that the structural flexibility of pri-miRNA is inversely correlated with Drosha cleavage fidelity. To support this concept, we found that the pri-miRNA-16-1 variants with the highest alternative cleavage rates (the top 1%) had the lowest average MFE values, whereas those with the lowest alternative cleavage rates (the bottom 1%) had the highest average MFE values. Similar results were observed with pri-miRNA-30a, pri-miRNA-125a, and their respective variants (Supplementary Materials), indicating that more flexible pri-miRNA structures were processed by Drosha with a lower cleavage fidelity.

draft: The Ormulum, a twelfth-century work of biblical exegesis, was composed by an Augustinian canon named Orrm (or Orrmin). Comprising just under 19,000 lines of early Middle English verse, this text offers invaluable insights into English pronunciation during a period of linguistic transition following the Norman Conquest of England in 1066. Its unique phonemic orthography makes it a significant resource for philologists and historical linguists in tracing the evolution of the English language. The Ormulum begins with a preface and dedication. The text consists of homilies that interpret biblical texts for use in the liturgical masses throughout the liturgical year. Its purpose was to be consulted as the texts were updated, but it is often considered tedious and repetitive when read in its entirety. Only about one-fifth of the Ormulum's promised material survives, housed in a single manuscript in the Bodleian Library in Oxford. Orm developed a distinctive spelling system to reflect his concern for priests' ability to speak the vernacular. This system, in turn, guided his readers in pronouncing the vowels. Given that many local priests likely spoke Anglo-Norman French, rather than English, this system was particularly useful. Modern scholars use these two features to reconstruct Middle English as it was spoken by Orm. Orm employed a strict poetic metre to ensure that readers could clearly identify stressed syllables. Modern scholars utilize these features to reconstruct Middle English as Orm originally spoke it.

Modern scholars use these two features to reconstruct Middle English as Orrm spoke it.

draft: The production of moderate reactive oxygen species (ROS), triggered by potassium channel openers, promotes the beneficial effects of these openers on ischemic preconditioning (IPC). However, during the reperfusion phase, an excessive ROS production can pave the way for tissue injury. It has been observed that the use of potassium channel openers mitigates this injury. When the causative agent of ischemia is eliminated and the tissue is exposed to reperfusion, reoxygenation occurs, which serves as a potent stimulant for the mitochondrial generation of reactive oxygen species (ROS). This, in turn, triggers cellular oxidative damage. Antioxidant therapy effectively restrains these reperfusion-induced injuries, thereby confirming the crucial role of ROS in such types of tissue damage.

draft: The Great Carrying Place was a navigable route of approximately 12 miles (19 km) that bypassed an impassable stretch of the Dead River, a tributary of the Kennebec. The journey involved a gradual elevation gain of about 1,000 feet (300 m) as the expedition ascended to the higher portions of the route, passing through three ponds along the way. Under the leadership of Lieutenant Church, the survey team described the route as a challenging but potentially manageable path. However, Lieutenant Steele's scouting party, which had navigated the first segment, found themselves on the verge of starvation. Due to depleted supplies and a diet primarily consisting of fish, moose, and duck, the men struggled to sustain themselves. Additional men supplemented their meager rations with local wildlife, necessitating a temporary halt at the second pond where a shelter was constructed to protect the sick. Supplies were also collected from Fort Halifax, where they had been cached. The team’s progress was significantly slowed by heavy rains and boggy terrain, culminating in the death of one party member when a falling tree struck him. Further challenges arose from the contaminated water sources, which led to illness among the crew. Arnold, the expedition’s commander, moved the first two battalions to the Dead River on October 13, with Arnold himself arriving three days later. He proceeded to inform Washington and Montgomery of their progress through a series of letters. These communications, originally intended for Montgomery, were intercepted by Quebec’s Lieutenant Governor Hector Theophilus de Cramahé, providing Quebec with its first indication of the expedition’s progress. Subsequently, Arnold dispatched the survey team to mark the entire route from the Dead River to Lake Mégantic.
human: The Great Carrying Place was a portage of roughly 12 miles (19 km), bypassing an unnavigable section of the Dead River, the tributary of the Kennebec that the expedition was to follow. The portage included a rise in elevation of about 1,000 feet (300 m) to the high points of the carry, with three ponds along the way. Lieutenant Church, the leader of the survey team, described the route as a "bad road but capable of being made good", an assessment that turned out to be somewhat optimistic. The vanguard of the main body, led by Daniel Morgan, met Lieutenant Steele's scouting party en route to the first pond. This party had successfully scouted the route to the height of land above the Dead River, but the men were near starvation. Their supplies had been depleted, and they were largely subsisting on a protein-rich diet of fish, moose, and duck. Most of the men continued to supplement their meager supplies with the local wildlife as the expedition continued. Church, in his description of the route, had failed to account for the heavy rains and the boggy conditions between the first and second ponds. Rain and snow slowed the long portage, and the expedition had its first casualty when a falling tree killed one of the party. Some of the men who drank the stagnant waters along the way became violently ill, forcing Arnold to order construction of a shelter at the second pond as cover for the sick, and to send some men back to Fort Halifax for supplies that had been cached there. The first two battalions finally reached the Dead River on October 13, and Arnold arrived three days later. At this point, Arnold wrote a number of letters informing Washington and Montgomery of his progress. Several letters intended for Montgomery were intercepted and turned over to Quebec's Lieutenant Governor Hector Theophilus de Cramahé, giving Quebec its first notice that the expedition was on its way. Arnold also dispatched the survey team again, this time to mark the trail all the way to Lake Mégantic.

The inclusion criteria for the search were centered around faulty prosthesis and damaged prosthesis. The data was then imported into SPSS version 23.0 for statistical analysis. draft: Ensuring clinical competence among nurses, who are the largest group of healthcare providers, is highly important. Despite this, evidence-based practice is rarely incorporated into nursing undergraduate programs. The reasons for this neglect include: 1. **Lack of Cognitive Skills**: Nurses often do not possess the necessary cognitive skills to effectively implement evidence-based practices. 2. **Recognition Issues**: Nurses may fail to recognize the importance and utility of evidence-based practices. 3. **Lack of Instructor Support**: Nursing instructors rarely provide guidance on how to integrate evidence-based approaches into their practice. 4. **Limited Time**: Undergraduate programs typically do not allocate sufficient time for developing these skills. 5. **Insufficient Search Techniques**: Nurses struggle to use appropriate search techniques to find and apply the latest evidence. These factors collectively mean that many nurses are not adequately prepared to use evidence-based practices when they enter their professional careers. As a result, it is crucial to integrate evidence-based approaches into nursing undergraduate programs to ensure that graduates are well-equipped to provide high-quality care.

draft: Regarding the endogenous systemic levels of GABA in patients with Type 1 Diabetes (T1D) compared to healthy controls (HC), it has been observed that these levels are not decreased in T1D patients when compared to HC. For patients with newly diagnosed T1D, the levels of GABA are also similar to those of healthy controls. draft: It is widely recognized that probiotics effectively manage the intestinal microbiota, with Bifidobacterium being a primary source. Specifically, Bifidobacterium adolescentis (B. adolescentis) and Bifidobacterium bifidum (B. bifidum) are the primary bifidobacteria found in the human intestinal microbiota, predominantly inhabiting the young. Past research indicates that both B. adolescentis and B. bifidum significantly contribute to mitigating metabolic diseases. However, studies focusing on the alleviation of Non-Alcoholic Fatty Liver Disease (NAFLD) through probiotics are relatively scarce, resulting in fewer probiotics capable of this effect. Most of the existing research on this topic has focused on individual strains, making direct comparative analysis challenging due to variations in modeling methodologies, intervention times, and measurement criteria. This disparity complicates the identification of underlying patterns and mechanisms. To address these issues, we have selected seven strains of B. adolescentis and seven strains of B. bifidum for an in-depth evaluation of their efficacy in alleviating NAFLD. This comprehensive approach aims to enrich the existing probiotic resources and further elucidate the mechanisms by which bifidobacteria help manage NAFLD.

Bifidobacterium adolescentis (B. adolescentis) and Bifidobacterium bifidum (B. bifidum) are the dominant bifidobacteria in the human intestinal microbiota, and are mainly colonized in the young. Former studies have found that B. adolescentis and B. bifidum play an important role in alleviating metabolic diseases. At present, there are relatively few studies on the mitigation of NAFLD by probiotics, so the number of probiotics with the mitigation of NAFLD is also relatively small. Among the relevant research, we found that a large number of studies focused on single bacteria, which could not be compared between the same bacteria due to the differences in modeling methods, intervention time and measurement indicators. This would create obstacles to the analysis of rules. Based on the above difficulties, we selected seven strains of B. adolescentis and seven strains of B. bifidum to evaluate the effect of alleviating NAFLD, enrich existing resources and, finally, understand the mechanism through which bifidobacteria alleviates NAFLD.

draft: American singer and songwriter Banks released her third studio album, III, on July 12, 2019, through Harvest Records. This came following the release of her second album, The Altar, and its accompanying tour, The Altar Tour. Banks began composing material for III over a period of approximately two and a half years, primarily at Westlake Recording Studios in Los Angeles. She wrote around 50 songs before narrowing the track list to 13. The album was produced in collaboration with Buddy Ross, BJ Burton, and Hudson Mohawke. Banks announced the album's title and release date in May 2019 and released its cover art and track listing. Three singles were released to support the record: "Gimme," "Look What You're Doing to Me," and "Contaminated." Additionally, Banks embarked on her third headlining concert tour, the III Tour, which played across North America and Europe. draft: Amino acid gamma-aminobutyric acid (GABA) is a crucial and predominantly inhibitory neurotransmitter within the central nervous system (CNS). Within peripheral tissues, endogenous GABA functions as a mediator. It is most concentrated in immune cells and pancreatic beta-cells. draft: Santamental, released in October 2003, is a collaborative album that features a roster of prominent musicians, including guitarists Eddie Van Halen, Slash, and Steve Vai, and drummer Gregg Bissonette. When Lukather's record company, Bop City Records, approached him to create a Christmas album, he responded with a quip about his suitability for the project. The company was convinced that Lukather's unique approach would bring something distinctive to the project, distinct from the typical Christmas music offerings. Lukather enlisted the help of keyboardist Jeff Babko and guitarist Larry Carlton, who he had previously worked with, to arrange the songs. The project posed a significant challenge to Lukather, who had to be creative in transforming the traditionally simple Christmas tunes into something engaging for listeners without altering the core structures. Lukather stated, "But I never dreamt in a million years that I'd do a Christmas record." The musicians chosen for Santamental, many of whom were part of the hard-rock genre, contributed a heavy and distinctive sound to the album. Van Halen recorded his guitar tracks for "Joy to the World" after a considerable absence from the studio, impressing Lukather with his playing. Steve Vai, along with Lukather's son Trevor (aged 14 at the time), provided the guitar work for "Carol of the Bells." Slash, who completed his part in one take, contributed to "Broken Heart for Christmas," a Lukather/Stan Lynch composition. Michael Landau, a well-known session guitarist, played on "Look Out For Angels," and the album includes a version of "Jingle Bells" featuring a big band and Sammy Davis Jr. singing. The recording process for Santamental was completed in just six days, after which Lukather declared, "It is my first and last Christmas album."

draft: Previous studies have identified long non-coding RNAs (lncRNAs) with more than 200 nucleotides as playing crucial roles in the progression of multiple cancers, including Paired Adenocarcinoma of the Duodenum (PAAD). A more recent body of research has uncovered that long intergenic non-coding RNAs (lincRNAs), a subclass of lncRNAs, are dysregulated in various cancers such as colorectal cancer, hepatocellular carcinoma, and PAAD. For example, LINC01232 has been shown to act as an oncogene, promoting the progression of PAAD. Additionally, LINC00857 has been reported to enhance the expression of EMT (Epithelial-Mesenchymal Transition) in hepatocellular carcinoma cells. Notably, high expression of LINC00857 has been correlated with poor survival in lung cancer patients, through its role in mediating tumor progression. However, the association between LINC00857 and PAAD remains unclear. For this reason, our objective is to focus on LINC00857 and investigate its molecular mechanism in PAAD.

draft: The sucrose fractions, isolated from plant samples at two different temperatures, 22°C (fractions 8-11) and 37°C (fractions 9-12), were cleaned using Filter-Aided Sample Preparation (FASP) to remove sucrose and buffer. Five femtomoles of Bovine Serum Albumin (BioRad, Des Plaines, USA) were added to each fraction as a positive control for sample preparation. Proteins were reduced, alkylated, and subsequently digested with rapid trypsin/LysC at a 1:10 enzyme-to-protein ratio (Promega, Madison, USA). Peptides were acidified with formic acid and then desalted on a Bravo AssayMap (Agilent Technologies, Santa Clara, USA) before being injected onto an LC-MS/MS coupling system, consisting of a NanoAcquity LC-system (Waters, Milford, MA, USA) coupled to a Q-Orbitrap (Q-Orbitrap, Q-Exactive Plus from Thermo Fisher Scientific, Waltham, MA, USA) mass spectrometer equipped with a nanoelectrospray ion source. The database searches were performed using Mascot (version 2.6.2, MatrixScience, London, UK) against an Arabidopsis thaliana protein sequences database from The Arabidopsis Information Resource (TAIR) site (TAIR10 version gene model), where common contaminants and decoy sequences were included (2 x 27,534 protein entries in total). The search was conducted with a mass tolerance of 15 ppm in MS mode and 0.07 Da in MS/MS mode. One missed cleavage of trypsin was allowed. Carbamidomethylation of cysteine residues was set as a fixed modification, while oxidation of methionine residues and acetylation of the proteins’ N-termini were set as variable modifications. Identification results were validated using Proline software (http://proline.profiproteomics.fr/) and only PSMs with a rank score of one were retained. The False Discovery Rate (FDR) was optimized to be below 1% at the level of PSMs using Mascot E-value and below 1% at the protein level using Mascot scores, with the requirement of more than one specific peptide. The protein abundances of RPS (ribosomal protein S), RPL (ribosomal protein L), and RPP (ribosomal protein P) ribosomal proteins were estimated using weighted spectral counts. Detailed sample preparation and LC-MS/MS protocols, as well as data analysis workflows, are provided in Supplementary Information 3 and data 1.

draft: In vitro starch digestibility (IVSD) was conducted using the method outlined by [Author Reference]. This process involved dissolving 5 mg of the sample in 1 mL of 0.2 mol/L phosphate buffer (pH 5.9) to create a suspension. Porcine pancreatic alpha-amylase (20 mg) was suspended in 50 mL of the same buffer. Then, 0.5 mL of the enzyme suspension was added to the sample suspension, followed by incubation at 37 °C for 2 hours. Subsequently, the sample suspension was analyzed for reducing sugar content using a Nelson-Somogyi alkaline copper reduction method. For this analysis, the homogenized sample (5 mg) was mixed with 450 μL of deionized water and 500 μL of copper solution (a mixture of 4 g copper sulphate, 0.185 g sodium sulphate, 23.96 g sodium carbonate, 15.96 g sodium bicarbonate, and 12.14 g sodium potassium tartrate in 1000 mL of distilled water). The mixture was heated in a boiling water bath for 60 minutes and then cooled to 25 °C. The mixture was subsequently reacted with 500 μL of asenolymolybdate solution (an aqueous solution of 49.43 g ammonium molybdate tetrahydrate, 5.93 g sodium asenyladiabasicheptahydrate, and 756 mmol/L sulphuric acid in 1000 mL of distilled water). The content of reducing sugars was determined by measuring the absorbance at 546 nm using a spectrophotometer (model number V-200-RS LW, Germany), against a standard curve containing glucose monohydrate concentrations of 0, 40, 80, 120, 160, and 200 μg in 500 μL deionized water. The degree of hydrolysis (DH) in percentage was calculated by finding the difference between the reducing value of the enzyme blank and the total carbohydrate content of the equivalent sample, then dividing that difference by the difference between the total carbohydrate content of the equivalent sample and the enzyme blank content, and finally multiplying by 100. To summarize, the IVSD was performed by dissolving the sample in a phosphate buffer, adding the amylase, and incubating it at a specific temperature. The reducing sugar content was measured using a Nelson-Somogyi alkaline copper reduction method, and the hydrolysis degree was determined by comparing the absorbance values against a calibration curve.

draft: To determine the Construct Validity (CVI) of the tool, the following steps were taken: 1. **Score Analysis**: The percentage of respondents who gave scores of 3 or 4 for each of the options in the categories of "relevance," "clarity," and "simplicity" were calculated. 2. **Comment and Modification**: Following this analysis, respondents were asked to comment on whether they needed to delete, modify, or add phrases to the tool based on the Waltz-Basel (2005) CVI framework. 3. **Tool Modification**: Based on the comments and feedback, the tool was then modified accordingly. 4. **Student Feedback**: After the modification, the modified tool was given to a group of students. The students were asked to provide their views on the comprehensiveness of the content, the clarity of the phrases, and the simplicity of the content. To further assess the construct validity of the research tool, a stratified random method was used to select 200 students. This method ensured an equitable distribution of the sample across different groups. The exploratory factor analysis (EFA) was then conducted on the responses from these students to validate the research tool's construct validity.

draft: In the field of genomic medicine, genetic testing and molecular analysis play a crucial role in the diagnosis of various disorders. Genomic medicine is a growing medical discipline that utilizes genetic information about an individual to inform clinical care and health policies. Genetic testing can include targeted DNA sequencing (employing the Sanger method) and next-generation sequencing (NGS), which can further include whole exome sequencing. NGS is particularly useful for designing gene panels that can include different combinations of genes. In cases involving hereditary periodic fever syndromes, targeted DNA sequencing, such as testing for mutations in the MEFV gene for familial Mediterranean fever (FMF), is typically ordered when clinically indicated. However, the clinical presentations of autoinflammatory diseases often overlap, necessitating a broader gene panel. For such complex cases with unclear causes or for research purposes, whole exome sequencing is employed. Genetic panel testing frequently employs NGS for its comprehensive gene profiling capabilities.

draft: In the latest issue of the KI Reports, Chen et al. investigated the incidence, risk factors, and prognosis of acute kidney injury (AKI) following acute decompensated heart failure (ADHF) using comprehensive electronic health data from seven hospitals in Taiwan. After excluding patients on maintenance dialysis and those suffering from another significant insult like sepsis or urinary obstruction, the team identified 7,519 adults hospitalized for ADHF over a ten-year period. Among these, 678 patients (9%) developed in-hospital AKI, and 1,592 patients (21%) progressed to acute kidney disease (AKD), as defined by persistent kidney dysfunction relative to the baseline at or closest to three months post-hospitalization. Subsequently, the authors identified key predictors of AKD, including sex, diabetes, AKI stage, pre-hospitalization serum creatinine (SCr) levels, hemoglobin, albumin, and B-type natriuretic peptide (BNP), as well as the use of inotropic and high-dose intravenous diuretics. For the composite outcome of stage 3 AKD and death, the risk factors differed only in age and pre-hospitalization blood urea nitrogen (BUN), with diabetes and chronic kidney disease being replaced. Over a five-year follow-up period, AKD was associated with an increased risk of all-cause death (hazard ratio, HR 1.32 [95% confidence interval, CI 1.17–1.49]) and major adverse kidney events (HR 1.30 [95% CI 1.21–1.40]). Finally, the researchers developed prognostic scoring models with sufficiently high concordance statistics (c-statistics) for any-stage AKD (0.73 [95% CI 0.71–0.74]) and for the composite outcome of stage 3 AKD and death (0.81 [95% CI 0.79–0.82]).

draft: ### Clear Explanation of the Importance of Well-Maintained Registries for Rare Disease Research #### Importance of Well-Maintained Registries Well-maintained registries are fundamental for rare disease research. Without a structured and collaborative approach to collecting and organizing laboratory and clinical data, it becomes challenging to provide comprehensive natural history data. This data is crucial for planning and interpreting clinical trials that evaluate new therapies for rare and orphan diseases. #### Natural History Data Natural history data, which encompasses the progression of a disease over time, is essential for understanding how diseases develop and how treatments affect patients. This information is particularly important for rare and orphan diseases where treatments are often lacking, leading to a significant unmet medical need. #### Value of Natural History Data Natural history data serves multiple purposes. It informs the design of clinical trials, providing a baseline that ensures the effectiveness and safety of new therapies. Additionally, it helps researchers understand how patients respond to treatments, thus improving the clinical evaluation and outcome prediction. #### Benchmarks for Patient Outcomes These data also serve as important benchmarks for measuring the effectiveness of treatments on patients once they start receiving them. This ensures that patients receive the best possible care and allows for continuous improvement in treatment efficacy. #### Acknowledgment of Efforts We appreciate the dedication of the authors and their colleagues who have contributed to this important data analysis and presentation. Their work underscores the critical importance of registry maintenance for advancing rare disease research and improving patient care. ### Summary Well-maintained registries are essential for rare disease research. They provide natural history data that are vital for planning and interpreting clinical trials, informing treatment efficacy, and ensuring patient outcomes are accurately measured. The efforts of the authors and their colleagues are commendable and underscore the significance of registry maintenance in advancing rare disease treatment and care.

Only through organized and collaborative collection of laboratory and clinical data can we provide natural history data to inform the planning and interpretation of well-designed clinical trials that evaluate the novel therapies desperately needed for so many rare and orphan diseases. These data also provide important benchmarks for the outcome of patients once on treatments. We appreciate the authors’ dedication to their patients and colleagues, illustrated through this important data analysis and presentation.

draft: Our objective is to elucidate the specific factors that prompted the ancient individuals of the R. nuchalis Group to utilize the larvae of lampyrine fireflies as a source of toxin. This study posited that R. chiwen species distinguishes between BD fireflies and non-BD fireflies through chemical means. Our behavioral tests confirm this hypothesis. Furthermore, we hypothesized that R. chiwen detects BDs as a chemical indicator of the toxin source. However, our findings did not fully support this prediction: R. chiwen exhibited a moderate preference for a single BD compound, cinobufagin, but showed a strong preference for BD fireflies. Consequently, we suspect that the primary chemical cues involved in R. chiwen's active response may include multiple compounds of BDs. It is also possible that the ancestral species of the R. nuchalis Group recognized chemical substances shared between toads and lampyrine fireflies, which facilitated the use of lampyrine fireflies as a toxin source. In this scenario, given R. chiwen's reliance on BD sources, we hypothesize that it might have lost its response to these common substances due to the toad stimulus. Alternatively, the firefly-eating snakes may have developed a preference for other surface chemicals that are not present in toads. However, considering that toads and fireflies are the only known or suspected animals with biologically produced bufadienolides (BDs), and given the low probability of such a coincidental shift between these two species, this alternate possibility is unlikely. Future studies of R. chiwen's response to multiple BD compounds and investigation into other common chemicals shared by toads and lampyrine fireflies are necessary.
human: Our ultimate goal is to clarify the factors that have induced the ancient species of the R. nuchalis Group to exploit larvae of lampyrine fireflies as the toxin source. In this study, we hypothesized that R. chiwen chemically distinguishes BD fireflies from non-BD fireflies. Our behavioral tests supported this hypothesis. We also predicted that extant R. chiwen detects BDs as the chemical cue of toxin source. However, our results did not fully support this prediction: R. chiwen showed only a medium chemical preference for a single BD compound (cinobufagin), but showed a strong preference for BD fireflies. Thus, we presume that the possible chemical cues that may be involved in the active response of R. chiwen would be multiple compounds of BDs. It is also possible that the ancestral species of the R. nuchalis Group recognized chemical substances other than BDs that are common to toads and lampyrine fireflies, and the presence of those common substances may have facilitated the new exploitation of lampyrine fireflies as the toxin source. In this case, as implied by the low response to the toad stimulus, R. chiwen, which relies on fireflies as the toxin source, would subsequently have lost the response to such chemical substances. Another possibility is that the firefly-eating snakes have evolved preference to some other surface chemicals that are not present in toads. However, we think this possibility is unlikely considering that toads and fireflies are the only animals that are presently known or suspected to possess BDs , and thus the chance of a coincidental shift between them would be extremely low. Future studies of the chemical response of species in the R. nuchalis Group to multiple BDs and investigation of chemical substances other than BDs that may be common to toads and lampyrine fireflies are necessary.

draft: In our national survey among early career pharmacists, we collected essential evidence and feedback on the recommended credit hour values for various educational modules and knowledge areas. Our findings indicate a need to recalibrate the educational focus to better align with contemporary professional development goals. Internationally, there is a trend toward shifting the curriculum from one centered on products, medications, and manufacturing to a patient and therapy-centered approach. Our national survey results on the reallocation of credit hour values echo similar European changes in the 'medical sciences' and 'chemical sciences' course credit ratios. Studies among pharmacists and pharmacy students from Europe and the Eastern Mediterranean Region highlight a need for more practice-based training and curriculum modernization. Perception surveys conducted in countries such as Egypt, Sudan, Qatar, Kuwait, Pakistan, and Saudi Arabia demonstrated that participants were dissatisfied with the curriculum, viewing it as outdated and disconnected from daily pharmacy practices (including complementary and alternative medicine, clinical skills, pharmaco-economics, and social pharmacy). Arakawa et al. also reported that similar curriculum trends, with a chemistry-focused approach and recommended modifications, are prevalent in Bosnia and Herzegovina, Croatia, Austria, and Iceland.

Aligned with the international professional development goals, educational content should shift from ‘product-, medication- and manufacturing- centered’ curricula to ‘patient and therapy-centered education’ . Our national survey findings on the recommended reallocation of credit hour values correspond with the European shift in the ‘medical sciences’/’chemical sciences’ courses credit value ratio described by. draft: ### Explanation of Recruitment and Preparations for Departure In the aftermath of the Battle of Bunker Hill in June, the American camps surrounding Boston were facing significant inactivity. Many units stationed within these camps were growing weary of garrison life and yearned for the prospect of engaging in direct action. **Selection of the Expedition Force** Lieutenant Colonel Henry Arnold chose a force of 750 men from a pool of volunteers who expressed interest in the proposed expedition. These volunteers were further divided into three battalions: 1. **Battalion 1**: Commanded by Lieutenant Colonel Roger Enos. 2. **Battalion 2**: Led by Lieutenant Colonel Christopher Greene. 3. **Battalion 3**: Under the command of Daniel Morgan, it included three companies of Continental riflemen—250 men—together known as the Virginia and Pennsylvania Rifle Regiment. These frontier riflemen, drawn from the Virginia and Pennsylvania wilderness regions, were particularly suited to combat in wooded and difficult terrain. They had already been causing issues near Boston due to their disruptive actions. A total of approximately 1,100 men were assembled for the expedition. **Notable Volunteers** Several prominent figures among the volunteers would later become significant figures during and after the war: - Aaron Burr - Return Joseph Meigs - Henry Dearborn - John Joseph Henry **Concerns and Preparations** Both George Washington and Arnold were concerned about the support for their expedition from the Native American population and Canadians. Specifically, they worried about whether the local Indian tribes and Canadians would either offer support or opposition to their campaign. **Abenaki Scouts and Guides** On August 30, Washington wrote to General Schuyler about a meeting he had with an Abenaki chief. According to the chief, "the Indians of Canada in general, and also the French, are greatly in our favor, and determined not to act against us." To further support this expedition, four Abenakis accompanied the force as scouts and guides.
human: Recruitment and preparations for departure Because there had been little direct action at Boston after the Battle of Bunker Hill in June, many units stationed in the American camps besieging the town were bored with garrison life and eager for action. Arnold selected a force of 750 men from the large number who expressed interest in the proposed expedition. Most of these were divided into two battalions: one commanded by Lieutenant Colonel Roger Enos and the other by Lieutenant Colonel Christopher Greene. The rest were placed in a third battalion under Daniel Morgan that included three companies—250 men—of Continental riflemen from Virginia and the Pennsylvania Rifle Regiment. These frontiersmen, from the Virginia and Pennsylvania wilderness, were better suited to wilderness combat than to a siege, and had been causing trouble since arriving outside Boston. The entire force numbered about 1,100. Among the volunteers were other men who rose to later prominence during and after the war, including Aaron Burr, Return J. Meigs, Henry Dearborn, and John Joseph Henry. Washington and Arnold were concerned about Indian support for (or opposition to) the effort, as well as the reception Arnold's forces might receive from the Canadians once they arrived near the Saint Lawrence River. On August 30, Washington wrote to General Schuyler of a meeting he held with an Abenaki chief, "[The chief] says the Indians of Canada in general, and also the French, are greatly in our favor, and determined not to act against us." Four Abenakis accompanied the expedition as scouts and guides.

draft: Previous studies suggested that similar to breast cancer and melanoma, a radio-guided sentinel lymph node biopsy (SLNB) with sentinel lymph node (SLN) frozen section can help identify patients who have sentinel lymph node metastasis (SLNM) and that a lymph node dissection (LND) of the neck compartments should be performed in such cases. However, Carcoforo et al. highlighted a significant false negative rate (FNR) for isolated sentinel lymph node biopsies and the risk of remnant lymph node metastasis. Consequently, they propose a new concept of radio-guided surgery for the staging of patients with papillary thyroid carcinoma (PTC). This concept suggests using sentinel lymph node biopsy (SLNB) as a guide to selectively perform a lymph node dissection (LND) of the sentinel lymph node compartment without regard to the status of the sentinel lymph node. This approach may be beneficial for the final staging of the disease and the reduction of persistent disease.

draft: In this study, innovative nanocomposites comprising Sn–SiO2@TiO2(B) were successfully prepared through a straightforward chemical method. The research utilized rice husk-derived SiO2 and tin nanoparticles, which were evenly attached to the surface of TiO2(B) nanorods. The SiO2 and Sn nanoparticles, ranging in size from 5 to 10 nanometers, exhibited excellent distribution. Compared to other products, the Sn–SiO2@TiO2(B) electrode demonstrated superior electrochemical properties for lithium-ion batteries. Specifically, the specific capacity of Sn–SiO2@TiO2(B) with good cycle stability was 143.03 milliamps per gram (mA h g⁻¹), which was notably higher than that of TiO2(B)-based products synthesized in the same study. Additionally, the internal resistance of the Sn–SiO2@TiO2(B) electrode was relatively low (∼250 ohms). The research elucidated the mechanism of how the self-assembly of SiO2 and Sn nanoparticles on TiO2(B) enhances battery performance. This study significantly contributes to improving the electrochemical characteristics of TiO2(B)-based anode materials. Consequently, Sn–SiO2@TiO2(B) nanocomposites could become promising candidates for use as fast-charging anodes in lithium-ion batteries in the future.

draft: ### Analysis of Survey Responses To analyze the survey responses, we conducted a chi-squared test (χ²) using SPSS v25 software (IBM, Armonk, NY, USA). The chi-squared test was applied to compare differences between physicians and the general public. ### Consideration of Design Effects We also accounted for design effects in the survey by calculating the effective sample size for each survey. This step was crucial for ensuring that our sample sizes reflected the true population structure accurately. ### Adjustment for Sampling Biases To further address potential biases due to sociodemographic differences, we compared respondents and nonrespondents to ensure the sample was representative. Specifically, we examined sociodemographic factors including: - **Sex** - **Age** - **Level of Education** - **Years of Experience** ### Ensuring Representativeness To achieve this, we found that there were no significant differences between respondents and nonrespondents in terms of the sociodemographic factors mentioned above. This validation was performed based on: - **Sex** - **Age** - **Level of Education** - **Years of Experience** ### Statistical Significance All reported P values are based on two-sided tests. We considered the results significant if the P-values were less than 0.05.

All reported P values are based on 2-sided tests and were considered significant when below 0.05.

draft: Patient One is an 80-year-old male with a history of cardiopathy who underwent a left total hip replacement due to primary osteoarthritis. In the third year following the procedure, he experienced a Vancouver B2 periprosthetic femoral fracture, necessitating a revision of his total hip replacement. One year post-revision, he was transferred to our center due to chronic prosthetic joint infection (PJI). Upon presentation, the patient exhibited a productive wound discharge, with serum C-reactive protein (CRP) at 20.4 mg/L and an erythrocyte sedimentation rate (ESR) of 22 mm/h. Radiographs initially showed proximal femoral diffuse osteomyelitis and signs of non-union from his previous periprosthetic fracture. Samples of periprosthetic tissue and wound drainage were collected and cultured, revealing the presence of *Pseudomonas aeruginosa* in both. Given this multidrug-resistant bacterial infection, we elected for a one-stage exchange revision arthroplasty with a megaprosthesis: a Stryker GMRS® proximal femoral prosthesis (Kalamazoo, MI, USA) and a trident® acetabular shell with a constrained liner (Stryker, Kalamazoo, MI, USA). The patient received antibiotics, including 12 days of intravenous Ceftazidime and Ciprofloxacin, to reduce the bacterial load before the procedure. One of six intraoperative cultures also tested positive for *P. aeruginosa*, and histological analysis confirmed findings consistent with prosthetic joint infection, including greater than five polymorphonuclear leukocytes (PMNs) per high-power field observed at 400× magnification. The patient was hospitalized for a total of 19 days following the revision arthroplasty, receiving intravenous antibiotics for the duration. Post-discharge, the patient was prescribed oral Ciprofloxacin for six weeks. At the six-year follow-up, there were no clinical, laboratory, or radiological signs of infection present.

The initial radiograph showed proximal femoral diffuse osteomyelitis and signs of non-union of his previous periprosthetic fracture . At the six-year follow-up, the patient did not show any clinical, laboratory, or radiological signs of infection .

draft: The comparison between films synthesized using the solvent casting method and those manufactured by electrospinning reveals significant differences in their microstructures. Solvent cast films exhibit an undefined structure with numerous discontinuities and non-uniform pore distribution, resulting in a microstructure that is neither uniform nor homogeneous. On the other hand, electrospun films consist of entangled fibers that are uniformly distributed, creating a visibly homogeneous microstructure. Porous surfaces generally have a positive influence on cellular feedback. Specifically, it was observed that microgrooved substrates of an implant surface did not promote cell proliferation or osteogenic differentiation of hMSCs into osteoblasts. However, these microgrooved substrates did favor the migration of collective cells, thereby promoting wound healing. To engineer functional tissue equivalents that closely mimic the unique properties of native tissues, it is necessary to develop strategies for reproducing the complex, highly organized structure of these tissues. As discussed in subsequent sections, both solvent cast and electrospun films promote cell growth and improve cellular response compared to titanium substrates, which are the traditional orthopedic metal. However, electrospun substrates have a distinct advantage in enhancing cellular feedback. They promote better development (morphology), division, and multiplication of cells. In summary, while solvent cast films show non-uniform microstructures, electrospun films exhibit uniform, homogeneous structures. Both types of films enhance cell growth and response compared to titanium substrates. However, electrospun films offer superior cellular feedback, particularly in terms of cell division and multiplication.

Initially, after the first month of treatment, the average CT enhancement rate of sacral or pelvic lesions still remained significantly higher compared to limb bone lesions. draft: ### Enhanced Delivery of Drugs to the Eye Using Nanoparticles The eye is protected by complex anatomical and physiological barriers, which prevent many drugs from effectively penetrating to the inner tissues. Consequently, conventional eyedrops are often insufficient for delivering therapeutic levels of drugs to treat posterior eye diseases such as Age-Related Macular Degeneration (AMD), diabetic retinopathy, glaucoma, and uveitis. However, other administration routes, although promising, come with significant drawbacks, including high side effects. Recent developments in drug delivery systems, specifically lipid nanoparticles (SLNs and NLCs), have shown significant promise in overcoming these limitations. These nanosystems offer several advantages: 1. **Physiological and Biodegradable Composition:** The lipid nanoparticles are composed of materials that are naturally compatible with the body, ensuring minimal biocompatibility issues. 2. **Good Ocular Tolerance:** These nanoparticles have shown good tolerability when administered via the eye, minimizing adverse effects. 3. **Up-scalable Production:** The ability to produce these nanoparticles in large quantities makes them cost-effective and feasible for widespread use. A substantial number of lipid nanoparticles have been developed and are encapsulating various drugs, providing a new avenue for treating posterior eye diseases. These nanosystems open up the possibility of using safe and effective drug delivery systems to treat conditions such as AMD, diabetic retinopathy, glaucoma, and uveitis. Nevertheless, more extensive preclinical and clinical data are required to validate these lipid nanoparticles as suitable treatment options for the posterior ocular segments. This research will be essential to ensure the safety and efficacy of these nanosystems when used to target the back part of the eye.

However, there are other administration routes that allow us to reach inner tissues, but these routes present important drawbacks, including high side effects. In recent decades, lipid nanoparticles (SLNs and NLCs) have been designed to enhance bioavailability of the drugs into the inner tissues of the eye. Several advantages of these nanosystems include their physiological and biodegradable composition, good ocular tolerance and the possibility of upscale production. A high number of SLNs and NLCs have been developed, encapsulating several drugs, which opens a window for the treatment of posterior eye diseases employing safe and effective drug delivery systems. Furthermore, additional preclinical and clinical data regarding lipid nanoparticles for the posterior ocular segments will be necessary in order to obtain suitable treatments targeted towards the back part of the eye.

draft: Monogenic hereditary periodic fever syndromes encompass Familial Mediterranean Fever (FMF), cryopyrin-associated periodic syndrome (CAPS), hyper IgD syndrome/mevalonate kinase deficiency (MVK), and TNF receptor-associated periodic syndrome (TRAPS). These conditions are inherited in a Mendelian fashion, typically through either autosomal recessive or dominant inheritance. The genetic mutations associated with these syndromes are highly penetrant, with an allele frequency of less than 1% in the general population. However, low-penetrance variants, which may have an allele frequency greater than 5%, can also be identified and pose significant diagnostic challenges. In the cases of FMF and CAPS, low-penetrance genetic variants are detected and utilized for diagnosis when characteristic clinical phenotypes are present. There has been some controversy surrounding this practice. For instance, the MEFV E148Q variant is observed in 4.7% of healthy Caucasians and up to 23% in the Japanese population. This variant, when present in the context of a typical clinical phenotype, supports the diagnosis of FMF. Additionally, the NLRP3 Q703K variant, detected in healthy Caucasians at a frequency of 5–6.5%, may be used to support the diagnosis of CAPS when a proper clinical phenotype is observed. Moreover, in NLRP12-induced autoinflammatory disease, the most common genotype reported is the NLRP12 F402 variant, with a frequency of 5% among healthy Caucasians.

draft: Webster was depicted as malicious, reckless, and willfully evil. Commentators found her crime gruesome and scandalous. Servants were expected to be deferential to their employers. However, her act of extreme violence towards her employer was deeply disquieting. At the time, about 40% of the female labor force was employed as domestic servants across various societal levels, from the wealthiest to respectable working-class families. These servants and employers often lived and worked in close proximity, and the servants' honesty and orderliness were a significant concern. Servants were paid very poorly, which made larceny a persistent temptation. If Webster had successfully completed the deal with Church to sell Thomas's furniture, she would have stood to gain roughly two to three years' worth of wages. The jockeys of the three past Triple Crown winners, Steve Cauthen, Jean Cruguet, and Ron Turcotte, also attended. Cauthen, jockey of Affirmed, stated, "This horse has got a great chance of pulling it off," but added, "you never know, that's why they have to run the race."

Some believed Chagatai, Genghis’s eldest son, would make an excellent successor due to his qualities, but Genghis criticized him for being overly rigid and narrow-minded, perceiving him as exhibiting traits unsuitable for leadership. Genghis also disapproved of Chagatai’s harsh treatment of his half-brother Jochi, whom Chagatai regarded as illegitimate. During a family gathering, Chagatai had called Jochi a “Merkit bastard” and engaged in a physical altercation. Consequently, Genghis excluded Chagatai from the succession. Jochi’s legitimacy was also questioned, but he was not a prime candidate because of rumours surrounding his illegitimacy. Ultimately, Ögedei was appointed as the heir. After Genghis’s death in 1227, Chagatai played a crucial role in stabilizing the empire before Ögedei’s coronation in 1229. Chagatai’s uncle, Tolui, who had also been considered for succession, attempted to seize power. However, numerous loyal followers, including Chagatai himself after his power over Jochi, adhered to Genghis’s wishes. This ensured the stability of the empire. Chagatai presided over the coronation ceremony alongside Tolui and their uncle Temüge, and he remained loyal to Ögedei throughout his reign. draft: The Spectralis High Magnification Module (HMM, Spectralis ®, Heidelberg Engineering, Germany) is a recently introduced imaging modality specifically designed for use with the company's Spectralis confocal scanning laser ophthalmoscope. This module acts as a lens-attachment that enhances the visualization of the retinal photoreceptors mosaic pattern. The HMM is particularly effective in providing a detailed view of ocular fundus structures without requiring pupillary dilation. To achieve optimal results, the pupil size is minimized to approximately 1.5 mm, and the room is kept dim to minimize ambient light. The HMM magnifies the fundus image, with a field of view measuring approximately 8° × 8° (equivalent to about 2500 μm × 2500 μm). Using this module, specific regions of interest on the fundus can be identified and magnified to examine the microstructure of the cone mosaic. The HMM offers several advantages. Firstly, its application is straightforward and suitable for clinical settings. Secondly, it significantly reduces the time needed to acquire images, and importantly, it ensures consistent results due to its high reproducibility.

draft: Hodkinson et al.'s study published in this issue of the AJTCCM represents the initial examination of the impact of hospitalization for severe COVID-19 on mental health in a South African context. The study involved 21 participants, all of whom had survived high care or intensive care unit (ICU) admissions and were interviewed in general wards prior to discharge. While the study was small, it focused on patients who experienced severe respiratory compromise. Specifically, 18 patients required high-flow nasal oxygenation (HFNO) and five patients required mechanical ventilation for a mean duration of 15 days (with a range from 5 to 27 days). The mortality rate for patients with severe SARS-CoV2 in South Africa is particularly high, and this is more pronounced in resource-constrained settings where intubation is delayed due to a shortage of ICU beds. At Groote Schuur Hospital in Cape Town, during the first wave of the pandemic, 293 patients were offered HFNO. Of these, 156 (53%) failed to respond to treatment, and 82.7% of these patients subsequently passed away. Given that this study was conducted during the initial wave of the pandemic in South Africa, it is plausible that patients who were admitted were not fully aware of the low chances of survival. Consequently, the fear that all patients would die, witnessing others in their care die, would have had a significant psychological impact. Despite being discharged and feeling relatively confident of survival, the psychological scars these patients experienced persisted and would likely continue for some time.

draft: Our study examined the impact of IPoC (Interventional Protection of Cardiopulmonary Circulation) on intestinal ischemia-reperfusion (I/R) injury in an experimental rat model using five groups with three distinct IPoC models. We focused on the early minutes of reperfusion. Specifically, after 30 minutes of global ischemia induced by laparotomy and application of the superior mesenteric artery, we observed the following interventions: 1. **Control Group (No Intervention)**: The rats underwent global ischemia and were reperfused for 120 minutes without any intervention. 2. **IPoC-3 Group**: These rats received three cycles of 10 seconds of reperfusion-reocclusion over a total of 1 minute. 3. **IPoC-6 Group**: The rats were treated with six cycles of 10 seconds of reperfusion-reocclusion, amounting to a total of 2 minutes. 4. **Sham Group (Laparotomy Only)**: Only the laparotomy was performed without further intervention. Our findings indicated that the use of IPoC models attenuated the progression of infarct area, serum total creatine kinase (CK), lipid peroxidation, and tissue malondialdehyde (MDA) levels, as well as improved ileum morphology and histopathological scores. Notably, the IPoC models, particularly the IPoC-6 model, significantly reduced post-ischemic findings by decreasing intestinal tissue malondialdehyde (MDA), serum total creatine kinase (CK) activity, and histopathological scores according to the Chiu classification. These results suggest that IPoC exerted a protective effect on the intestinal mucosa by diminishing mesenteric oxidative generation, lipid peroxidation, and neutrophil accumulation. Importantly, the six-cycle algorithm demonstrated the best protection against intestinal I/R injury.

We reported that the deterioration in the infarct area, serum total creatine kinase (CK); lipid peroxidation, tissue MDA; and ileum morphology, histopathological scoring; was attenuated with the use of IPoC models. Of note, the IPoC, especially IPoC-6, was effective in attenuating post-ischemic findings by decreasing the intestinal tissue MDA, serum total CK activity, the inflammation scores with total histopathologic injury scores of Chiu classification. Herewith, the IPoC models exerted a protective effect on the intestinal mucosa by reducing the mesenteric oxidant generation, lipid peroxidation, and neutrophil accumulation. Last but not least, the six-cycle algorithm demonstrated best protection for the intestinal I/R injury.

draft: In the ecological environment, the dog conch inhabits muddy sand bottoms and seagrass and algae beds along the shores of both insular and continental coastlines. It typically shows a preference for major islands and continental coasts over the shores of smaller islands. However, this does not constitute a strict rule. L. canarium has a particular preference for areas with mixed seagrass beds (predominantly Halophila seagrass) and sediments rich in organic matter. Conversely, it avoids environments rich in Enhalus acoroides, a large seagrass species indigenous to the coastal waters of the Indo-Pacific. The dog conch is observed in both littoral and sublittoral zones, occurring from near the surface down to a depth of approximately 55 meters (180 feet). It is commonly found in large colonies and is relatively abundant wherever it occurs.

draft: El Greco's approach emphasized the primacy of imagination and intuition over the subjective nature of creation. This fundamental principle set the stage for his unique style, which rejected the classicist criteria of measure and proportion. For El Greco, the supreme objective of art was to achieve grace, which he attained effortlessly by addressing the most intricate challenges. He viewed color as the most significant and least controllable element of painting, asserting that it held greater importance than form. Francisco Pacheco, a painter and theoretician who encountered El Greco in 1611, described the artist's preference for bold, unaltered colors—a display of his skill. Additionally, Pacheco noted that El Greco believed in the necessity of extensive retouching and repainting to ensure broad areas of color accurately reflected the flat, natural hues observed.

He believed that grace is the supreme quest of art, but the painter achieves grace only by managing to solve the most complex problems with ease. draft: The current study focused on patients with left-sided motor area gliomas, either with or without the occurrence of ISE. We considered only 28 of the 246 subregions of the brain network (also known as the brainnetome 246 atlas). ISE typically occurs around the stimulation point and is most commonly found in or near the motor cortex (or the supplementary motor area) of the brain. The motor-sensory network is particularly susceptible to major epileptic seizures. Controlling the mass effect caused by the tumor during the network analysis is a significant challenge. The tumor's compression, invasion, or infiltration can alter the surrounding anatomical structure, which in turn can affect the normalization procedure. Consequently, this can lead to inaccuracies in the identification of regions of interest and in atlas-based fiber tracking. To address these issues, we developed a tumor-overlapping map, and any subregions that overlap with this map were excluded from the analysis. Consequently, the number of subregions included in the final analysis was reduced to 22.

draft: Exploring the subjective nature of mental health through biological perspectives is likely to significantly advance psychiatry, while simultaneously presenting numerous ethical challenges. The World Health Organization’s constitution outlines our mission as health care providers to promote “complete physical, mental, and social well-being.” Individuals from various religious backgrounds, political affiliations, and philosophical persuasions generally agree on concepts of good and bad, and the judgment that happiness and well-being are positive, whereas pain and suffering are negative. Psychiatry is the medical field that directly addresses the biological underpinnings of these mental states. Ethical quandaries will inevitably arise if our technology advances sufficiently to replicate these experiences in a laboratory setting, detached from the millions of years of evolutionary processes needed to create living beings. While our current ignorance in psychiatry is undoubtedly frustrating, for the time being, we are spared the need to confront these dilemmas.
human: Understanding the subjective reality of the mind in biological terms would doubtless lead to huge advances in psychiatry, as well as to ethical dilemmas. The constitution of the World Health Organization describes our goal as health care providers to promote “complete physical, mental and social well-being”. People of nearly all religions, political affiliations, and philosophical persuasions can agree on the general concepts of good and bad, as well as the value judgments that happiness and well-being are good things and the opposite, pain and suffering, are bad. Psychiatry is the only branch of medicine that directly targets the biological substrates corresponding to these states of mind. Difficult ethical questions would surely emerge if and when our technology becomes sufficiently advanced to reproduce such experiential phenomena in the lab, separate from living beings whose creation according to theory required millions of years of evolution. As frustrating as our ignorance in psychiatry may be, at least for the time being, we are spared from having to confront these dilemmas.

draft: Acute kidney injury (AKI) during and following hospitalizations for acute decompensated heart failure (ADHF) is a common and well-established risk factor for adverse clinical outcomes. AKI is typically quantified based on serum creatinine (SCr) values relative to a baseline, with specific changes occurring within the first seven days. However, this straightforward approach is increasingly recognized as insufficient, as AKI does not always manifest in the same manner. During ADHF, AKI can be categorized into different pathophysiological pathways. AKI can serve as the underlying cause of heart failure (type 3 cardiorenal syndrome), a subsequent consequence of ADHF (especially in cases of cardiogenic shock, type 1 cardiorenal syndrome), or a collateral effect of a systemic disease (such as sepsis), adversely affecting both the kidneys and the heart (type 5 cardiorenal syndrome). There is growing appreciation that AKI characterized by only slight increases in SCr (i.e., stage 1 AKI, with SCr elevating by no more than 0.3 mg/dl) may not be linked to significant long-term adverse outcomes in various clinical settings. This is particularly relevant in ADHF, where acute increases in SCr following the initiation of heart failure treatments such as renin-angiotensin system inhibitors and diuretics do not necessarily predict adverse outcomes but may instead indicate a beneficial hemodynamic response.
human: Acute kidney injury (AKI) during and after hospitalizations for acute decompensated heart failure (ADHF) is a common and established risk factor for adverse clinical outcomes. Although AKI is most often defined by serum creatinine (SCr) values relative to a baseline (where specific changes are documented or presumed to have occurred within 7 days), there is increasing understanding that not all AKI is equal. For example, AKI in the context of ADHF can be delineated into various pathophysiological pathways. AKI can be the underlying cause of heart failure (type 3 cardiorenal syndrome), the sequela of ADHF (especially in cardiogenic shock, type 1 cardiorenal syndrome), an unfortunate collateral event from a systemic disease (e.g. sepsis) with detrimental effects on both kidneys and the heart (type 5 cardiorenal syndrome), or some combination of the above. There is also growing recognition that AKI consisting of only small changes in SCr (i.e. stage 1 AKI, meeting only a 0.3 mg/dl increase in SCr) may not be associated with important long-term adverse outcomes in many clinical scenarios. This is especially relevant in ADHF, where acute increases in SCr that occur after initiation of heart failure therapies such as renin-angiotensin system inhibitors and diuretics do not necessary portend adverse outcomes and may signify a therapeutic hemodynamic effect.

draft: ### Importance of Prevention Strategies in Hospital Infection Control In hospitals, prevention strategies are crucial for controlling the spread of infections. Antiseptic molecules play a significant role in this process, particularly in managing methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA) and other multidrug-resistant Gram-negative bacteria, such as those found on skin, wounds, and mucous membranes. #### Chlorhexidine (CHX) and Its Use Chlorhexidine (CHX) has been found to be highly effective in controlling the spread of these bacteria. It is recommended for both preventive and decolonization strategies. Additionally, octenidine (OCT) has shown excellent efficacy in eliminating multi-drug resistant (MDR) bacteria, including Gram-negative pathogens. ### Study on the Efficacy of Octenidine (OCT) A recent study evaluated the efficacy of octenidine (OCT) against multi-drug resistant Gram-negative bacteria, including several clinically significant pathogens. These pathogens were selected due to their multidrug resistance phenotype, which includes resistance to β-lactams, aminoglycosides, and fluoroquinolones. The key pathogens studied were: - **E. coli** - **K. pneumoniae** - **E. cloacae** - **Acinetobacter baumannii** - **Pseudomonas aeruginosa** #### Key Findings The study found that OCT demonstrated highly effective activity against these MDR bacteria at clinically relevant concentrations.
human: In general, prevention strategies within the hospital are a key element in infection control. Use of antiseptic molecules contributes significantly to the control of dissemination of methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA), but also to control of (multidrug resistant) Gram-negative bacteria on skin, wounds and mucous membranes. In that context, use of chlorhexidine (CHX) is recommended and CHX is being heavily used for prevention and for decolonization strategies. Likewise, octenidine (OCT) is another antiseptic molecule that shows excellent efficacy in eradicating MDR bacteria. We recently performed a study evaluating the efficacy of OCT against MDR Gram negatives (including E. coli, K. pneumoniae, E. cloacae, Acinetobacter baumannii and Pseudomonas aeruginosa). These clinically-relevant Gram-negative pathogens were chosen for their multidrug resistance phenotype, including resistance to ß-lactams, aminoglycosides, and fluoroquinolones. OCT activity was proven to be extremely efficient against these MDR bacteria at clinically-relevant concentrations.

Unlike the Diagnostic and Statistical Manual of Mental Disorders (DSM) and the International Classification of Diseases (ICD), which focus on symptom clustering and descriptive nosology, RDoC centers on specific brain functions and neural circuitry. Therizinosaurs are primarily known from the Cretaceous in Asia and North America but have controversial remains from other periods and regions. In 2010, Zanno proposed two scenarios for the paleobiogeographic distribution of therizinosaurs. One hypothesis posits that they dispersed through vicariance, implying their presence in regions that later became Asia and North America before the rifting events that divided these areas in the Late Triassic. Alternatively, Zanno suggested that basal therizinosaurs could have dispersed between Asia and North America via Europe after the rifting but before the middle Barremian period; this temporary land bridge, active between 132 to 138 million years ago, could explain the morphological divergence between Falcarius and Beipiaosaurus, the latter being from Asia. Recent findings, including Nothronychus, a derived therizinosaurid closely related to Asian genera, found in North America during the Turonian stage of the early Late Cretaceous, also support the existence of a land bridge between North America and Asia during the Late Early Cretaceous, indicating a faunal interchange between these continents during this era.

draft: Panzer Dragoon Saga, known in Japan as Azel: Panzer Dragoon RPG, is a 1998 role-playing video game developed by Team Andromeda and published by Sega for the Sega Saturn. The game introduces RPG elements such as random encounters, semi-turn-based battles, and free-roaming exploration, replacing the rail shooter gameplay of previous Panzer Dragoon titles. The player controls Edge, a young mercenary who rides a dragon and encounters a mysterious girl from a vanished civilization. Sega commissioned Team Andromeda to create this RPG to compete against the PlayStation and Final Fantasy VII on the Saturn. Development began in early 1995 alongside Panzer Dragoon II Zwei, and the project was marked by challenges and delays. Incorporating the Panzer Dragoon shooting elements with full 3D computer graphics and voice acting pushed the Saturn to its technical limits and strained the team. Two staff members died during development, which the director, Yukio Futatsugi, attributed to stressful working conditions. Sega released Panzer Dragoon Saga in Japan in January 1998 and in the West in April. The game received minimal marketing, leading to low sales, which were attributed to the Saturn's issues, a lack of promotion, low circulation, and Team Andromeda's disinterest in creating a mainstream product. After the release, Sega disbanded the team, and several staff members joined Smilebit, where they developed Panzer Dragoon Orta for the Xbox in 2002. Despite low sales and its cult status, Panzer Dragoon Saga has never been re-released, and English-language copies can fetch more than US$1000 on the secondary market. Many publications have named this game one of the greatest video games of all time.

draft: The binding of integrin receptors and cell recognition motifs triggers the downstream mechanotransduction pathway, which controls how cells behave and function. Integrins transmit information from the extracellular matrix (ECM) to the actomyosin cytoskeleton through focal adhesion complexes. The strength of these forces is determined by the mechanical properties of the ECM, particularly the Young's modulus, which affects how the cell interacts with its environment. The Young's modulus of the ECM varies significantly among different tissues. For instance, skeletal muscle tissue has an intermediate range of stiffness, with a Young's modulus of approximately 10 kPa. Hard bone tissue, on the other hand, has a higher Young's modulus of about 30 to 45 kPa. If the ECM Young's modulus does not match the specific tissue, the cells will not respond to the cues in the ECM, thereby affecting their differentiation and behavior. To control the fate of stem cells, especially when recreating specific tissues, the matrices should be engineered with the appropriate Young's modulus. A landmark study by Engler et al. demonstrated this, showing that mesenchymal stem cells differentiate into specific lineages based on the stiffness of the substrate on which they are cultured. Specifically, when mesenchymal stem cells were cultured on polyacrylamide substrates with a Young's modulus ranging from 8 to 17 kPa, they differentiated into a skeletal muscle phenotype, which aligns well with the stiffness of the native muscle microenvironment. This effect is also observed in three-dimensional (3D) matrices. In these environments, stem cells can reorganize the ECM based on the stiffness of their surrounding matrix. This mechanosensing mechanism involves forces from the cytoskeleton to the adhesive bond, which can be influenced by the composition of the ECM and the expression of particular subsets of integrin heterodimers. In summary, the mechanical properties of the extracellular matrix play a crucial role in controlling cell behavior and differentiation. By engineering the appropriate stiffness of the matrix, it is possible to direct stem cells to specific lineages, thereby enabling the creation of specific tissues.
human: The binding of integrin receptors and cell recognition motifs will induce the downstream mechanotransduction signaling pathway and, consequently, control how the cell behaves and functions . In essence, integrins function by transmitting information from the ECM to the actomyosin cytoskeleton in the cell through the focal adhesion complexes. The amplitude of the forces generated depends on the mechanical properties of the ECM, one important parameter of which is matrix stiffness. Skeletal muscle tissue has an intermediate range of matrix stiffness, with a Young’s modulus value of approximately 10 kPa, while hard bone tissue has a higher Young’s modulus value of approximately 30 to 45 kPa. If the Young’s modulus is not within the range of the specific tissue, the cells will not be able to take on cues from their ECM. In the same vein, matrices should be engineered with the appropriate Young’s modulus value, thus controlling the fate of stem cells when recreating specific tissue. In a landmark study, Engler et al. showed that mesenchymal stem cells differentiate into specific lineages in accordance with the stiffness of the substrate upon which the cells are cultured. Mesenchymal stem cells cultured on polyacrylamide substrates with Young’s moduli ranging between 8–17 kPa were shown to differentiate into a skeletal muscle phenotype, which agrees well with the stiffness of the native muscle microenvironment . Such an effect is also observed for cells cultured in 3D matrices. Interestingly, by sensing the stiffness of the surrounding matrix stem cells can contextually reorganize the ECM to create a local niche. This mechanosensing mechanism involving forces from the cytoskeleton to the adhesive bond is influenced by the ECM composition as well as by the expression of particular subsets of integrin heterodimers.

draft: Long-term exposure to pesticide residues increases the risk for bees. The hazard quotient (HQ) is a method to quantify this risk. The HQ is calculated by dividing the concentration of the contaminant in the beeswax by the LD55 value (the lethal dose that would kill 50% of the test group individuals). HQ evaluates the individual risk posed by a single contaminant to the bees. However, since bees perform various tasks within the colony, they come into contact with different substances depending on their roles. When dealing with multiple contaminants, calculating the HQ helps to comprehend the contribution of individual contaminants to the overall risk to the colony.
human: Long-term contact with pesticide residues exposes bees to a certain risk. One way to quantify the potential risk is to calculate a hazard quotient (HQ). HQ is calculated by dividing the concentration of contaminant in wax with the LD50 value (the concentration that would kill 50% of the test group individuals) of the substance. HQ simply evaluates the risk of individual contaminants to bees. However, depending on their specific tasks in colony, the individual honey bees are in contact with different materials. In the case of multiple contaminants, the calculation of HQ still helps to understand the contribution of individual contaminants to the overall risk.
