draft: To gain a deeper understanding of the structural and interfacial behavior of the as-prepared nanocomposite electrodes, electrical impedance spectroscopy (EIS) was performed at room temperature over a frequency range of 100 kHz to 0.5 Hz. Nyquist plots for the TiO2(B), SiO2@TiO2(B), and Sn–SiO2@TiO2(B) electrodes are depicted in Figure d. At high-to-medium frequencies, the semicircle in the Nyquist plot corresponds to the charge-transfer resistance (Rct) and double-layer capacitance through the electrode-electrolyte interface. At low frequencies, the inclined line corresponds to the Warburg diffusion impedance (Zw) and the diffusion resistance of lithium ions through the solid-state electrodes, as detailed earlier in this section. The charge-transfer resistance (Rct) values of the fabricated electrodes followed this sequence: Sn–SiO2@TiO2(B) (∼250 Ω) < TiO2(B) (∼300 Ω) < SiO2@TiO2(B) (∼400 Ω). This clearly indicates that the Rct of the SiO2@TiO2 electrode is lower than that of TiO2(B) and Sn–SiO2@TiO2(B), suggesting that amorphous silicon dioxide nanoparticles can reduce electrical conductivity. The Nyquist plot at high-to-medium frequencies for the prepared electrodes showed that the interfacial impedance was reduced upon the addition of Sn, indicating that Sn nanoparticles were consistently deposited to serve a conductive purpose. This characteristic could potentially improve electrical conductivity, leading to a decrease in internal resistance and better Li-ion transportation in the composite electrode. Importantly, the pseudocapacitive channel within TiO2(B), according to theoretical analysis, could enhance the faster Li-ion diffusion. Consequently, the Sn–SiO2@TiO2(B) electrode outperforms the other electrodes in reducing interfacial impedance.
human: To study the structural and interfacial behavior of as-prepared nanocomposite electrodes further, electrical impedance spectroscopy (EIS) was performed at room temperature across a frequency range of 100 kHz–0.1 Hz. Nyquist plots of TiO2(B), SiO2@TiO2(B), and Sn–SiO2@TiO2(B) electrodes can be seen in d. The semicircle at high-to-medium frequency corresponded to the charge-transfer resistance (Rct) and double-layer capacitance through the electrode–electrolyte interface, whereas the inclined line at low frequency corresponds to the Warburg diffusion impedance (Zw) and also to the diffusion resistance of lithium ions through the solid-state electrodes described earlier in this section. The Rct values of the fabricated electrode were incremented in the following order: Sn–SiO2@TiO2(B) (∼250 Ω) < TiO2(B) (∼300 Ω) < SiO2@TiO2(B) (∼400 Ω). Obviously, the Rct of the SiO2@TiO2 electrode is lower than that of the TiO2(B) and Sn–SiO2@TiO2(B) electrodes, demonstrating that amorphous SiO2 nanoparticles could decrease electrical conductivity. The semicircle at a high-to-medium frequency of prepared electrodes revealed that interfacial impedance was reduced when Sn was added, implying that Sn nanoparticles were consistently deposited to serve the conductivity. This characteristic could potentially improve electrical contraction, resulting in lower internal resistance and better Li-ion transportation in the composited electrode. draft: Inotersen (Tegsedi) is an antisense oligonucleotide (ASO) that targets the gene encoding transthyretin (TTR) for the treatmenticulo of familial amyloid polyneuropathy (FAP). As the disease advances, patients experience escalating muscle weakness, walking difficulties, balance issues, and sensory loss due to nerve fiber injury. The severity of neurological manifestations in FAP patients can be influenced by the specific genetic mutation type (over 140 TTR genetic mutations have been identified). However, these patients suffer a significant burden on their health-related quality of life (HRQOL). Inotersen, a 20-mer fully phosphorothioate (PS) chimeric gapmer ASO with each terminus modified by 2’-O-methoxyethyl (2’-MOE) sugar, exhibits a knockdown efficiency of 80% in a human TTR Ile84Ser transgenic mouse model. Clinical trials have shown that Inotersen reduces both mutated and wild-type TTR levels in humans and does not have off-target effects. A phase I clinical trial involved 65 healthy volunteers, with four doses of 300 mg subcutaneous (s.c.) Inotersen resulting in a serum TTR reduction of 75%. In a subsequent phase III clinical trial, where a 300 mg s.c. once-weekly dose of Inotersen was administered, the primary endpoint—a measure of neuropathy improvement—and secondary endpoints, including a 10-meter walk test, were met. Common adverse events included injection site reactions, nausea, headache, fever, and vomiting. However, thrombocytopenia, which represents a more severe side effect, was observed. Therefore, close monitoring of blood platelet counts during Inotersen treatment is essential. Interim data indicate that long-term treatment with Inotersen for up to three years preserves HRQOL. A longer-lasting compound based on the same therapeutic principle, AKCEA-TTR-LRx (eplontersen), is currently undergoing phase III trials. While mRNA-specific therapies effectively prevent newly formed amyloids by suppressing the production of plasma TTR, they do not remove amyloid from tissues and organs. These findings underscore the importance of early treatment for patients with familial amyloidosis.

draft: A 2-year-old girl presented with neck and cheek swelling approximately 4 months before any imaging studies. Despite antibiotic therapy, the symptoms persisted. Further examination was conducted, including radiography, bone scintigraphy, MRI, and ultrasound. Initially, radiography did not detect hyperostosis. However, bone scintigraphy revealed increased uptake in the mandible (B), while no abnormal uptakes were found at other locations. T2-weighted fat-suppression images showed high signal intensity in the bone marrow of the mandible and a mild periosteal reaction (C and D). An axial sonogram of the mandibular body showed a slightly hypoechoic area adjacent to the cortex (E and F). Given these findings, the mandible was selected as the biopsy site since it was the only location showing abnormalities in these examinations. A biopsy of the mandible was performed, and the pathology revealed a slight accumulation of leukocytes and plasma cells, along with predominant fibrous stroma (G and H). Cultures for bacteria and malignant cells were negative. Based on these results, chronic myelomonocytic leukemia (CRMO) in its chronic phase, without an acute phase reaction, was diagnosed.

draft: The most recent nationally representative seroprevalence study of HCV in Mexican adults, conducted in 2012, found that approximately 0.30% of adults aged 20 to 49 years were seropositive for HCV. Since then, no other such representative estimates have been published. However, in high-risk subpopulations, the pooled prevalence of HCV has been estimated at 84.2%. HCV infections can result in liver cirrhosis, cancer, and hepatocellular carcinoma. Liver cirrhosis is the fourth leading cause of death and one of the principal causes of disability in Mexico. Prior to 1993, blood transfusions were the most common risk factor for HCV in the country. Since then, the Mexican government has implemented official standards for blood donation and established a specific action plan for the prevention, diagnosis, and treatment of hepatitis C from 2016 to 2018, with the goal of reducing morbidity and mortality. Current modes of HCV transmission include intravenous drug use, multiple sexual partners, unsafe tattooing, and perinatal transmission. In 2018, direct-acting antivirals were introduced by public providers as part of their basic drug formulary to combat HCV. The National Program for Hepatitis C Elimination offers free access to screening and diagnostic tests, as well as treatment, focusing on primary care.

draft: The results of our study indicate significant alterations in the protein expression in the rat striatum and cerebellum following six months of morphine withdrawal compared to a three-month abstinence period. Specifically, the number of altered proteins increased from seven to ten in the striatum and from four to eleven in the cerebellum. The majority of these changes were related to metabolic alterations, including L-lactate dehydrogenase B chain (Ldhb), malate dehydrogenase (Ldh1), creatine kinase B-type (Ckb), fructose-bisphosphate aldolase C (Aldoc), and triose phosphate isomerase 1 (Tpi1). Our findings suggest that prolonged morphine withdrawal leads to substantial changes in the energy metabolism of different brain regions. The results indicate potential alterations in glucose metabolism, the tricarboxylic acid cycle (TCA), and fatty acid metabolism. We also suspect changes in metabolites involved in antioxidant and nucleotide pathways. However, further detailed studies are needed to fully understand these changes. In summary, our research highlights significant proteomic changes in the striatum and cerebellum after six months of morphine withdrawal, particularly in metabolic pathways. Further investigations are required to explore these metabolic changes in more depth.

For some allergic individuals, exposure to specific food allergens can even cause life-threatening reactions (anaphylactic shock). Currently, the only effective way to prevent such reactions is avoidance, making proper labeling quite essential. Many legislations on food allergen labeling have been put into place in different countries or organizations. However, besides knowingly and deliberately introduced allergenic ingredients, some “hidden allergens” contaminated unintentionally during the products transportation, storage, and/or processing, can also pose a threat to the health of allergic individuals, which has further challenged the tracing of allergens more accurately, rapidly, and conveniently.

draft: The polyphenol compounds of interest were subjected to chromatographic separation using an ultra-high performance liquid chromatography (UHPLC) system equipped with an autosampler device, a degassing system, and a quaternary UHPLC pump. Polyphenol separation was accomplished with the use of a Kinetex column F5 (50 mm × 2.1 mm, 1.7 µm particle size, Phenomenex, Torrance, CA, USA). The mobile phase was composed of a mixture of water (A) and methanol (B), prepared at a concentration of 0.1% by volume of formic acid (FA). This solution was pumped at a flow rate of 0.5 mL per minute. The injection volume was set to 5 µL. A gradient elution program was employed to separate the polyphenols, commencing with a 100% concentration of mobile phase A for the first minute, after which the concentration of A was gradually decreased to 20% over the next two minutes. This gradient was then further reduced to 0% A over the next three minutes. Following this, the gradient returned to 100% A for the final two minutes. Column re-equilibration was conducted for an additional two minutes to ensure the column remained in a stable and optimal state.

draft: To date, the clinical outcomes of BET inhibitors have been somewhat constrained. One of the primary obstacles to their anti-tumor efficacy is the tendency for these inhibitors to induce the upregulation of BET proteins themselves. This limitation is effectively circumvented through the use of BET degraders, which employ the PROTAC concept. These degraders consist of a BET inhibitor moiety fused with an additional small molecule that targets an E3 ubiquitin ligase complex, leading to the ubiquitination and subsequent proteasomal degradation of the BET proteins. Various BET degraders have been developed with distinct binding motives for BET proteins and various E3 recruiters. MZ1 represents a potent BET degrader, consisting of JQ1, an inhibitor of the BET binding domain (BD), fused with a ligand for the E3 ubiquitin ligase von Hippel-Lindau (VHL), which triggers the degradation of the BET proteins. Here, we present data on the anti-tumor efficacy of MZ1 in both in vitro and in vivo models of ABC DLBCL.

BET degraders with different BET-binding motives and E3 recruiters have been generated. MZ1 is a potent BET degrader composed of the BET inhibitor JQ1 for its BET BD binding and a ligand for the E3 ubiquitin ligase von Hippel-Lindau (VHL) for proteasomal degradation. Here, we present data on the anti-tumor activity of MZ1 in ABC DLBCL in vitro and in vivo models.

draft: In the domain of Big Data, processing SARS-CoV-2 RNA sequences necessitates the use of high-performance computing (HPC). To accurately measure the similarities between these sequences, we employ optimal and efficient algorithms and methods. In this context, we have developed a distributed approach utilizing the Hadoop framework. We began by applying the longest common subsequence (LCS) algorithm to compare the SARS-CoV-2 RNA sequences and subsequently constructed relevant clusters by measuring their similarities. The computation of the LCS involves identifying the longest common subsequence between two sequences. The LCS algorithm utilizes dynamic programming (DP) to simplify the problem by breaking it down into simpler sub-problems recursively. In bioinformatics, dynamic programming is frequently utilized for tasks such as sequence alignment, protein folding, RNA structure prediction, and protein-DNA binding.

In this context, we developed a distributed approach, based on the Hadoop framework and started comparing SARS-CoV-2 RNA sequences by using the longest common subsequence (LCS) algorithm to finally measure similarities between sequences and build relevant clusters. Computing the LCS consists of finding the longest subsequence common to two sequences. LCS algorithm leverages dynamic programming (DP) to simplify the problem by breaking it down into simpler sub-problems in a recursive manner. In bioinformatics, DP is commonly used for tasks like sequence alignment, protein folding, RNA structure prediction, and protein-DNA binding.

draft: Type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) and oxidative stress (OS) are fundamental mechanisms that lead to endothelial dysfunction, thereby increasing the risk of cardiovascular disease (CVD). Elevated levels of plasminogen activator inhibitor-1 (PAI-1), a marker of general endothelial dysfunction, have been documented in diabetic retinopathy, diabetic nephropathy, and coronary heart disease. Given the presence of vitamin D receptors (VDR) in various tissues including endothelial cells, vascular smooth muscle cells, pancreatic beta cells, T helper cells, macrophages, and adipose tissues, vitamin D is now subject to detailed investigation. The active form of vitamin D is synthesized by the specific endothelial α-hydroxylase on circulating 25(OH)D. A significant correlation has been observed between vitamin D and cardiovascular events such as angina pectoris, myocardial infarction, and stroke. A 10-year follow-up survey among an elderly population-base cohort indicated that low levels of 1,25(OH)2D were predictive of acute myocardial infarction and stroke. Cross-sectional studies have also shown a relationship between vitamin D25(OH)2D levels and markers of inflammation. In a large-scale report involving more than 15,000 subjects, it was observed that 25(OH)D levels under 53 nanomoles per liter were inversely associated with inflammatory biomarker C-reactive protein (CRP). Vitamin D has been demonstrated to regulate the expression of pro-inflammatory cytokines and adhesion molecules in the vasculature.

Elevation in plasminogen activator inhibitor-1 (PAI-1) levels has been considered as a marker of general endothelial dysfunction with elevated levels reported in diabetic retinopathy, diabetic nephropathy, and coronary heart disease in type 2 diabetes. Vitamin D is now under precise investigation due to the expression of vitamin D receptors (VDR) in body tissues such as endothelial cells, vascular smooth muscle cells, β cells of the pancreas, T helper cells, macrophages, muscles, and adipose tissues. The active form of vitamin D is also produced in endothelial cells through the activity of a specific endothelial α-hydroxylase on circulating 25(OH) D. A strong and independent association between vitamin D and cardiovascular events such as angina, myocardial infarction, and stroke has been observed. Low serum levels of 1, 25(OH) 2 D predicted acute myocardial infarction and stroke after a 10-year follow-up in an elderly population-based survey. Some cross-sectional studies have shown a relationship between 25(OH) 2 D and markers of inflammation. In the largest report, on more than 15,000 subjects, it was found that 25(OH) 2 D levels less than 53 nmol/L levels were inversely associated with inflammatory biomarker C-reactive protein (CRP). Vitamin D was found to regulate the expression of pro-inflammatory cytokines and adhesion molecules in the vasculature.

human: With hundreds of dysferlinopathy cases now reported, the most common MRI patterns of muscle involvement have been unambiguously identified. draft: To ensure high filling repeatability and short processing times, it is essential to properly seal the bottom sides of the through-holes. This was accomplished by pressing a circular PTFE nub (height: 0.1 mm, diameter base area: 0.6 mm) against the bottom rim of the through-holes. PTFE was selected to prevent adhesion between the substrate and the nub. PTFE exhibits excellent chemical and temperature resistance, and its low hardness allows it to accommodate any irregularities in the rim geometry. The nub structure was created by sandwiching a 0.1 mm thick PTFE foil between the substrate and a supporting plate, which has the same geometry as the substrate but is filled with high-temperature epoxy adhesive. The amount of epoxy was precisely controlled using a dispensing system to create a specific topography on the supporting plate. This topography was then used to impress the corresponding nubs into the PTFE foil. The entire stack, including the substrate, supporting plate, and PTFE foil, was secured in place by a uniform clamp made from a 0.5 mm thick stainless-steel plate, which was clamped to the carrier with 16 M2.5 screws. To apply the clamping force uniformly along the edge of each circular sample plate, spring elements (lock washers) were attached to the clamping plate. The supporting plate is reusable, while the PTFE foil is replaced each time a new substrate is installed on the carrier.

draft: There is a significant demand for incorporating innovative technical advancements into daily life to ensure a safe and comfortable lifestyle. A variety of smart technologies, including intelligent electric cars, portable gadgets, power tools, medical equipment, and communication devices, are increasingly integrated into our everyday experiences. To function effectively, these systems require reliable energy storage, and lithium-ion batteries (LIBs) are commonly employed for this purpose. LIBs offer several advantages over conventional batteries, such as high energy density, high specific capacity, extended operational life, the absence of memory effect, a long shelf life, and a low self-discharge rate. LIBs are widely used as primary energy storage due to their exceptional performance. Typically, LIBs consist of key components such as a cathode, anode, electrolyte, and separator membrane. Notably, graphite is a common anode material for commercial LIBs, but it has limited capacity (372 mAh/g) and operates at a relatively low voltage (0.05 V vs Li/Li+). This can lead to the formation of lithium dendrites, potentially causing short circuits and posing a risk of explosion. Consequently, the industry is actively seeking alternative materials to replace graphite.

draft: The primer pair DpinodellaTef, selected for the insertion of an LNA probe, was shown to have high specificity for targeting the TEF-1 alpha gene in *D. pinodella*. It was evaluated on a panel consisting of 3 isolates and 3 species, demonstrating no cross-reactivity with *D. pinodes* and *D. lethalis*. When the assay was tested under conditions with annealing/elongation temperatures above 60 °C, it maintained specific binding. Upon testing the primers against genomic DNA from 35 non-target organisms (a panel of 54 isolates and 35 species), cross-reactivity was observed with five species of Didymella, namely *D. heteroderae*, *D. aurea*, *D. microchlamydospora*, *D. protuberans*, and *D. americana*. However, these non-target species were amplified with significantly higher Cycle Threshold (Cq) values, ranging from 10 to over 30 Cq units higher than the target species *D. pinodella*. Specifically, the Cq values for amplifying the non-target species *D. heteroderae* and *D. americana* were 28 and 34, respectively, whereas those for the reference strain *D. pinodella* were 18 and 19 at a DNA concentration of 100 ng/µL. Consequently, the detection sensitivity for non-target species was more than 10^3 and 10^5 times lower, respectively, compared to *D. pinodella*. No detectable amplicons were generated using the genomic DNA of the remaining non-target species of Didymella or other species within the genus *Fusarium*.
